items.body: Cedric Wattergniaux has been active under the alias Kilmarth for several years now. With “Au Bord Des Ténèbres”, he returns with his third album, self-released this time and also available as a limited-edition vinyl release. The eight tracks draw inspiration from artist Pierre Soulages’ concept of ‘Outrenoir’. Kilmarth adapts this concept to the human experience, exploring the idea that black is never the final destination. Naturally, the music is the main focus here, and in this regard, Wattergniaux seems—for the first time—to have found a truly consistent musical direction. Gone are the guest vocalists, Jazzy influences, and Latin American experiments. Instead, the entire album is built around Experimental-Electro, Glitch, and occasional Cinematic influences. Some might not consider this the most accessible music, yet Kilmarth surprises the listener with cold soundscapes that are sometimes underpinned by a melodic touch, but are primarily defined by an overwhelming array of sound manipulations and effects, creating a truly grim atmosphere. Occasional spoken-word samples add genuine value to the mix. Another significant improvement can be heard in the mixing and overall production, areas in which Kilmarth has made great strides. In short, this album was a pleasant surprise. It demonstrates real potential and paves the way for even greater things to come. Kilmarth seems ready to take the next step and is sure to appeal to fans of labels such as Ant-Zen. (Rating:8). The album was preceded by the three-track single “Avant de céder…”, covered in Kilmarth releases three-track single ‘Avant de céder…’ as prelude to upcoming album, and Wattergniaux discussed the Soulages concept behind the record in Kilmarth interview: the light inside Pierre Soulages’ black on ‘Au bord des Ténèbres…’. Listen to “Outrenoir”: Outrenoir by Kilmarth About Kilmarth Kilmarth is the solo project of Belgian musician Cedric Wattergniaux, working in IDM, glitch and post-industrial ambient. Side-Line first covered the project in 2018 with the ‘Click Interview’ with Kilmarth: ‘Music Is A Legal Drug That Has The Immense Power To Make Us Escape’, published on 19 August 2018, and reviewed the CD mini-album “Catharsis” the same year. The EP Kilmarth – Derrière Le Miroir (EP – Kilmarth) followed in 2021, together with a video for “M-Fia41”. The two-track single “Baryum” arrived in January 2022 and the mini-album Kilmarth – Better Days (EP – Kilmarth) in 2023, the first Kilmarth release with a guest singer. The debut full-length Kilmarth – Sociological Veranda (Album – Kilmarth) was released in January 2024, preceded by the glitch single “Vergessen”, and the IDM EP “My Son of The Moon” followed in November 2024. In January 2025 Wattergniaux teamed up with D-Fried for the album “Micrometeoritic Flowerpot”. The concept album Kilmarth – Cherophobia (Digital Album – Adventurous Music), built around the fear of happiness, was issued in January 2026 through the Adventurous Music digital series. “Au Bord Des Ténèbres…” was released on 6 June 2026 on Bandcamp and holds eight tracks, opening with “Le seuil” and closing with “Outrenoir”. It is the first Kilmarth album pressed on vinyl.

items.body:
Strong debut album by one of China’s most distinctive new industrial/dance music producers, Tzusing, for L.I.E.S.; portraying the Shanghai-based artist’s full breadth of kinky darkroom rhythms and sleazy cinematic arrangements. 

Under the title 東方不敗, meaning Invincible East, the record wraps an armoury of powerful percussion and native instrumentation around a narrative locus based on a swordsman character in a Jin Yong novel “who must make the ultimate sacrifice to attain knowledge and transform”. Coupled with the artist’s own observations on living in, and travelling around, Asia, it’s an urgent and gripping listen with a versatility and varied topography lending itself to DJ use and soundtracking industrial subterfuge alike.

日出東方 唯我不敗 starts out like ’05 sino grime or dubstep from a parallel dimension; Digital Properties trades in secretive choral code at a killer New Beta momentum which decelerates into the the wind-tunnel chug and pealing cyber-tribal chant of Esther. 

His signature triplets last heard on A Name Out Of Place wickedly come into play against sheer electric blue synth tone in King Of Hosts; we’re put thru an intense, Americanised club drill in Post-Soviet Models; and Torque Pulsations both literally and physically lives up to its name with a belly and spine-twysting EBM tattoo. 

 TIP!
items._genre: industrial / EBM / dark electronic / experimental
items._cn_summary: Tzusing 首张全长专辑以金庸小说人物东方不败为叙事核心，将武术修行的自我牺牲与蜕变主题投射到亚洲当代生存体验之中。制作层面融合强劲打击节奏与本土器乐采样，构建出兼具暗室俱乐部张力与电影化叙事质感的声响景观。曲目编排展现高度多变性：从带有 dubstep 影子的开场曲，到带有合唱采样的俱乐部律动、再到具有部落仪式感的工业段落，节奏与情绪在多维度地形间自如切换。三连音动机与电子蓝调合成器音色交织出鲜明的个人标识，EBM 段落以物理性的冲击力贯穿听感。专辑在 DJ 实用性与叙事深度之间取得了难得平衡，既适合俱乐部场景播放，也具备作为工业潜行配乐的完整张力。

items.body:
Oh man this is just incredible; Oren Ambarchi cracks open the work of lesser-known guitar god (and notorious instrument builder) Hans Reichel, selecting solo recordings spanning 1973-1988 that highlight his innovative approach to the instrument. It honestly sounds like nothing else, but followers of work by Oren Ambarchi, Fred Frith, Henry Kaiser, Derek Bailey or Keith Rowe - this will do you in.
Best known these days as the location of Open Ground, the German club opened by Mark Ernestus with one of the world's best soundsystems, North Rhine-Westphalia's Wuppertal is also the hometown of Hans Reichel, an improv titan and "experimental luthier" who genuinely changed the way improvisers approached the guitar. Don't take our word for it, guitarist (and Black Truffle boss) Oren Ambarchi credits Reichel with shaping his philosophy, and now celebrates the pioneer with a groegously compiled anthology of 23 tracks from his vast (and fairly impenetrable) catalog. Many might be familiar with Reichel mostly for his inventions, particularly the daxophone, an experimental idiophone he created to mimic animal sounds that's become a Hollywood staple in recent years, but the fact that his own work hasn't been raked over makes 'Dalbergia Refusa' a vital missing link, shining a spotlight on his work as both a player, composer and luthier - and it is quite honestly one of the most crucial reissues we’ve heard in years.
Ambarchi first came in contact with Reichel's work when he heard 1987's 'Return of the Knödler show' on a Guitar Player magazine cover disc -  and it soon changed the way Ambarchi thought about the instrument, you can very clearly hear its impact on his early recordings - especially his milestone 'Grapes From The Estate'. So it's a fitting way for Ambarchi to open the compilation - particularly because keen-eared listeners might recognise it for another reason, it's the track that Daniel Lopatin samples (and croons over) on 'No Good', 'Garden of Delete's light-headed highlight. With that one out of the way, the rest of the tracks really display Reichel's range: his technical skills using extra strings, moveable pickups or extra bridges, and his compositional boldness, freely shifting from solo guitar to multiple instruments or from pick to hammer.
'Wenn Das Rohr Dommelt', the opening track from Reichel's first album, 1973's 'Wichlinghauser Blues', foregrounded one of the artist's oddest instruments - an 11-string zither-style device that used piano strings and was hammered, with a shot glass used as a slide. It's shockingly unique sound that established a benchmark for Reichel as he went on to pull from US and UK rock and folk he grew up with, like on 'The call (I)' from 1979's ace 'The Death of the Rate Bird Ymir' - you can hear those ideas chewed up through his unique methodology. The American primitive concepts that Fahey distributed to a network of his acolytes sound different here, trampled by Reichel and his "full fret guitar" but not lost entirely. Similarly, there's an echo of psychedelic rock on the closing track 'Heimkehr der Holzböcke', taken from a rare 7" released in 1975, that Reichel corrodes with his advanced techniques, overdubbing bird-like squeaks and dissonant, blues-y plods.
Another utterly indispensable history lesson from Black Truffle, then.
items._genre: experimental guitar / free improvisation / avant-garde / luthiery
items._cn_summary: Oren Ambarchi策划了一张Hans Reichel的独奏吉他精选辑，收录1973至1988年间23首作品。Reichel不仅是即兴吉他演奏家，更是一位实验乐器制造者，发明了daxophone（一种模仿动物声音的实验体鸣乐器）以及使用钢琴弦的十一弦齐特琴装置、配有shot glass滑奏器的全品丝吉他等独创乐器。合辑展示了Reichel如何通过添加额外琴弦、可移动拾音器、附加琴桥等技术手段，彻底拓展了吉他的表现边界。曲目横跨他从美国原始音乐、摇滚民谣中汲取养分后形成的独特方法论，以及他作为作曲家和乐器制造家的多维成就。文章将其定位为补全即兴吉他史缺失环节的重要再版，并指出其对Ambarchi本人哲学形成的深远影响。

items.body:
Plunging headfirst into fuzzy psychedelic melancholia, Klara Lewis leans into her role as this generation's Mego figurehead, mulching acoustic samples and offhand recordings until the concept of analog and digital vanishes in the aether. Properly good - required listening if you're into PITA, early Fennesz or Jefre Cantu-Ledesma.

We should have known when we heard her killer 20-minute redraft of PITA's 'Get Out' standout 'Track 3' that Lewis had entered a new phase in her artistic evolution. That track, part of a pared-down album of dedications to the sorely missed Mego boss, felt like a turning point, a way for Lewis to pay her respect to the "extreme laptop music" family tree. And 'Opening' builds on those foundations; it's a free-er record than 2020's brief but powerful 'Ingrid', similarly cinematic - two of the cues were originally composed for Mika Taanila's experimental film 'Failed Emptiness' - but refreshingly free of the self seriousness that bogs down so much contemporary experimental music. That mischievous element is exactly what made 'Thankful' so gratifying; Lewis followed Rehberg's example and harnessed the power of juxtaposition, messiness and absurdity, the aspects that made the Mego catalog so enduringly distinctive. 

And she's never sounded as liberated as she does on 'Opening'.. From the intro track 'Ta Min Hand' there's a self-assured swagger that's wholly captivating. Perhaps it's the way Lewis uses distortion, uglifying a soaring loop in a such a way that the showboating romance becomes genuinely heartbreaking. Just tune into how she isolates schmaltzy horns and makes them part of her vocabulary, pitch-shifting them to assure us she's in control. As soon as the track fizzles out, it's replaced by a very different expression of noise, a grottily captured urban excursion that's disrupted by a passing jazzy guitar - she lets the environmental recording play out to force us to pay attention; when we hear voices, they don't quite sound human, eventually raptured by deafening distortions. The impact on the listener is startling -  like an ice cream van with a busted speaker careening into a quiet Northern European plaza.

These various short-form experiments - like the heady, orchestral 'Vaknar' and 'Hardcore', a simple, memorable piano riff that Lewis sculpts into a fragile symphony - lead towards the album's lengthy centerpiece 'Tide', a track she originally composed for 'Dissolving Strawberry', a compilation released last year on Stockholm's Irrlicht label. Here, she takes her time, upsetting an implacable sample with cautious glitches and anxious hesitations. If anything, it's a breather between the album's two sides, cushioning the blow as Lewis pushes into even quirkier territory on the second half. 'How Far', sounds like an early AFX demo, all broken synths and strangulated voices, while 'Small Harp' is a tonal study using what sounds like a zither. On 'Drip', Lewis plays ukulele, accompanying brittle strums with ruptured subs that increase in intensity with each terrifying hit, before leading us out with the title track, a noisy mellotron-like drone vignette that plays like a thank you for staying locked in.
items._genre: experimental electronic / avant-garde / abstract / glitch / field recording
items._cn_summary: Klara Lewis 的专辑《Opening》延续了 Mego 厂牌的极端笔记本音乐传统，将原声采样与即兴录音拆解重组，使模拟与数字的界限彻底消解。专辑融合了她为 Mika Taanila 实验影片《Failed Emptiness》创作的配乐，呈现出电影化的空间感。Lewis 擅长通过失真、变调、错位等手法制造并置效果，将甜美铜管扭曲成悲伤回声，让环境录音被噪声撕裂，甚至用尤克里里搭配爆裂音墙。她借鉴了 PITA 与 Rehberg 的方法论——混乱、荒诞与并置的力量——这正是 Mego 目录历久弥新的特质。专辑曲目多为短篇实验，中段长曲《Tide》作为喘息缓冲，将不安的采样层层剥离。整体展现出自由而自信的创作姿态，摆脱了当代实验音乐常有的严肃包袱。

items.body:
2023 Reissue of the very first Buddha Machine, newly upgraded with better sound quality and user experience including a louder speaker and 2 new individual side buttons to make the device control more direct and intuitive. Available in 5 colours.
You either know what these are and have already hit the buy button, or you’re too young to remember the Brian Eno-fuelled craze for these ambient boxes and are about to enter a portal to a different time. We must have sold several - many - thousands of these in their various iterations, including editions made in collab with Philip Glass and Throbbing Gristle, and after about a decade in the wilderness, they’re now back, in a new replica version of the very first edition from 2005 - that’s before the Iphone era - with improved controls and sound quality. oh, and that all important line out, for your buddha boxing!
In 2005 the Beijing-based duo of Christiaan Virant and Zhang Jian released their first, soon to be iconic  “Buddha Machine” loop box, a quirky pocket soundsystem that propelled sound art into the consumer mainstream. It spawned a whole cultural movement, fuelled by Brian Eno professing his love for them, and an era of live show "Buddha Boxing" improvisations.
The original version has been long sold-out and fetches crazy prices second hand, followed by various further iterations made in collaboration with Philip Glass and Throbbing Gristle. This new edition is a replica of the very fiest version, featuring the original loops in all their 8-bit Lo-Fi glory and available in 5 different colours.
"The classic loops of the original FM3 Buddha Machine evoke instant nostalgia for a slower, more simple world. Born before the iPhone era, this iconic device has weathered two decades of pop culture and fashion trends, yet remains defiantly, heroically unique. Its enduring simplicity cloaks an extraordinary power: the ability to transcend time. It is both a sonic portal to a hands-on analogue past and a bridge to a digital ever-present. This is not just a re-issue; it is a revival and refinement of a sonic manifesto that unfolds softly, gently and organically, resonating with the subtle rhythms of life. The Buddha 1 2023 edition from FM3. Available in 5 colours: Red, Orange, Green, Blue and limited-edition Pink. Features upgraded sound quality and user experience. Louder speaker and 2 new individual side buttons make device control more direct and intuitive."
The Buddha Machine is a truly unique musical device that prefers to sit in the background, quietly and gently working its sonic magic.
*Batteries not included!!!*

items._cn_summary: 本文介绍北京双人组2005年推出的《佛祖机》首版于2023年再版。原版是一台口袋型环境音乐循环播放器，曾得到布莱恩·伊诺的公开喜爱，并带动了现场即兴演奏的风潮。再版复刻第一代外形，保留原始八位低保真循环素材，同时加大扬声器音量、新增两个独立侧键，使控制更直接，还保留线路输出。文章将这个小装置视为连接前智能手机时代模拟触感与数字当下的声音通道，强调它不只是再版，而是对一件另类声音作品的延续。它以极简硬件方式让环境音乐成为可随身携带的日常物件，在背景里持续释放声响，也因而成为声音艺术与消费文化之间的特殊交汇点。

items.body:
Remastered for its 1st vinyl cut, The Bug aka Kevin Richard Martin’s immensely forlorn ’22 solo jag immures the senses in a slow-burn blizzard of white-out atonalities and infrasonic rumbles shot thru with an unnerving isolationist melancholia. One hard RIYL Thomas Köner, Mika Vainio’s elemental Ø works, or GAS, gone noxious.

Positively the bleakest thing he’s ever made, ’Sub Zero’ is a supremely powerful listening experience. Thry a dozen tracks Martin pushes the hallmarks of his work, under various guises and collaborations, to a logical conclusion of aesthetic and emotive obliteration. Effectively the heaviest ends of his work as part of EAR (with Porter Ricks’ Mellwig/Köner, Kevin Shields, Pete Kember), the dankest frequencies of The Bug, the detachment of ’Sirens’ (Room 40) and utterly heartbroken qualities of King Midas Sound, are collapsed into the sound of a luscious black hole succour, with a grasp of life-affirming heaviness that dangles it just above the end of the rope. 

Perhaps KRM’s finest, purest hour of aural haunting, the dozen tracks unfurl in glacial streaks on the imagination with a sense of scale and presence that pins heads in place, vulnerable to the elements. He continues to limn the void like he’s lived inside it and survived to tell the tale. A longhand conviction in dub-as-method guides him to the limits of that sound, where it crosses the threshold into realms shared by dark ambient, at the peripheries of BM, post-techno electronics and doom metal. In this atmospheric no-man’s-land he leaves an indelibly ambiguous impression, palpably stricken by existential dread but with pangs of beauty, as in the upswell of Eno-esque choral pads on ‘Too Human’ and ‘Higher Than the Sky’ that cling to hope like a limpet on the hull of his icebreaking structures. 

Magisterial stuff by an artist arguably in his imperial phase.
items._genre: dark ambient / drone / dub / minimal electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是制作人The Bug（Kevin Richard Martin）2022年个人作品的首次黑胶再版，以极度缓慢的冰封感声场著称。十二首作品将次声波低频、白色噪音与原子化音调推向极端，营造出听觉上的孤立与荒凉。整体声音逻辑延续了他在EAR、King Midas Sound等项目中对频率底部的执着追求，同时将dub技法推至其极限，与黑暗氛围、后工业电子、末日金属的边缘地带交汇。部分曲目如'Too Human'与'Higher Than the Sky'引入了类似Eno的合唱pad音色，在阴郁中残存一丝希望的气息。乐评认为这是他艺术生涯中最纯粹、最具重量的时刻，声音如同黑色引力场，将听者牢牢锁在原地。

items.body:
Effortlessly easy on the ear and yet still somehow fathoms-deep, Tara Clerkin Trio’s latest is their most refined and fully-formed transmission yet, mining a precious sweetspot between chamber-jazz, Plone-style bric-a-brac electronics, Crescent’s lo-fi reveries and the urban pressure of the Young Echo collective, unpicking decades of British musical history in the process. Trust, it’s a special one.

Like every great band, TCT know their history. They've grown up with and formed their identity in the shadow of Bristol's musical lore, whether it's The Pop Group, Massive Attack or Flying Saucer Attack, and when they use traceable elements, it feels like a believable part of their DNA. Thankfully, they meaningfully add to that narrative too, not adapting an aesthetic for easy consumption. Part of this might be down to their makeup; they formed in the late 20-teens from the ashes of the Tara Clerkin Band, a larger ensemble that Clerkin had put together to expand the scope of her folk-y pop compositions. And when most of the members moved on, stepbrothers Sunny-Joe Paradiso and Patrick Benjamin stuck around to see where the road might lead. All "proper" players, they've traditionally let their songs appear from what sounds like loose, casual improvisations, like you're tuned into Don Cherry's 'Organic Music Society' band running through Laika's 'Silver Apples of the Moon'.

So you get a song like the brilliant 'Ups & Downs', that simmers for a good four minutes with wheezing harmonium, double bass and clarinet, percussion just rumbling in the background somewhere, before a jerky sampled beat, Mellotron strings and Clerkin's voice would have you thinking Matt Elliott's behind the boards. But 'Somewhere Good' is also remarkably tight when it needs to be, walking a tightrope between easy breezy and meticulous with acrobatic skill. Opener 'Lake Walk', for example, sounds intentionally naive, jammed out loosely on synthesised and real woodwind that's caught in a vortex of Space Echo, before 'Lazy Daisy' cuts it short with its more ordered (but still kinda slouchy) beat-heavy dreampop atmosphere. It's where the album's shape really coagulates, between Broadcast's dramatic early EPs (back when they were touring with Plone) and Pram's best shit, just lightly tweezed at the edges, its creases relaxed to fit in with Laila Sakini's quietly genius 'Paloma'. And that mood carries the record even when Clerkin's voice - pursed into a soulful croon or a lackadaisical murmur - vanishes completely. One of the most gripping moments arrives with 'There Was a Nice Sunset', effortlessly matching slowcore drums with piano flourishes and synths, locking into the same general feeling but widening the boundaries, nodding to Adrian Sherwood's lysergic work on Creation Rebel's 'Starship Africa'. 

There's years of British musical history baked into this stuff, and yet it feels wholly new.
items._genre: chamber jazz / experimental / electronic / lo-fi / avant-garde
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑融合室内爵士、拼贴电子、低保真梦幻流行与即兴演奏，从布里斯托音乐历史中汲取养分，将松散随性的即兴感与细致编排平衡在微妙张力中。开篇曲以合成器与木管在回声效果中形成迷幻漩涡，随后用节拍驱动的梦幻流行段落收束，整体气质介于Broadcast早期戏剧化EP、Pram的代表作与Laila Sakini的安静天才之间。人声时而是灵魂式低吟，时而是慵懒呓语，当人声完全消失时，器乐部分依然牢牢抓住听众，如慢核鼓与钢琴、合成器铺陈出开阔边界，并隐约指向Adrian Sherwood的迷幻制作传统。专辑将数十年英国音乐历史内化为自身语言，既有可辨识的脉络，又呈现出全然新鲜的面貌。

items.body:
Of all Jan Jelinek’s formidable output, this album has always been the one for us. More resolved and driven than 'Loop-Finding Jazz Records' (which appeared two years later), less reliant on glitch than Farben, it was essentially Jelinek's most satisfying and complete prototype for a new kind of sample-based music deeply immersed in the spirit of Jazz, without making any direct reference to it. 

Originally released via Move D’s Source imprint back in 1999, 'Personal Rock' is situated somewhere between 'Loop-Finding Jazz Records', his Farben output, and Move D's Conjoint work, full of subtle production flourishes sliding around deep House structures that belong to pre-millenial IDM, but which transcend its overly-fussy, masculine templates.

The music is brooding and full of romance, designed for late night immersion and bolstered by what we reckon is the most forward thinking and timeless production of Jelinek’s output over the last two decades. Impossible to pull highlights, it’s an album best experienced from end-to-end through multiple listens, drawing you into its quietly euphoric, blue mood.
items._genre: electronic / IDM / deep house / experimental / jazz
items._cn_summary: 这是 Jan Jelinek 于 1999 年经由 Move D 的 Source 厂牌发行的专辑，介于其后来《Loop-Finding Jazz Records》与 Farben、Conjoint 项目之间。作品以采样为基础，在深度浩室结构中嵌入细腻的制作细节，延续了千禧年前 IDM 的语言，同时突破其过度繁琐与男性化的既有框架。音乐整体带有沉郁与浪漫气质，适合深夜沉浸式聆听，制作上展现出前瞻性与持久魅力。专辑不依赖单一曲目出彩，而强调整张从头至尾反复聆听，在连续的流动中逐渐将听者引入一种静谧而欣悦的蓝色情绪。它没有直接引用爵士素材，却深刻浸染于爵士精神，形成一种新的采样音乐原型。独立厂牌发行，兼顾实验性与可听性，与用户偏好的实验电子、IDM及爵士融合方向高度契合。

items.body:
Among our most loved ‘90s ambient house records, Terre Thaemlitz’s debut album is mercifully - finally - expanded and reissued for its 30th anniversary, including an incredible prototype for ambient Memphis rap instrumentals and some would even say dubstep - now expanded to well over two hours long, with a delectable bonus disc full of deep cuts.

One that puts a lump in our throat from the opening strokes, ‘Tranquillizer’ marks a key point of departure for Thaemlitz from the deep house they DJ’d at NYC clubs from the late ‘80s to fully embrace its spiritual descendants - ambient house and downbeat - and embark on a stellar oeuvre defined by a timeless sound sensitivity and pathos. 

The original version of Thaemlitz’s maiden album voyage would include ‘Raw Through a Straw’ - a sublime 11 minute transition from new age synth blooz to rollin breaks - alongside seven other cuts that beautifully took the potential of a broader canvas to paint widescreen visions of post-club music at the ’90’s midriff. This reissue now expands the 69 minute OG to over twice the length with never-before-heard, raw, alternate versions and inclusions of related, contemporaneous material from the same era.

Effectively picking up the baton from the likes of the KLF or The Orb and L.B. Bad’s new age house, and with uncanny parallels here and there to Move D and Jonah Sharp’s Reagenz project of the same era, on ‘Tranquilizer’ Thaemlitz would delineate and diffuse deep house’s romantic energies and spirit along electro-acoustic and sanguine vectors with a dreamlike seduction and melancholic traction that resonates with listeners’ needs into the present day. His perfectly slanted opener ’040468’ is titled for the date of MLK’s death (and coincidentally the year of Terre’s birth) and is a massive percy for us, spending over 8 minutes layering radio interceptions and shine-eyed synths into a lather, underlined by an LFO-flared sub-bassline with a gait that surely parallels the humid lean of early Memphis rap instrumentals (just down the road from her formative Missouri) or G-funk, and most uncannily pre-echoes the halfstep and meditative minimalism of early dubstep by a decade. A longtime travelling partner for us, it definitely warrants the cost of admission alone - it’s that good.

The rest of the OG follows to limn the sort of curious magick Thaemlitz would expand on in later years, with the ambient blues of ‘Fat Chair’ like a solemn echo of The Orb, and ‘Meditation of the Mountain Oyster’ rolling out tabla breaks into acidic horizons, and the closing section of melt-on-mind downbeats in ‘Hovering Glows’ thru the concrète-ambient frissons of ‘2 A.M. On a Silo’ to ‘Fina/Departure’ frankly leaving us in a puddle of tears and feels. The bonus disc is also totally prime, threading reverb-contrails thru ‘Get in and Drive’, an unmissable reminder of her deep house roots, two previously unreleased edits of ‘Fina’, and a stunning version of the spine-kissing ‘Hovering Glows’, plus its subtly re-tuned ‘Little Guy Mix’.

For us, ‘Tranquillizer’ is an epitome of ambient music as deeply affective, dematerialised soul music, we can only hope others will get as much from this reissued prompt as we have over the years - an indelibly imprinted carousel of memories, fond and forlorn. 

please remember that we support Terre and Comatonse Recordings' efforts to keep projects offline, minor, and acting queerly. When purchasing this item, we ask you to refrain from uploading and indiscriminate sharing in any form. <3
items._genre: ambient house / deep house / electronic / experimental / downtempo
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是 Terre Thaemlitz 1994 年首张专辑的 30 周年扩展再版，标志其从纽约俱乐部 deep house 转向 ambient house 与 downbeat 的创作路径。原版 69 分钟内容扩充至两小时以上，收录未发行曲目与同期素材。开场曲《040468》以无线电截听、合成器与 LFO 低音线营造潮湿氛围，被认为提前预见了孟菲斯说唱器乐与早期 dubstep 的形态。其余曲目融合了 new age 合成器、碎拍、tabla 与酸性音色，结尾部分在氛围声响与具象音乐之间流动，情绪沉静而富有感染力。附加碟则收入其 deep house 根源作品及未公开混音版本，呈现同一时期更广的创作光谱。整体是 90 年代氛围浩室的重要文献，兼具历史价值与聆听深度。

items.body:
Oren Ambarchi's kraut-techno-free jazz magnum opus is back for its 10th anniversary -  an ambitious ensemble piece featuring an all-star list of players including Ricardo Villalobos, Keith Fullerton Whitman, Mark Fell, crys Cole, Will Guthrie, Arto Lindsay and Konrad Sprenger... Wooooo

You've got to admire Ambarchi's chutzpah here. 'Hubris' is an all you can eat buffet of his various musical cravings, a chance for his friends, influences and collaborators to flex a little and for Ambarchi to attempt to ride the groove like an experienced cowboy on an out-of-control bucking bronco. The first side is the biggest surprise, a dedication to Wang Chung's enduring, disco-influenced 'To Live and Die in L.A.' soundtrack that begins with ping-ponging guitar notes and Jim O'Rourke's synth blips, before elusive Berlin-based composer Konrad Sprenger (aka Joerg Hiller) drops in with some motorized guitar vamps. It's rhythmic gear that fits in with the Berlin school until Mark Fell appears in the final third with some typically fractured percussion.

On the flip, the groove loosens after a short guitar interlude. Ricardo Villalobos takes over with a suitably winding, minimal throb over live rhythms played by Joe Talia and Will Guthrie simultaneously as krautrock techno mutates into disco fusion. Keith Fullerton Whitman tries to nudge the track off the rails with his modular expositions, but the path is set - Arto Lindsay's axe is just the icing on the cake. By the end of the side, we're in full jazz-noise mode: everything's still pegged to Villalobos' central pulse, but that's the only element that's bolted down. 

Hard to believe it's 10 years already - we can't think of a better skeleton key to unlock the secrets behind Black Truffle's musical identity.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是奥伦·阿姆巴尔基的十周年重制版，集结里卡多·维拉洛沃斯、基思·富勒顿·惠特曼、马克·费尔、阿尔托·林赛等乐手，以大型合奏形式将德国摇滚律动、极简科技舞曲与自由爵士和噪音融为一体。A面受王昌《生与死在洛杉矶》原声启发，吉他拨弦与合成器脉冲开场，后段出现摩托化吉他重复段和马克·费尔碎裂打击乐；B面律动松散，维拉洛沃斯以蜿蜒的极简低音脉冲贯穿，乔·塔利亚与威尔·古思里的双鼓组同时叠奏，惠特曼的模块合成器试图偏离轨道，林赛的吉他作为最终点缀，逐步进入爵士噪音状态。所有元素仍锚定在维拉洛沃斯的中心节拍上，体现黑松露厂牌的音乐身份与跨领域融合方式。

items.body:
Cooper Crain, Dan Quinlivan and Rob Frye extend the 'Inland See' universe with two sides of additional tweaks and edits, adding field recordings, autoharp and kalimba to their analog synth vamps and motorik rhythms.

If you tuned into their last album, an ecstatic, Cluster-inspired romp that sprayed whipped cream over Bitchin Bajas usual proggy selection of exotic oscillations, then 'Isle Peaks' will play like a fitting sequel. It's not a remix record, but the source material was pulled from the same electric sessions, where stems were re-examined, edited and tweaked and new elements were added to build out the "Bajas cinematic universe," in their own words. On the first side, 'Ajami' evolves its pinging kalimba sequence with brassy analog exaltations, bringing in the horn only when necessary before the track explodes into a post-Stereolab firework display of squelchy synths, two note basslines and distorted leads.

On the title track, crickets sing in the background while the trio build up their atmosphere from reverberating autoharp textures that they layer into Laraaji-like cascades of ambient bliss - only tipping into Berlin school kosmische biz in the final act.
items._genre: experimental / electronic / ambient / kosmische / motorik
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Bitchin Bajas对前作《Inland See》世界的延伸，从同一批电子录音中提取素材，重新编辑、调整并加入田野录音、autoharp与kalimba等新元素。第一首《Ajami》以kalimba的清脆律动为基底，辅以黄铜般的合成器音色，在必要时刻才引入号角，随后爆发出类似后Stereolab风格的合成器烟火，包含吱吱作响的音效、双音贝斯线与失真主旋律。标题曲中，蟋蟀声在背景鸣唱，三人组以回响的autoharp纹理层层叠加，营造出Laraaji式的氛围极乐，直到最后段落才滑入柏林学派的kosmische电气律动。整张专辑延续了Cluster启发的迷幻气质，在模拟合成器与motorik节奏之间保持了独特的平衡，既是前作的续篇，又以新的编辑思路和声音素材拓展了原有的听觉版图。

items.body:
The latest from A Colourful Storm’s Fleetway Tapes sublabel comes from Tokyo-based selector, composer and NTS resident Abiu, mining an hour of mostly Japanese prog, no wave and avant-industrial nuggets, floating into spoken word, free jazz and fringe dubs that’ll make you wonder where the hell she finds her tunes. If you've chewed up the Concentric Circles mixes on Berceuse Heroique and exhausted Blackest Ever Black’s ‘Id Mud’ mixtape series - this one’s for you.

One of those tapes you have to sink deep into rather than a casual dip, 'It's the Rest of a Stump' is packed to the gills with unclassifiable fire - avant oddities that are far too deep for any algorithm. Abiu will be a familiar name if you've scraped around the edges of the NTS schedule where her regular transmissions betray her vast knowledge; a show where you can find lesser-known art rock next to scrappy outsider techno, EBM and synthwave, Japanese folk sandwiched between spoken word and modern jazz sides. How she finds any of it, we're not sure, but it's the kind of gear that will inevitably lead to lengthy Discogs sessions - we guarantee it. 

So she's a lifer, for sure. And that's exactly the kind of feeling you get when you sit through this one. There's no need to go track to track because the individual elements aren't really why it works - it's the expedition that Abiu takes you on, harking back to a time when digging hadn't been so sanitised by bait algorithms and “released on this day xx years ago” campaigns. For an hour, we're dropped into a musty back room leafing through used bins and racks of tapes, searching through newsgroups and blogs - finding loose threads and wormholes and following them to albums that are prob 95% shit with just a few short minutes of glory buried inside. Abiu's done the work for us basically.

And if you want some added credentials, Abiu is also a researcher at Saidera Ai Design, the acoustics wing of Saidera Mastering, the team that just restored and remastered Miles Davis's catalog. 

Whewwww!
items._genre: progressive rock / no wave / avant-industrial / free jazz / dub
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑出自东京创作者 Abiu，是她为 Fleetway Tapes 制作的一小时选曲，素材以日本地下档案为主，也纳入大量来源不明的边缘录音。乐评认为它不适合零碎聆听，而是一次需要沉入的寻宝式旅程：Abiu 的选曲线索看起来来自实体唱片店的旧货箱、新闻组和博客深处的虫洞，远离算法推送和纪念日营销的整齐套路。她本人是 NTS 常驻主持，并曾参与迈尔斯·戴维斯母带重制团队的声学相关工作，为这套选曲的听觉判断力提供佐证。整张作品的重点不在于单曲，而在于跨度极大的素材被编排成连贯的探索过程，呈现一种未被数字平台过滤的挖掘传统。

items.body:
Ezra Feinberg’s third album Soft Power sees the composer-guitarist enlist an impressive array of fellow musicians including Mary Lattimore, David Moore (Bing & Ruth), Jefre Cantu-Ledesma, and Robbie Lee.

"Defined by its abundance of melodies, repeating figures and ecstatic improvisations, Soft Power exudes an enlightened and transformative spirit to empower the listener. The compassionate, tender-hearted opener ‘Future Sand’ deftly interweaves flutes and steady arpeggios. The Reichian pulse beneath the soaring melody is played not on the customary analogue sequencer, but on finger-picked acoustic guitar, one of the lodestars of Feinberg’s compositional approach. ‘Soft Power’, the buoyant and mesmeric title track that follows builds over a rich bed of guitars and a reverb-y Rhodes melody reminiscent of a Strata East LP, its narrative arc bountiful in energy, optimism and future dreaming, a perfect accompaniment to long days of summertide.

‘Pose Beams’ blends the chamber-jazz approach of Penguin Café Orchestra with a balletic kosmische, climaxing with a galvanising crescendo and “free improv” section performed by fellow New Yorkers - Robbie Lee (piano) and Jefre Cantu-Ledesma, whose granular and modular synths sprinkle particle dust over the expressive drumming of John Thayer. ‘Flutter Intensity’ evokes in part the music of Cluster as played on acoustic guitars, which ping-pong across the stereo field, providing the canvas for a plaintive vibraphone line reminiscent of TNT-era Tortoise. Instruments move in tandem, but also drift and glide allowing them the space to hang in the air, the variegated rhythms, textures, and tones all laced into the fabric of the album.

At the centrefold of the albums 7-tracks is ‘The Big Clock’, a tryptic piece that evolves from pairs of stretched varying tones, creating fields of technicolour over an unabashed motorik beat, serving to offset the pastoral and ambient registers heard elsewhere. It features the first of two appearances from David Moore (Bing & Ruth) who plays lilting piano lines on the come-down. ‘There Was Somebody There’ returns to the album’s earlier wistfulness, a hard stereo-panned soundworld with lightly strummed, interlocking acoustic guitars combining to pigment a washy, painterly scene. David Moore and Jefre Cantu-Ledesma provide reviving synths, the underlying pulse that seems to simulate a life cycle; another day on Earth. The album closes with the reflective ‘Get Some Rest’ featuring Mary Lattimore, whose harp pluckings set a dreamlike tone against bare organic acoustics and flourishing flutes to create a sense of realignment and restoration.

Feinberg artfully transcends the listener to an enriched place, his compositions distinguished by the deep humanity that lies at their core, plugging the listener into a state of wide eyed being, open and alive. Soft Power then is Ezra’s own mantra but also one of power giving - a colourful catharsis translated into music. Feinberg’s music always speaks to the listener, but Soft Power, in whispering, speaks loudest."
items._genre: experimental / chamber jazz / kosmische / ambient / avant-garde
items._cn_summary: 专辑《Soft Power》是Ezra Feinberg的第三张作品，邀请Mary Lattimore、David Moore、Jefre Cantu-Ledesma、Robbie Lee等乐手共同参与。音乐以指弹原声吉他为核心，融合了Reich式的脉冲律动、室内爵士的编制思维与kosmische氛围，长笛、竖琴、钢琴、模块合成器和鼓组在不同曲目中交织。开场曲《Future Sand》以长笛与稳定琶音铺展；《Pose Beams》从室内爵士过渡到自由即兴高潮；《Flutter Intensity》让人联想到Cluster与Tortoise的器乐对话；三部分的《The Big Clock》在motorik节拍上营造色彩丰富的音场；终曲与Mary Lattimore合作的竖琴段落则带来沉淀与修复感。整体在作曲与即兴、原声与电子之间取得平衡，器乐声部既同步又各自漂移，呈现出开阔而充满生命力的聆听体验。

items.body:
Suzanne Ciani’s ‘gay male’ alter ego Steve with a 1982 foray into peak time wavey business, including that coca cola bottle opening sound she did the sound design for plus a pitched down vocal from Ciani and a cameo from Peter Baumann of Tangerine Dream, followed by a killer slice of filtered House  ‘Steve Saves the World’ and a crazy, ‘Home Of The Brave’ style linndrum closer “Steve Happy Birthday Wishes”. Crazy find!

"Legendary composer, sound designer, and Buchla maestra Suzanne Ciani has a staggering list of accolades and accomplishments, from scoring Hollywood films to releasing influential new age records to literally designing the Coca-Cola bottle-opening sound. In the late 70s/early 80s, Ciani, while living in New York, acquired an Eventide H 949 harmonizer, which offered high fidelity pitch-shifting. In her words, “When I adjusted the pitch of my voice to 0.80, my natural voice became re-invented as what was clearly a gay man, who I called Steve. I became Steve; and Steve expressed himself as only he could.” Ciani adopted the male persona and collaborated with Peter Baumann of Tangerine Dream on “Steve Goes to a Party.” The track features Ciani-as-Steve adlibbing in decadent and delirious fashion alongside Baumann’s robotically funky beats.

Steve would emerge again a few years later at George Louvis’s Stardust Studios in New Jersey, to create “Steve Saves the World,” an absurdist and ecstatic proto-house groover complete with a gospel-esque chorus from the Stardust All-Stars. This EP is rounded out by a birthday wish to Ciani’s then-boyfriend Alfred on “Steve Happy Birthday Wishes” featuring Suzanne. Steve’s Out of the Closet perfectly captures the delirious techno-poptimism of the 1980s downtown avant-garde, with parallels in Robert Ashley’s Perfect Lives or Lynn Goldsmith’s project Will Powers, responsible for the track “Adventures in Success.” The Steve sleeve was designed by Eloise Shir-Juen Leigh, and the record also includes a birthday card with liner notes from Ciani."
items._genre: electronic / avant-garde / proto-house / experimental / new wave
items._cn_summary: 这张由Suzanne Ciani以男性分身Steve名义发表的EP，是她1980年代在纽约与纽泽西两地实验声响的奇异结晶。Ciani利用Eventide H 949效果器将人声降调至0.80，创造出名为Steve的男声人格，并在《Steve Goes to a Party》中与Tangerine Dream的Peter Baumann合作，以机械放克节拍搭配即兴癫狂的吟诵。同名曲《Steve Saves the World》呈现出福音合唱与早期浩室律动融合的荒谬狂欢气息，而结尾曲《Steve Happy Birthday Wishes》则用Linndrum鼓机勾勒出戏剧化且亲密的生日祝词。整张EP既是性别角色扮演的声音实验，也是对1980年代市中心前卫艺术中技术乐观主义与流行文化碎片的折射，与Robert Ashley、Will Powers等作品形成互文。除音乐外，封面由Eloise Shir-Juen Leigh设计，并附有Ciani撰写 liner notes 的生日卡，让这枚罕见的唱片兼具文献价值与私人纪念意义。

items.excerpt: Bit of a special one from John T. items.body:
Bit of a special one from John T. Gast’s 5 Gate Temple, finding anomalous wildcard St Agnis with a set of classical guitar improvisations under the Victoria Mingot alias - all enchantingly loose-limbed lowercase strums and murmurs tipped for fans of Loren Connors, Graham Lambkin, Virginia Astley, Vincent Gallo, Klein.

‘God Spill’ runs like a diary of broken sleep, taking things to their quietest, most ruminative depths. The dozen pieces are defined by plaintive melodic structuring for classical guitar, voice and pedals, on what sounds like dictaphone recordings that imbue everything with an eerie ferric intimacy. And those vocals are pretty special when they do appear, like a flickering filament in the aether of ‘i saw the sign’, recalling Mary Maddox off Mike Ratledge’s ‘Riddles of the Sphinx’, floating, Virginia Astley-like, on the frayed Lambkin-esque strum of ‘in plentitude of the harvest’, or more textural in the mournful raga meditation ‘om dhyana’.

The exquisitely discreet balance of un-showy yet transfixing instrumental economy is magnified by an un-moored sense of time and place and what the label call “soft rage” -  fully revealing itself with repeat listens.

Special stuff.
items._genre: experimental / lowercase / classical guitar / improvisation / avant-garde
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以十二首古典吉他即兴曲构成，采用录音机拾音与踏板效果，营造出低音量、松散的私密声响。人声在作品中如微光闪现，与拉格式冥想相互交织，旋律带有哀婉的轮廓。整体像一本破碎睡眠的日记，时间和地点感被剥离，留下一种被标签称为“柔和的愤怒”的情绪，需反复聆听才逐渐显形。作品在朴素克制的器乐编排中保持高度专注，延续了实验吉他与地下民谣脉络，并加入独特的个人语汇。

items.body:
Up until the release of his debut album in 2014, Shinichi Atobe managed to stay off grid since his release on Basic Channel’s Chain Reaction imprint back in 2001. He delivered the second-to-last 12” on the label and then disappeared without a trace, leaving behind a solitary 12” and a trail of speculation that led some people to wonder whether the project was in fact the work of someone on the Basic Channel payroll.

That killer Chain Reaction 12” was also a long time favourite of Demdike Stare, who had been trying to follow the trail and make contact with Atobe for many years before a lead from the Basic Channel office turned up an address in japan and - unbelievably - an album full of archival and new material. That material was compiled and released back in 2014 as Butterfly Effect.

And what a weird and brilliant album it is - deployed with a slow-churn opener that sounds like a syruppy Actress track, before working through a brilliantly sharp and tactile 9 minute Piano House roller that sounds like DJ Sprinkles at his most bittersweet, before diving headlong into a heady, Vainqueur inspired droneworld. It’s full of odd little signatures that gives the whole thing a timeless feel - like a sound bubble from another era.
items._genre: electronic / dub techno / ambient / deep house / drone
items._cn_summary: Shinichi Atobe 在 Chain Reaction 发行唱片后消失多年，直到 2014 年以这张专辑回归。开篇曲以缓慢铺陈的声响营造出类似 Actress 的粘稠氛围，随后转入一首质感锋利、触感清晰的九分钟钢琴浩室作品，情绪在 bittersweet 与律动之间游走，最后坠入受 Vainqueur 启发的深邃 drone 空间。专辑在 disparate 声音元素间自由切换，却始终保持着统一而奇特的个人印记，仿佛来自另一个时代的声音气泡。这种对 dub techno、deep house 和 ambient 的交叉处理，既延续了 Chain Reaction 体系的美学，又展现出作者独有的时间感与空间感，使整张作品在实验性与可听性之间取得平衡。

items.body:
Wah Wah Wino​'s Davy Kehoe, Morgan Buckley and Olmo are joined by avant legend Roger Doyle, among others, on a delectably brilliant, 54 minute collage, re-upped with new artwork for 2026.

An ode to the putative pleasures of ketamine, ‘KWALK’ emulates the effect of everyone’s fave equine dissociative with a mazy disarray of folk rock, ambient electronics and balmy, bandy-legged grooves bent for getting ketty with it. Inside, song structures quiesce to smeared samples and fractal lines of thought perhaps familiar to anyone who’s done a bump or two.

As with all Wino joints, normal logic is out the window, replaced by a loosey goosey slant that's a real pleasure to follow. In their slippery snakes ’n ladders chicanery, ‘KWALK’ recalls everything from Davy Kehoe's endlessly-rinsed 'Storm Desmond' to the Lost Highway OST, The KLF’s 'Chill Out' to Sigtryggur Berg Sigmarsson & BJ NIlsen’s ‘Avantgardegasse’ ace thru to Don Cherry’s communal free jazz jams and Laura Cannell’s folk flights in our minds, and should be considered a go-to slab for those times when the sofa’s on the ceiling and everyone’s too munted to pick another tune.

We have a special place in our hearts for mixtapes/collage pieces pressed to vinyl - and this one is prob the best we've heard since John T. Gast's 'Invocations II' set for Blowing Up The Workshop a few years back.
items._genre: collage / avant-garde / ambient / experimental / folk rock / free jazz
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是一部长约54分钟的声响拼贴作品，由Wah Wah Wino成员与先锋音乐家Roger Doyle等人共同创作。音乐以氯胺酮的迷幻解离体验为灵感，将民谣摇滚、环境电子与松弛歪斜的律动搅拌在一起，歌曲结构被溶解为模糊的采样与碎片化的思绪。整体逻辑松散而自由，呈现出一种如坠梦境般的流动性，令人联想到Davy Kehoe的经典曲目、电影《妖夜慌踪》原声、The KLF的《Chill Out》乃至Don Cherry的集体自由即兴。作品以黑胶形式呈现，在拼贴/混音带类发行中堪称近年来最出色的之一，适合在彻底放空、恍惚失焦的时刻聆听。

items.body:
An iconic album originally brought to life via Sweden's peerless iDEAL Recordings, Kali Malone’s 'The Sacrificial Code’ is a major work featuring almost two hours of concentrated, creeping organ pieces aligned to non traditional intonation/tuning systems. It's a stunning realisation of ideas borne out of academic and conceptual rigour, with a perception-altering quality that encourages exploration without a preordained endpoint.

The Sacrificial Code’ takes a more surgical approach to the methods first explored on last year’s ‘Organ Dirges 2016 - 2017’. Over the course of three parts performed on three different organs, Malone’s minimalist process captures a jarring precision of closeness, both on the level of the materiality of the sounds and on the level of composition.The recordings here involved careful close miking of the pipe organ in such a way as to eliminate environmental identifiers as far as possible - essentially removing the large hall reverb so inextricably linked to the instrument. The pieces were then further compositionally stripped of gestural adornments and spontaneous expressive impulse -  an approach that flows against the grain of the prevailing musical hegemony, where sound is so often manipulated, and composition often steeped in self indulgence. It echoes Steve Reich’s sentiment “..by voluntarily giving up the freedom to do whatever momentarily comes to mind, we are, as a result, free of all that momentarily comes to mind.”

With its slow, purified and seemingly austere qualities ‘The Sacrificial Code’ guides us through an almost trance-inducing process where we become vulnerable receptors for every slight movement, where every miniature shift in sound becomes magnified through stillness. As such, it’s a uniquely satisfying exercise in transcendence through self restraint and by this point inarguably a modern classic.
items._genre: contemporary classical / experimental / drone / minimalist / organ
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以近两小时的管风琴作品构成，采用非传统调音与律制，并在三架不同管风琴上完成录音。制作上通过近距离拾音尽可能消除大厅混响与环境标识，使声音的物质性直接呈现；作曲层面则剥离姿态性装饰与即兴表达，保留高度克制、近乎静止的结构，让细微的变化在静默中被放大。这种自反而严苛的创作路径呼应了极简主义传统，却以更具概念性的方式推进，形成一种通过自我限制达成的沉浸式聆听体验。专辑由瑞典独立厂牌发行，延续了实验音乐与当代古典的交叉脉络，在声音处理与作曲逻辑上均具有显著辨识度。

items.body:
Not the birth of acid house, but a thrilling piece of synth raga set to brisk disco beats, Bollywood soundtrack composer Charanjit Singh’s ’82 LP is simply a landmark in its own right, and a proper ‘floor-filler to boot.

Since its first reissue in 2010, Singh’s cult, early use of the TB-303 on driving machine beats has been erroneously hailed the birth of acid house. OK the formula is there, but Chris Carter’s ‘Spaces Between’ (1980) and his CTI jam ‘Dancing Ghosts’ got there a couple of years before Singh, at the very least, and neither really inform the genius of Phuture and co a few years later. In any event, ‘Synthesizing: Ten Ragas To A Disco Beat’ is just an incredibly fruity boost to any club, revolving 10 hypnotic, pulsating jams closer to early Irdial (say, Aqua Regia’s ‘Hot Love’) than owt from the Chi. 

Taking a minute away from knocking out Bollywood scores and leading his wedding band covering popular songs, Singh would land upon a stroke of genius with ‘Ten Ragas To A Disco Beat’, finding the sweetspot between prevailing hi-NRG disco and millennia of raga traditions that patently transcended the sum of their parts more than 40 years later. It sounds very much of its time, rather than the stripped back linearity of later acid house, evidenced in the florid keyboard urges of ‘Raga Bhupali’, transposing a steamy sort of club canter to somewhere even more humid.

A real club evergreen, suck it and see.
items._genre: synth raga / disco / electronic / experimental
items._cn_summary: 印度电影配乐作曲家Charanjit Singh于1982年创作的这张专辑，将千年拉格传统与当时兴起的hi-NRG迪斯科节拍结合，并以极早期的TB-303驱动机械律动。十首曲目围绕催眠性的脉动展开，键盘装饰繁复，使俱乐部节奏浸入湿润的热带氛围。文章指出其常被误认为酸浩室的起源，但实际上更接近一种独特的时代产物，既带有宝莱坞配乐的浓厚色彩，又超越了单纯东西方拼贴的范畴，成为兼具文化厚度与舞池能量的独立里程碑。

items.body:
Roping in Pierre Bastien and Mark Cunningham to provide brass, Mike Cooper turns in his most kaleidoscopic fourth world dream sequence to date, drawing on dub and exotica to harmonise with Andrew Pekler's marooned soundscapes...

Cooper admits in the liner notes that although he's often compared with Jon Hassell, it's German painter Mati Klarwein fantastical album covers that always reminded him exactly why he was doing what he was doing. Because Cooper makes music for imaginary places, not tangible soundtracks but half dreamed, half lived experiences that course through his catalog of experiments. And his process has never been quite so vivid as it is on 'Stochastic Parrot', a suite of vertiginous reverberations that are struck through with Cooper's "real and virtual" lap steel twangs, collaged together from samples and field recordings that wobble like heat haze. 

Different pockets of rhythm bash into each other on 'ARCHAEOPTERYX', accompanied by Bastien and Cunningham's spiraling brass improvisations. And Cooper holds the sounds together with his lulling repeated phrases; the hand drums might sound as if they're in conflict with the cycling drum machine crashes, but that's the point - it's not like channeling a dream so much as it's like being subjected to three or four dreams simultaneously. It's the ghosts of jazz fusion being raked over coals at midnight: just tune into 'SUMATRA SAMPHIRE', with its distant animalistic wails and popcorn drums, or the granulized 'HAT YAI', that sounds like the prelude to a druggy ritual.
items._genre: fourth world / exotica / dub / experimental / sound collage / improvisation
items._cn_summary: 专辑邀来 Pierre Bastien 与 Mark Cunningham 演奏铜管，以 lap steel、采样和田野录音拼贴出悬坠的声响景观。不同节奏段落互相碰撞，手鼓与电子鼓机形成不协调的对位，铜管即兴螺旋上升，人声反复句则将碎片粘合。Cooper 称其创作是为了虚构之地，而非实存影像，音乐如多重梦境同时涌入，爵士融合的幽灵在午夜被灼烤。全作在浑浊混响与颗粒化处理中保持高度画面感，既是音景也是仪式性的前奏。

items.body:
For us, still the standout Short Span, ​a staggering label debut from Marija Rasa aka emer, previously seen on Stroom and here operating at the opiated levels where classic steppers dub techno x Lolina’s frayed dubs collide, all smouldering dubwise pearls tipped FFO False Aralia, Ugnė Uma, Rhythm & Sound, Sade.

Marija Rasa’s dream sequence of crawl-pace slugs sways on syrupy bass and is fully sublimated to seductive vapours. For anyone paying closer attention, ‘Fog’ clearly reprises and expands on the elusive, smoky vibes felt on her 2024 drop for Stroom and in ’25 for Chicago’s Lillerne Tapes. However her sound is notably strapped with more supple layers and perfused with a groggy spirit that really hits for night owls or those chasing trip hop dragons.

‘Fog’ operates at the speed of slowed thought with seven cuts to sink right into. For half an hour she swaddles minds in high tog textures as tracks pass-out into hazed bliss from the gentle descent into swole subs on ‘Below Altitude’, to gorgeous, spongiform bass and soul-grab chords of ‘Open’, and like Moritz Von Oswald smelting his jazz trio back to Rhythm & Sound fundamentals in ‘Nobody Speaks’. A knack for eking out organic detail is most enchanting on the interplay of aerosolised thizz and subs on ‘Room Five’, and leaves us levitating in the ssabæ-esque wooze to ‘The Evergreen Fog’ and hobbled, ghostly shape of ‘Calling’.

A modern classic of the form.
items._genre: dub techno / experimental / ambient
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑将经典dub techno的步进节奏与Lolina式的松散拼贴相结合，在黏稠贝斯和烟雾缭绕的声场中构建出催眠般的慢速梦境。七首作品在三十分钟内持续下潜，从低音晕染的缓降氛围到海绵质感的和弦抓握，再到近乎爵士三重奏被熔炼回律动根基的段落，展现了对有机细节的敏锐捕捉。人声碎片与亚低频的相互作用令人悬浮，整体气质慵懒而迷醉，适合深夜聆听。作为Marija Rasa在Stroom与Lillerne Tapes之后的新作，其声音层次更为柔韧，且带着一种恍惚的醉意，在当代电子乐语境中延续并拓展了dub与ambient交汇处的独特脉络。

items.body:
A richly metaphoric expression of worries about climate change and marine devastation, blending hydrophonic acoustic and electronic sources to spell out a sonorous, subaquatic narrative FFO Mark Jenkin film scores, Thomas Köner, AFX’s SAW II...

“After All Hands Bury The Cliffs At Sea (2023) and Black Clouds Above The Bows (2022), Amsterdam-based collective Wanderwelle presents the final entry of their album trilogy for Important Records (IMPREC). Conceived as a sonic reflection on the climate crisis and its devastating impact on coastal ecosystems, Ghosts Beneath The Brine (2026) addresses the mass deaths of fish, seabirds, crustaceans and countless other creatures that call these seas home, now rapidly being overfished, warming and acidifying.

Where antique cavalry trumpets played a central role on Black Clouds Above The Bows and a dying church organ shaped All Hands Bury The Cliffs At Sea, cymbals form the core of Ghosts Beneath The Brine. The instruments were submerged in seawater for extended periods of time and played with a bow at various stages of corrosion. As the bronze alloy gradually reacted with the saltwater, their sound transformed, becoming darker, more fragile and unstable. Over time, the metal began to sing in ghostly overtones, as if haunted by the waters that shaped it. Much like large groups of fish shimmering beneath the surface, the cymbals slowly lost their shine, both sonically and physically, as salt and time took hold.

Alongside its environmental narrative, the album draws from maritime mythology. Echoes of the sea bishop, the kraken, devil whales and sea serpents emerge throughout its soundscape. Once feared and revered, these creatures now exist only in the liminal space between folklore and memory, haunting the collective imagination like omens from a forgotten age. Through immersive textures and submerged harmonies, Wanderwelle intertwines myth and mourning, inviting listeners to drift between the real and the spectral. If humanity continues on its current course, familiar species such as sharks, oysters and even gulls may soon share the same fate as their legendary predecessors, becoming ghosts beneath the brine.”
items._genre: ambient / dark ambient / experimental / electronic / drone
items._cn_summary: Wanderwelle以浸入海水并随腐蚀程度用弓演奏的铙钹为核心声响，为气候危机与海洋生态灾难谱写沉郁的水下叙事。作为三部曲终章，专辑延续了前作对濒危自然与神话记忆的凝视，将鱼类、海鸟与传说中海怪的身影交织在逐渐暗哑、碎裂的金属泛音中。环境音色与电子声源融合，营造出介于真实与幽灵之间的漫游感，既是对过度捕捞与海水升温的哀悼，也是神话在当代的余响。

items.body:
Following 2024's avant-prog-Americana song cycle 'Viewfinder', guitar deity Wendy Eisenberg goes chamber pop on their self-titled latest, tipping their hat to Judee Sill, Gillian Welch, Van Dyke Parks and Joanna Newsom.

When they relocated from rural Western Mass to Brooklyn in 2020, Eisenberg was hit with a wave of longing for the open landscape they'd left behind. They were drawn to classic country and folk records, perfectly poised offerings from Willie Nelson and John Hartford and lavish pop-folk records from Jimmy Webb and Van Dyke Parks as well as the weirdo fare of Richard Dawson et al. So when 'Viewfinder', a way of deconstructing the experience following eye surgery in 2011, was finished, Eisenberg started writing "genuinely folk songs" and swapping out their usually showy, complex performance for a form of relative simplicity that they explain is inherently strange all the same. Prog becomes folk, basically. And they're not on their own; more eaze handles the lush string arrangements, playing pedal steel and synthesizer, and a loose band forms around that axis, with drummer Ryan Sawyer and bassist Trevor Dunn.

But despite the personnel, it's resolutely Eisenberg's album. Their voice sounds unrestrained, capturing the era they're referencing and their own emotional (and physical upheaval). It's fragile but strangely warm on the country-tinged Jim O'Rourke-like 'Will You Dare' and hypnotic on the baroque 'Meaning Business', a track they wrote in the wake of David Lynch's death as the antithesis of the "Lynchian" aesthetic. And they should really get their flowers for this one; Americana, especially now, is teetering on a precipice, almost knocked off the edge by half-assed, churned attempts and underwritten pastiches. Eisenberg's an attentive listener and someone who's surrounded themself with similarly sensitive ears, people who are able to fill their heart and their sound so what we hear is as byzantine as a Gastr del Sol record but sounds as effortless as John Prine's 'Angel From Montgomery'. If you loved Joanna Newsom's 'Ys' and have never found anything quite as satisfying, this is the one.
items._genre: chamber pop / avant-garde / progressive folk / Americana
items._cn_summary: 这张同名专辑延续了温迪·艾森伯格从上一张前卫民谣作品开始的转向，将前卫摇滚的复杂结构带入室内流行和美国根源音乐，形成一种简化却依然奇异的声响。制作上由莫尔·伊兹负责弦乐编排、踏板钢棒和合成器，瑞安·索耶与特雷弗·邓恩提供节奏基底，整体松散而丰满。艾森伯格的人声在乡村色彩与巴洛克织体之间游走，脆弱中带着暖意；评论称其编曲如加斯特·德尔·索尔般繁复，听感却像约翰·普莱恩那样自然流畅，是乔安娜·纽森代表作之后少见能满足类似期待的专辑。

items.body:
Stefan Betke aka Pole’s holy trilogy of frayed dub experiments resurfaces for a 20th anniversary reissue, taking us back to smokey nights at the turn of the century and some of the finest post basic-channel dub echoes ever released. Essential listening if you’re into anything from Rhythm & Sound to Vainqueuer, Jon Hassell to Jackie Mittoo.

As legend goes, Pole took his name from a malfunctioning Waldorf 4-Pole filter which produced hisses and pops which weren’t really controllable or predictable, much like a living organism. Betke realised the potential and came to alchemically morph and render them with judicious FX dubbing into a groundbreaking sort of minimalist electro-dub that sounds exceedingly good with a spliff and glass of booze. Working somewhere between the variants of abstract techno on Chain Reaction and Mille Plateaux’s cutting edge minimalist strains, Pole’s first trio of albums inarguably helped lay the foundations for dub techno as it’s come to be known and are held in the highest regard by practically everyone who owns them. 

The Pole aesthetic is patently laid out in ‘1’, where his organic clicks ’n pops come out to play accompanied by lilting organ and jazzy bass channelling Jackie Mittoo via Jon Hassell and Rhythm & Sound into a uniquely, gauzy, gaseous state. But for us, his sound really comes into its own on ‘2’, where the opening melodica motif still sends electric shivers down the spine and opens out into the kind of sculpted, layered dub bass that spawned dubstep, and flows out into myriad, mesmerising permutations, but this time swapping out the hazy licks for a cavernous, brooding melancholy (that really matched this moody teenager’s psyche at the time) and reverberated through into the more humid, drizzly and funereal atmosphere conjured in the equally spellbinding spectral dub metaphysics of ‘3’.

So strong was the impact of these albums on the late ‘90s underground, they even generated a “pastiche” that was unwittingly issued (and subsequently deleted) by Fat Cat on their split series, but was purportedly made by V/Vm in a snidey but frankly hilarious prank, albeit one that demonstrates just how ubiquitous and influential Betke’s sound was at the time. More than that, it’s fair to say the 20 year cycle hasn’t rinsed out the appeal of this triptych one bit; it remains one of electronic music’s most enigmatic and strangely moving, tactile bodies of work.
items._genre: dub techno / minimal electronic / experimental / glitch
items._cn_summary: Stefan Betke以Pole为名，将失灵的Waldorf滤波器中不可控的嘶嘶声与爆音当作活体素材，通过效果器与混音手法转化为开创性的极简电子回响。本套重制版收录其最初三张专辑，作品在Ch沁一脉的抽象科技与Mille Plateaux的极简主义之间展开，以有机的点击声、风琴、爵士贝斯与旋律口琴构建出朦胧弥散的声响空间。第二张中的层叠低音与洞穴般的忧郁气质尤其影响深远，被视为dub techno奠基之作，甚至启发过一首恶搞式仿作。跨20年回听，它依然保持独特纹理与神秘感知力，是电子音乐史中兼具触感与情感张力的重要篇章。

items.body: From Finland with love. A couple of glasses of kossu, a book of Arto Paasilinna, a record of the hardcore punk legends Kaaos, and then a movie (Calamari Union, yes) of Aki Kaurismaki, our true Homeric hero, have always been more than enough to attest to our fascination with that wonderful country. But there's more: a record label that, with the icastic name "We Jazz," helps illuminate our music like a sonic aurora borealis. The operational branches are “We Jazz Records”, established in 2016 to present "cutting-edge music on the jazz continuum in various formats, with vinyl being the primary format," and its younger sibling, “Other Power,” "a platform of all great music that doesn't logically fall under the scope of We Jazz." Both labels are curated and designed by Matti Nives. Should it be not enough satisfactory, then know that a quarterly magazine (actually a real glossy volume with color photographs) guarantees you the best editorial coverage of jazz/free/impro music available out there. For those not yet familiar with Helsinki’s alleys, we'd like to map the area with three, red marked, albums from the catalog: Mike Reed, "The Separatist Party"; Cosmic Ear, "Traces"; and Pat Thomas & XT, "Strata, Act." Completely different records with an enormous musical profile as a common factor, they represent an artistic asset value able to guarantee immortality to any label. We Jazz's new initiative includes the digital release of 5 tracks per month by bands not part of its roster, for the benefit of Bandcamp subscribers, and the kick-off is provided by this compilation which, with volumes 1-3, covers the period from January through March. We are dealing with such a cornucopia of music that it's worth a quick overview of all the musicians involved. UUSI AIKA (Sammaltuka). Strings, harp, wind instruments, drive the listener towards Finnish woodland mythology, Indian raga-inspired colors and Asian minimalism. HENRIETTE EILERTSEN TRIO (Fly Ikaros). Flautist's new band delivers a captivating composition with balanced interactions that at the same time manages to be intimate and almost limitlessly expansive. LAU NAU (Kosmospyorat). Synth drones mesh with the sound of a living garden, bees buzzing along beneath singing birds while simple chords carry dreams on oscillating waves. FELIX ALEXANDER LYBECK (Slapat Allting Hem). The magic of a Nordic forest, strange, weird folk notes intertwined with indie intimacy, creating music that feels both grounded and unearthly. JYVASKYLA WORKSHOP BAND 1970 (Nadaswaram). A previously unissued post-bop gem, this concert captures a set of groovy, adventurous and exotic compositions that firmly placed Finland on the global jazz map. LINNEA TALP (She came out of the white fog). The pipe organ is pushed in an unusual manner that allows the instrument's character to be revealed, gently, patiently, as though being teased out of hiding. ALAN BRAUFMAN (Angels). Alto sax and flute, among the actors of the 70s "loft" scene in New York, he returns after a long hiatus to lead an all star team (Patricia Brennan, Luke Stewart and Chad Taylor) between post-bop and oriental influences. FYSIIKKA & KEMIA (Luontokokemuksia). “Rural psych-jazz improvisations by Finnish bastard sons of Arbete & Fritid". Or, free music beyond the threshold where Swedish prog and Finnish weirdness collide. PIETU ARVOLA (Kummallinen ilmestys). Experimental tools like the daxophone and a dual looper called Coquantus are used to process textures combined with modular synths. MARK HARWOOD (The Course of a Year). Australian born, Berlin based, he runs a platform that works at the intersection of experimental music, performance, literature and visual art. GARD NILSSEN ACOUSTIC UNITY (Acoustic Unity). The sound of the sublime trio wrapped in the brutalist architecture and the magnetic audience of Barbican Centre, London 2018, delivers sheer, top notch, jazz aesthetic. HATKA (Peace Piece). Free, electro-acoustic textures and raw impro for an intense and playful outcome by a Transatlantic ensemble of three seasoned improvisers. KADI VIJA (Hands). A vocal instrumentalist who treats the human voice as a horn or a rhythm machine, here accompanied by piano, synth, vibraphone and percussions. PHARDAH (Village of Skulls). Featuring veterans of the Finnish experimental music and free jazz scene, along with a younger generation drummer, to unleash a vigorous bass riff, eventually accelerating into a wild collective gallop. If you're looking for a way (one of a zillion…) to epitomize in 1 hour what “Free” in music means, this compilation could be the perfect spot to pitch your tent. For our part, we already put in the collimator Vol. 2, sure thing. Check it out on Bandcamp . Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑是芬兰We Jazz厂牌推出的订阅系列，收录2026年1至3月期间多组非厂牌音乐人的作品。内容涵盖多种方向：有以弦乐、管乐和竖琴营造芬兰森林神话与印度拉格色彩的UUSI AIKA，有长笛三重奏展现亲密与宽广并存即兴平衡的亨丽埃特三重奏，也有合成器嗡鸣与花园环境声交织的劳瑙，以及将北欧森林怪诞民谣与独立气息结合的创作；同时包含一段1970年芬兰爵士工作坊的未发表现场，展现后波普的律动与异域风骨，还有管风琴被以非常规方式缓慢揭示其特性的独奏，以及来自纽约70年代loft场景的萨克斯/长笛演奏。整体上，合辑以编辑视角呈现当代即兴、自由爵士、电子声响与北欧/东方民间元素之间的交叉，体现了厂牌在爵士连续性框架下的开放策展思路。值得关注的是其中多首作品将爵士即兴与地貌、自然、神话等文化意象结合，形成不同于主流爵士的听感维度。

items.excerpt: バトルスの創立メンバーとしても知られるタイヨンダイ・ブラクストンが、ポスト・クラシカル系のレーベルであるイレースド・テープスから新作を発表。丁寧に磨き抜かれ、ヒリヒリとした緊張感を醸す電子音の数々からは、オウテカやエイフェックス・ツインといったIDMの因子を見い出せる。一方で、肉感的グルーヴを創出するミニマルな反復フレーズには、そのようなIDMではあまり見られない享楽性が窺える。なかでも“UnFS”は、執拗に繰り返されるリズムとメロディーを少しづつ変化させることで、フロアでも映える機能的なダンス・ミュージックとしての側面を創出している。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑呈现了高度精炼的电子声响，在细密打磨的声音纹理中弥漫着紧张感，令人联想到IDM领域的标志性人物。与此同时，重复性的极简节奏与旋律在细微变化中逐渐展开，为音乐注入了肉感的律动与享乐气质，打破了实验电子常见的冷感框架。其中一首曲目尤其突出，它通过执着重复的结构创造出适用于舞池的功能性舞曲面向，将前卫声响与身体体验融合在一起。整体上，作品在智性设计与感官愉悦之间取得了平衡，适合对实验电子和IDM有深入兴趣的听众。

items.body: Label: Intakt Records, 2026 Personnel - Kaja Draksler: piano; Petter Elder: bass; Christian Lillinger: drums. The modern creative European trio Punkt Vrt. Plastik — comprising Slovenian pianist Kaja Draksler, Swedish bassist Petter Eldh, and German drummer Christian Lillinger — releases its fourth album. All three artists contribute compositions, adhering to unyielding rhythmic intricacy and classical melodicism to shape music that bristles with provocative interplay, freedom, and heightened expressiveness. Draksler's " Yogen " thrives on a half-step-shifting, mystery-inducing pulse. The pianist opts for motivic figures while the drummer moves from erratic fibrillation to deliberate syncopated fragmentation. This taut flow is regularly interrupted by pacifying jazztronica sections that contrast with the more Rage Against The Machine-inspired thrill of the opening. While Eldh's " Mariatorget 87 " also takes a distinctly jazz path, Lillinger's "For Sybille" finds Draksler veering toward a modern classical direction, rich with intervallic friction. The classical influence runs throughout the album but peaks with Eldh's arrangement of " När Världens Hopp Förtvinat Stod ”, a Lutheran chorale written in 1589 by German clergyman and composer Johannes Rhau. Draksler's 4/4 minor-mode piano movements find perfect backing from bass and drums. The classical vein continues on " Mere Punkt ”, co-composed by Draksler and Eldh, but shifts sharply for Lillinger's skittish “ Vrt ", which closes the album with a gallant composure. Eldh's "Trip" is one of the most gripping pieces, unfurling an oblique groove under a defiant time signature. Despite the complexity, the trio locks together in a fantastic, hooked-up rhythmic flow charged with creative harmonic progressions and tension. If " EKV " sounds progressive and warped, " For A / Kompress " is lyrical, cyclic, and powerful, opening with a dreamy aura that, handled with a firm grip, gradually intensifies. Surprising is hearing the trio lean into a hard-swinging juncture on " Granular Navigation ". Lillinger, unapologetic about his triplet-based ride cymbal patterns, wrote the piece; he also offers methodical snare buzz rolls that color a more abstract passage built from clustered chordal angularity. Punkt Vrt. Plastik engages in absorbing conversations of rhythm and breath, threading in occasional head-nodding grooves that arrive with atypical shapes and feels. The trio continues to seek new perspectives on composition, taking a freewheeling approach throughout. Kompress even offers a wider lens, feeling thoroughly contemporary without burying its influences from other eras. It stands as a fine addition to the group's catalog of state-of-the-art albums. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Yogen ► 02 - Trip ► 07 - For A / Kompress ► 09 - När Världens Hopp Förtvinat Stod
items._genre: avant-garde jazz / modern classical / experimental / progressive
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由钢琴、贝斯与鼓组成的三重奏呈现，三位成员各自贡献作曲，在复杂节奏与古典旋律之间建立张力。钢琴常以动机式短句推进，鼓手在颤动性律动与切分碎片之间转换，部分段落引入爵士电子氛围，形成对比。林林格的作品让钢琴走向现代古典方向，充满音程摩擦；德拉克勒斯勒与埃尔德合作的段落则突出循环性和抒情性，氛围从梦幻逐渐增强。专辑还改编了1589年的路德教派圣咏，钢琴以小调四四拍进行，贝斯与鼓提供稳定支撑。贝斯手的创作在非常规节拍中展开倾斜的律动，结尾曲以从容的作曲方式收束。整体上，三重奏在严密互动中保持自由表达，将古典影响、即兴逻辑与当代声响编织在一起，偶尔进入硬摇摆段落，也出现由音簇构成的抽象段落。它展现了乐队对作曲新视角的持续探索，兼具结构的复杂性与听觉上的可感流动。

items.body: Ahead of their thrillingly restless new record Honest Feeling Album, Hakushi Hasegawa speaks to Natalie Marlin about operating outside arbitrary boundaries, and the importance of leaving things unexplained Image by George Asakura Before Hakushi Hasegawa explains anything, remember this: not everything is meant to be explained. Fight the urge to wrangle their music’s restless gusts across genre and sound and touchpoint, to define their work by rigid tenets of avant-jazz or glitch pop or jungle or funk, or any other name that would trace mere portions of the work and cast aside the rest as unfit anomaly. To give yourself over to Hakushi Hasegawa is to enter a tacit agreement: not all will fit together neatly, or even be understood absolutely, even... The post The Necessary Unnecessary: An Interview with Hakushi Hasegawa appeared first on The Quietus.
items._genre: avant-jazz / glitch pop / jungle / electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以不安分的声响贯穿多类型边界，在先锋爵士、故障流行、丛林与放克之间急速游走，拒绝被单一标签覆盖。乐评强调其作品并不追求被完全理解，而是让不可解释的部分保持开放性，听者需放弃对秩序与明确定义的执念，才能进入其内部逻辑。声音设计充满速度感与断裂感，兼具即兴的松散和电子编程的精密，呈现出一种刻意不驯服的表达。值得关注的是它如何在类型缝隙中建立自己的语法，以及那种对固有分类体系的持续挑衅。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — For this ambitious recording of original compositions--which were dedicated to "the two immortals who produced the greatest orchestral jazz music," Duke Ellington and Gil Evans--Neil resuscitated the old New Jazz Orchestra that he had directed and help found back in the early 1960s with Jon Hiseman and Tony Reeves (as well as Jack Bruce, Dick Heckstall-Smith, and Ian Carr and Henry Lowther). The music was recorded sometime in 1971 but it was not released to the public until sometime in 1972, probably early. The list of musicians is a veritable Who's Who of British Jazz Rock.A. "A Symphony of Amaranths" (24:59) a seriously classical composition and production with some jazzy elements but more of an Impressionist/Expressionist type of cinematic music. Absolutely, stunningly beautiful! Without hesitation I must say that this composition alone does tremendous justice to the two heroes to which he dedicated it. I find no flaw; correction: I find myself too small to even possibly due justice to any critique or criticism to this amazing piece of music. I wouldn't change a single note it feels so perfect, feeds my soul so completely. (50/50) - "Carillon" - "Nocturne" - "Entracte" - "Improptu"B1. "The Dong With a Luminous Nose" (11:50) narrator Ivor Cutler recites the words of Edward Lear over Neil's wonderfully fitting jazz-infused orchestra soundtrack. (22.875/25)"Three Poems": Norma Winstone sings the poetry lyrics of W.B. Yeats, James Joyce, and Lewis Carroll, respectively, during the following three musical renderings of Neil's own musical interpretations. Norma was fresh off of being voted by Melody Maker magazine as the top female Jazz Singer of 1971 (which makes this quite the coup for Neil). B2. "After Long Silence" (4:09) Norma Winstone has an incredible voice: one that I would follow to the ends of the Earth. Her voice reminds me of the upbeat, positive tones of both Swing Out Sister's Corinne Drewery and No Small Affair's Demi Moore performance of "My Funny Valentine" as dubbed by Chrissie Faith. (10/10)B3. "She Weeps Over Rahoon" (3:22) Norma, again, but this time singing a very different style: here sounding like a fuller voiced, whisper-toned version of the great modern avant prog singer Elaine di Falco (Thinking Plague, Francesco Zago projects for Fading Records/AltrOck Productions in the 2010s). (9.125/10)B4. "Will You Walk a Little Faster?" (3:48) opening with some upper register scatting � la Ella or Urszula Dudziak, but once the song gets into full swing (pun intended) it's a showtune tour de force/extravaganza. Ver ysimilar to the skill level and stylings of Barbra Streisand's Broadway career and previewing the type of sounds and skills we'll soon be hearing from Renaissance's Annie Haslam. (9.25/10) Total time: 48:08A zesty tongue-in-cheek version of the UK national anthem ends the album, but we don't need to count that (as fun as it was to hear everyone in the studio's control room cracking up at the end).Neal was one of those incredibly gifted and talented humans whose artistic abilities almost require one to drop the mantle of "Renaissance Man" on his shoulders. What a loss to the music world it was that his career in the writing and publishing world spawned such a lucrative and demanding life for him. (Author of Britain's World Book Encyclopedia and founding member of the Dorling Kindersley [DK] "How Things Work" series of children's books--all of which led to sales in the multiples of millions.) Each of his symphonic, choral, and New Jazz Orchestra projects could have generated equal fame and, hopefully, fortune. But here we are.A/five stars; a masterpiece of music no matter what kind you want to call it. I am so glad to have discovered this amazing album; I will cherish FOREVER!
items._genre: jazz rock / orchestral jazz / avant-garde / fusion
items._cn_summary: Neil Ardley 1971年录制的这张专辑致敬了 Duke Ellington 与 Gil Evans，延续并扩展了他六十年代创立的 New Jazz Orchestra 的编制。A面是一首近25分钟的交响组曲，以古典作曲结构为基底，融合爵士即兴与印象派、表现主义色彩，营造出电影配乐般的宏大叙事感。B面则更富戏剧性与文学性：Ivor Cutler 朗诵 Edward Lear 的诗作，女歌手 Norma Winstone 以多变声线演绎叶芝、乔伊斯和卡罗尔的三首诗歌，从清亮抒情到拟声即兴再到百老汇式表演，展示了她刚从 Melody Maker 票选年度最佳爵士女歌手而来的实力。最后以一段幽默恶搞的英国国歌收尾，为整体氛围增添了几分游戏感。专辑将古典管弦乐、爵士大乐队、前卫作曲与诗歌朗诵融为一体，制作阵容几乎囊括英国爵士摇滚界的重要人物，是1970年代初大型融合作品中的独特样本。
