items.body:
Dreader than dread dub vapors from Ghost Dubs, in a lineage stretching from Dadawah to Burial Mix, Vainqueur to Resilent, Pole to Rod Modelll...​

Toiling in Berlin’s deep seam of abstract dub practice that scrolls back to Rhythm & Sound’s earliest via Pole’s dusty convections and Chain Reaction's fritzed mutations; Ghost Dubs embodies the art of dub as method with a strong haul of dematerialised, sludgy tramplers operating close to the scuzzy heart of Kevin Martin, aka The Bug. Uncompromisingly in-the-zone and dank as a bong, the dozen cuts get right under the skin, up-the-pharynx, with an intoxicatingly sedated and hallucinatory quality that impresses murky, vaporous patterns on the back of blunted eyelids and may possibly raise knees to its slompy skank and imaginary physics. 

Of course, the sound is rooted in the innovative, half century-old traditions of Jamaican dub, as established by King Tubby and Lee “Scratch” Perry, and developed by the likes of Scientist or Mad Professor. But Ghost Dubs picks it up at the point where it diffused into techno and noise during the ‘90s, taking that sound as a jump-off into his microcosm of granular, atomised atmospheric disintegration that nevertheless holds to a steady ballast of scoop-worrying sub-bass tremors. No doubt anyone who’s followed the devolution of this sound outside Jamaica, from NYC illbient to Berlin dub techno, will recognise his hands-on-desk tekkerz ushering the sound into oblique new spaces with a canny sense of proprioception that locates it somewhere in fissure between classic and contemporary soundspheres.

From the caustic attrition of ‘Chemical’, thru the inverted mulch of ‘Dub Lobotomy’, to the sensuous but elephantine trample of ‘Hot Wired’ and tumescent swell of ‘Circles Lines’ ,Ghost Dubs leaves his clammy fingerprint on every cut. Some are primed to bend your Clarks, as with the bilgy step of ‘The Regulator’, and airborne skank of ‘Thin Line’, and the harness-tugging pressure of ‘Dub Battle’, but they’re all held in check with a overarching slowness that gels the 12 tracks as a proper end-to-end listen in the manner of Pole’s early albums with a deeply reliable robustness and temper that stakes it out as arguably canonic tackle.
items._genre: dub techno / experimental dub / dark ambient / bass music
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑延续了从Dadawah到Burial Mix、从Rhythm & Sound到Chain Reaction的抽象dub脉络，将牙买加dub传统的回响处理拆解至微观层面，与柏林dub techno、噪声音响交织成一片浑浊的低频场域。十二首作品以颗粒感、雾化的音色解体为核心，厚重次低频贝斯线提供沉稳的根基，整体节奏缓慢而具有压迫感。从酸蚀感的磨蚀到沼泽般的钝步，从空中漂浮的律动到肿胀涌动的氛围，Ghost Dubs以极端内省的方式处理声音材料，在经典dub法则与当代声响实验的裂缝中开辟出自己的空间。十二首曲目连贯一体，适合作为完整的端到端聆听体验。

items.body:
A Colourful Storm's Fleetway Tapes series follows classic entries from Time Is Away, Vladimir Ivkovic, Felix K, Young Sparks and others with a heart-stopping selection put together by Berlin-based film journo Florence Scott-Anderton, a fathoms-deep, laser-focused mix that doesn't come around often, engulfing high-art/low-culture TV samples with a series of cues excavated from film - think of it as a sort of Blockbuster Video nostalgia-tinted answer to Time Is Away's flawless thematic mixes.

Florence knows her shit. Not only does she provide words and sounds for MUBI's international film mag Notebook, where she's covered Tōru Takemitsu and crafted an ode to Derek Jarman, but she's a resident on NTS's ace Sounds on Screen. Nose through her archive and you'll find a deep dive into the sonics of lesbian cinema, an exploration of Aussie icon Nicole Kidman's filmography, a mix dedicated to Japanese vanguard Satoshi Kon, a history of the sounds of Iranian cinema and loads more (really, there's so much). And it's this same anti-hierarchal level of expertise and passion she brings to 'A Requiem for Prime Time', a very personal journey thru her memory banks that collages dialog samples, TV ambiance, art oddities and various soundtrack selections that eschew the usual narrative. We'll be honest, we've gotten pretty fatigued with the OST industrial complex and its parallel stream of repetitive, hyper-referential shovelcore outings from genre dorks whose interest in music peaked with 'Stranger Things'. Thankfully, Florence opts to sail down a completely different channel, not avoiding the mythologised synth wave completely (Simon Boswell's killer 'Hardware' cue 'It's Horrible... I Love It... What Is It?' shows up as a bonus like a peanut in caramel) but concentrating on dislocated, provocative and often completely overlooked sounds that drift far from the established "score bro" cult canon.

"It's not like you want to be an accountant," a muffled Australian voice narrates over ketamized SFX on the opening side. "You, like me, want something that is creative, that is out there a little bit." A clip from Peter Mullan's 2002 drama 'The Magdalene Sisters' appears, pulling us right back to that moment when trip-hop aesthetics bled into Hollywood's mainstream, and before long we’re riding a different train of thought, stitching cavernous twee rock with pastoral post-Glass minimalism and scratchy, evocative environmental recordings. Canned sax solos and airy guitar plucks fade into cuts from Mike Figgis's notorious experimental film 'Timecode', and somehow Woijciech Kilar's end credits from Francis Ford Copolla's 'Bram Stoker's Dracula' show up for some thematic relief. On the flip, Florence opens the side with waved, Eno-style psychedelic ambient that's ruptured by a beat isolated from Joe Delia's sordid score for Abel Ferarra's famously abhorred erotic thriller 'The Blackout'. From here, we're catapulted across Christophe Beck's 'Bring It On' soundscapes, a cloudy, sub-heavy ambient marvel from Brooklyn artist Alex Bienstock and even Joe Jackson's aborted theme for 'Mike's Murder', a 1984 Debra Winger vehicle that had its entire soundtrack replaced with a more palatable one from John Barry.

Really, we can't say enough about this one. If you've been following Scott-Anderton's mixes (if you want just one, we recommend her Krzysztof Kieślowski selection), you'll already know how vital her point of view is, but she takes us to a completely new zone with this one. It's a head-scratcher that'll have you wondering what it is yr actually listening to - a way to contemplate the Y2K era as it completely vanishes into popular mythology.
items._genre: ambient / film soundtrack / experimental / post-rock / sound collage
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以电视黄金时代的影视配乐为素材的声音拼贴作品，由柏林电影记者Florence Scott-Anderton操刀。她在NTS电台长期主持Sounds on Screen节目，专注于电影声音的深度挖掘，这张混音延续了她反等级化、高低文化并置的策展思路。整张专辑穿越90至00年代的影视配乐线索，将Peter Mullan剧情片中的对话采样、Mike Figgis实验电影的切碎片段、Eno式迷幻氛围与独立吉他小品交织在一起，刻意回避了当下影视配乐圈层流行的怀旧合成器浪潮。作品呈现出一种漂移的、去叙事化的结构，将被主流遗忘的电视环境音与艺术电影配乐碎片缝合，在怀旧情绪与解构之间建立张力。

items.body:
Softly softly does it for the gorgeous debut duo of soundtrack composer Elori Saxl & saxophonist Henry Solomon with their lushly ephemeral grasp of 4th world ambient jazz, tipped for the anyone on the line between Lynch/Badalamenti, TLF Trio, Laurel Halo, Arve Henriksen or Alex Zhang-Hungtai's Love Theme side-wind.

Captured over a few days in LA, ‘Seeing Is Believing’ frames the sax player’s searching feel for tone across soundscapes sparingly coloured in subtle harmonic gradients by Elori Saxl’s fluttering Juno 106 keys. The nine parts are testament to the duo’s near-telepathic level of intuition and mutual vision of a palpably tissue-soft atmospheric music; one where spectres of ’70s minimalism and ’80s new age bleed forward into structures equally informed by soundsystem culture and contemporary pop production, achieving a sort of slow shifting, ecological pressure system that is a pleasure to sink into.

Within her richly visual, implicitly storytelling style, Elori Saxl draws on a wellspring of experience in composing for new music ensembles, and soundtracking and directing films for New Yorker and Slate, to set spacious dimensions for Solomon’s ruminative baritone sax and bass clarinet to wander freely. A quiet sense of restraint defines proceedings as their forms gently grow and sway from the dusky licks of ‘Reverence’ thru the gauzy lustre of the title piece, conjuring a geosmin waft in ‘Raindrops’ and LA hills panorama on ‘Reno Silver’, or balmiest breeze of Glass-like phrasing on ‘A Thousand Steps’, into the gorgeous, pitch bent and sensual sorcery summoned in standout ‘Heart.’

Stunner.
items._genre: ambient jazz / fourth world / experimental / new age
items._cn_summary: Elori Saxl与Henry Solomon的首张合作专辑在洛杉矶数日内录制完成，萨克斯的沉思音色与Juno 106合成器稀疏的和声梯度交织成柔软的声景。九段作品展现二人近乎心灵感应的直觉默契，将七十年代极简主义与八十年代新世纪音乐的气息注入当代制作结构，形成缓慢迁移的生态压力系统。Saxl为电影配乐与新音乐合奏团的创作背景在此化为广阔的空间维度，让Solomon的低音萨克斯与低音单簧管自由游走。从《Reverence》的朦胧乐句到标题曲的薄纱光泽，从《Raindrops》唤起的泥土气息到《Reno Silver》的洛杉矶山丘全景，再到《Heart》中弯曲音高的感性巫术，整张专辑以安静的克制感贯穿始终，让声音在轻柔的摇摆中自然生长。

items.body:
Two hours and 20 minutes of music split across three LPs, Sarah Davachi's latest studio album is a milestone for what's best described as deep minimalism, placing string, brass and woodwind ensemble works alongside chilling Renaissance-style choral pieces and heady solo organ compositions. Absolutely crucial material for engaged listeners - you know the deal.

Now Davachi's always been better than just good. Even back in 2016 when she released 'Vergers' and 'Dominions', there was something about her vision of minimalism that set her apart from a dense crowd of drone phonies. It's what made 2025's 'The Head as Form'd in the Crier's Choir' so effortlessly engaging; by this point known as one of the most skilled composers in her field, Davachi imagined an album of psychedelic chamber-prog that crowned her already impressive discography, using the Orpheus myth as a metaphor for her own experiences - not looking back but moving relentlessly forward. So it's even more remarkable that she's able to follow up with an album as different and as monumental as 'The Will of Tongues'. On the surface, it's business as usual for Davachi, an album of restrained, early music-informed long-form compositions that builds on the foundations laid out by some of her more demanding material, like 2023's epic 'Long Gradus'. But there's more going here on than you might expect; ignore the eye-watering duration if you can, 'The Will of Tongues' is a record that rewards patience and attentive listening. It's an album that's about the act of listening itself, in fact, putting the listener in control of their experience. If you tune out, relegating it to background music, it'll sail over you like cherry blossoms in the wind, but lock in and its beating rhythms, stirring harmonies and precise tonal variations will unlock a door of perception you may not have even realised was there.

Take the opening track, 'Interlude I: Polyphonic, for Strings', performed by The Sung Blood Players - Whitney Johnson and Eyvind Kang on viola and Lucy Railton on cello - it's a study that's meant to limber up our senses for what we're about to hear. If you're not paying close attention, it's nothing more than an eight-minute drone, but concentrate and you'll hear the three voices diverge and converge in the most unexpectedly beautiful ways, creating vibrating resonances and oddball rhythms in the process. And similarly, on 'Canto Duo' Davachi introduces us to one of five pipe organs that have been "tuned in historical temperaments". This isn't an aesthetic flex, expected to trigger buried memories of church services and historical movies, it's a chance for listeners to marvel at the instrument's range and its ability to create wind tones that can't be easily replicated on any other instrument. Davachi plays slowly and methodically, letting her long pauses between notes form a structure that's replicated in a more micro scale by the psychoacoustic components that might only reveal themselves on the third or fourth run-through. And when the piece ends and Davachi waves in the Chamber Choir Ireland for the first of three 'Songs of the Smile's Fig' parts, what should be a radical shift in mood sounds instead like synchronisation: those slow rhythmic changes, now sung by six voices in a Renaissance-era polyphonic style, suddenly make perfect sense.

And the first big payoff comes right after Davachi introduces Phaedrus, the Switzerland-based Renaissance flute consort who perform 'Interlude V: Harmonic, for Woodwinds'. On 'The Second Tuning', our appreciation of the finer elements is rewarded with one of Davachi's most moving, harmonically rich compositions to date, a faded organ work that imagines history as a circle rather than a straight line, reflecting its stacked-up eras in slowly building, densely textured harmonies that keep on revealing their stirring complexity until the last notes. And we need this if we're going to muster up the stamina to absorb 'The Rose Dialogues', a 45-minute string composition that's split into two equal parts, hinting oh-so-subtly at romantic music but always zeroing in on those mysterious resonances, the sounds that Davachi's taught herself how to reveal by so carefully using space, tone and texture. What's remarkable for a record that's so lengthy and so coherent thematically, is that Davachi keeps showing her range. Even the organ pieces are recorded and arranged to display just how different the instrument can sound: 'Four Narrow Forms', for example, is ghostly and whimsical compared with the dense, breathy hum of 'The First Tuning'. 

Even the third of Davachi's 'Songs of the Smile's Fig' chapters is remarkable different from its predecessors, surreal and only faintly historical compared with the first part, each word seemingly lapping over the next to create an effect that's shockingly hypnotic. We can't even tell you another record that's quite like this, there are traces of Arvo Pärt, Éliane Radigue, James Tenney and Alvin Lucier of course, but at this stage, Davachi has cooked those raw materials into her own unmistakable sound, a form of deep minimalism that's not exactly mystical - it's psychoactive.
items._genre: contemporary classical / minimalism / drone / chamber music
items._cn_summary: 莎拉·达瓦奇的新专辑以三分黑胶、长达两小时二十分钟的篇幅，延续她对深度极简主义的探索。专辑将弦乐、铜管与木管合奏作品并置，从中世纪风格的合唱段落到独立管风琴独奏，在结构上具有明显的仪式感与历史维度。她使用了五架以历史律制调音的管风琴，并非作为美学姿态，而是为了让听者感知到该乐器特有的音色共振与气息感，这些细节在其他乐器上难以复现。首曲由三位弦乐演奏者以多声部方式展开，缓慢的音像会在集中聆听时显现出不断分合的微妙节奏。整张专辑强调倾听行为本身——如果作为背景音乐，它会如风般掠过；但若投入注意力，则会逐渐展开其中蕴含的复调层次与声学现象。

HTRK slickly seduce with the unheimlich sensuality on 'Work (Work, Work)', on a new pressing for 2026.

While it may be gauche to attribute the lightless mood of this LP to the departure of Sean Stewart in 2010, it certainly lends some inescapable context. It's hardly like HTRK were doing tween-pop previously, but the sense of gloom and dystopia is almost suffocatingly closer to the edge, from the crawling-on-all-fours pacing, to the detached, androgynous vocals of Jonnine Standish and their perversely detailed production values.

They've got our attention instantly with the sideroom synth eurotica of 'Ice Eyes Eis', and sustain the mood beautifully into the pinging metallic delays and seeping reverb of 'Slo Go', sounding like Atelecine produced by a young Geoff Barrow after a Birthday Party binge. Dragging us further down into the abyss, on 'Eat Yr Heart' the drums become clammier while Jonnine's vocals drift like ghostly vapour trail. At the album's apex, 'Skinny', the beats feel like a dystrophied version of something from Mika Vainio's 'Life, It Eats You Up…' album, and 'Synthetik' serves a tangibly textured taste of steely Techno pulses and opiated post-punk guitar drifts into 'Poison'.

To close, the atmopshere weighs heavier still on 'Work That Body', tracing anaesthetic connections with their Melbourne forefathers, Pelican Daughters, before the bleak romance of 'Love Triangle' and the blank-eyed writhe of 'Body Double'.

For fans of occluded sonics from Pump to Atelecine or Mika Vainio, it's as good as it gets.

items._cn_summary: HTRK延续其阴郁暗潮美学，以极简节奏与残响密度的精妙调控营造出近乎窒息的末日氛围。专辑将缓慢爬行的节奏骨架、冰冷的合成器纹理与Standish中性化的幽灵般人声交织，形成去人格化的听觉景观。制作层面展现出对空间声学的敏锐把握：金属质感的延迟脉冲、淤泥般的鼓机、鸦片般的后朋克吉他漂移层层叠加，使每一轨都如同一场声学实验。整张作品在Melbourne系冷波传统基础上融入Atelecine式的遮蔽美学与Vainio式的techno脉冲，实现了暗潮、电子与后朋克的有机融合，2026年的再版让这张已被低估的经典重新进入视野。

items.body:
A holy spirit of lowercase musics imparts waking dream sensations ​on his gorgeous debut bow for mutual souls, Students of Decay - keenly advised to new ears and his legion admirers alike, and lovers of The Caretaker, Timo Van Lujik, Tom James Scott, Eno, Akira Rabelais...

‘Mystical Obscurant’ is Chalk’s umpteenth LP in a catalogue famously spanning decades - from mid ‘80s post-industrial scapes as Feral Confine to this type of pinch-yourself dream material, under his own name and part of Elodie or Mirror - and yet it’s just as vital to longtime disciples as it is to new ears seeking a way into his sprawling body of work. Aptly offered by SoD as “a rare opportunity to encounter the expansive character of that oeuvre in miniature”, his suite of powdered timbral glisten and harmonic perfume ideally portrays a sound-sensitive knack for evoking atmospheric nostalgia with the barest ingredients, all spun out at deeply rested heart rate that stealthily comes to calibrate with your own.  

Each of the seven pieces feel as though they appeared from air, rather than performed by any physical being. The softness of his brush-stroke guitar and liminality of electro-acoustic sorcery shortens the gap between imagination and materiality with signature concision, centring transcendence and bathing the senses in mirage-like vistas. In the shimmering stasis of ‘Against The Tide’ choral sirens pull the ear out from shore to a 12 min standout ‘Oratorio’ surely comparable with Eno pop ambient frissons, yet shrouded with a mystery closer to Akira Rabelais’ enigmatic processes.

That grasp of atmospheric intrigue & stuff also makes for utterly sublime, tongue-tip experience in ‘Divine Light’ and thru to the tousled, Caretaker-esque crackle of ‘Threads of a Dream’, into a beatific closer ‘Higher Love’, which, if his sandman magick does its job, should be scoring your descent into the pillow or states of pure bliss.

Really exquisite stuff.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Andrew Chalk以本名发表的最新作品，涵盖七首曲目，以极简的素材构建梦境般的氛围空间。弹拨吉他音色轻柔如笔触，电子原声手法模糊了想象与物质之间的距离，使每首曲子仿佛凭空浮现而非演奏所得。整张唱片以极低的心率节奏展开，缓慢校准听者的生理节律，在静谧中展开音色光泽与和声香气。'Against The Tide'以合唱般的人声泛音牵引耳朵离岸，十二分钟的'Oratorio'成为全碟焦点，兼具Eno流行氛围的质感与Akira Rabelais式的神秘感。'Divine Light'与'Threads of a Dream'延续氛围内省的肌理，后者带有The Caretaker式的老旧唱片噪音质地。终曲'Higher Love'以梦幻的音色收束，适合作为入睡前的聆听材料。

items.body:
Bursting at the seams with ideas and mushy emotionality, Cindy Lee's hypnagogic 2-hour magnum opus has quite rightly been touted as one of the best albums of the year - if not the decade. Ex-Women frontperson Patrick Flegel's vision of rock 'n roll is anachronistically nostalgic, an oily tincture of vintage psych, dilated funk and ghosted girl group pop that stews in its heartbreaking sincerity. Urgent listening for fans of Jessica Pratt, Brian Wilson, The Walker Brothers, U.S. Girls or Karen Carpenter.

It makes sense that Flegel launched their seventh Cindy Lee full-length on their web 1.0-style Geocities homepage earlier this year. The long-running web hosting service holds a special place in the hearts for people of a certain age - it's not so much what it was, exactly, but what it represented at a time when the implications of a digital future weren't yet clear. 'Diamond Jubilee' arrives at a time when nostalgia has been not just hyper-commodified, but weaponised; the concept of looking back to a time when life was easier, safer and simpler is intertwined with the acceleration of technological progress. Before we were made aware of the deluge of information that surrounded us, culture was very different - messages were easier to parse, and criticism, rightly or wrongly, was far more universally accepted. Flegel assaults us with content here - the album weighs in at 32 tracks - and although they repeatedly draw from the past, their yesteryear isn't fixed, or particularly physical. Their nostalgia is purposefully fantastical, a reverb-drenched collage of ideas that spans the long history of rock 'n roll and radio pop, and buried in amongst the tangled artifice is a strain of emotional earnestness that's refreshingly rare. 

None of this will be a huge surprise to anyone who's familiar with Flegel's prior Cindy Lee canon or their work with Women - one of the most quietly influential Canadian art rock bands of the '00s. But 'Diamond Jubilee', despite its length, focuses their gaze, subverting and twisting rock's litany of stereotypes until its impressionistic spatter of half-remembered aesthetics coagulates into an anxiously contemporary statement. There's the muddy echo of West African pop in the guitar phrasing that underpins the title track, before disco-era strings and boxy West Coast psych drums interrupt the mood abruptly; and it's Flegel's androgynous Brian Wilson-style cries that wring the passion out of the track. From bar to bar, the track morphs almost seamlessly, and Flegel anchors the chaos with their words. "What could I find, in a fantasy," they purr. "A burning memory, of something true." And it's not just genre that they cram into the meat grinder: on 'Baby Blue', the already lo-fi textures takes a hit when Flegel pushes the psych rock thuds into the red, transforming the kick drum into an empty pop that disappears into the fudgy, distorted guitars, and on the exotica-tinged 'Til Polarity's End', Flegel drowns the entire track in saturation so it sounds as if it's vibrating through a flooded abandoned factory.

It's an album that's craftily casual, as if you're supposed to assume it's been hastily cobbled together unless you decide to scratch at the wallpaper. There's a near-ambient quality to many of the tracks, that harnesses the same mixture of uneasy homesickness and reverie as the best vaporwave, but Flegel is consistently there to remind us that whatever it is we might be feeling, we're not isolated. "I'm only dreaming," they sing over near invisible bass twangs and kosmische arpeggios on 'Always Dreaming'. "Things aren't as awful as they're seeming." Even on the more formal pop moments - like 'Kingdom Come' or the heartbreaking 'If You Hear Me Crying' - Flegel's girl group swing is disrupted by their diaphanous reverb, peculiar tunings and odd rhythms. A chirpy, echoing beat patters over the former, while Flegel adds wonky strums and coarse, unexpected noises, singing "I could have sworn I heard you call my name, over the melodies of yesterday," as if pulling flesh from bone, and revealing the album's circulatory system.

It's an album that sticks in the throat, a set of broadly hypnogogic pop vignettes that embrace the expected cultural nihilism, but also grasping the passion that defined another era. "All I've got's this song," they cry on 'Don't Tell Me I'm Wrong'. "And your memory."

items._cn_summary: 《钻禧》是辛迪·李主脑帕特里克·弗莱格尔的长达两小时、32首曲目的长篇专辑，以低保真、催眠质感的拼贴方式重构复古流行记忆。他将迷幻摇滚、放克、女子组合流行、西非吉他泛音与迪斯科弦乐混入同一声道，段落间频繁切换，再用推到失真的鼓机和模糊吉他制造粗粝声响。弗莱格尔的假声/高音带有布莱恩·威尔逊式色彩，歌词在幻想与真实记忆之间摆动。专辑刻意回避技术时代被商品化的怀旧，转而用虚构的、混响浸透的旧日图景承载真挚情感。其形式松散却组织细密，在摇滚陈规中不断偏移，形成焦虑而当代的声音陈述。

items.body:
One of those releases that makes you feel like no other music exists for a hot minute, Dean Blunt returns with a second Black Metal album for Rough Trade, delving deeper into his unfathomable yet completely approachable and direct take on visceral x melancholic folk-pop. Spoiler: It’s really fucking good.

Aided on most of the songs here by Joanne Robertson’s vocal counterpoint and Giles Kwakeulati King-Ashong’s skittering drums, these songs once again connect to AR Kane’s distinct approach to the avant grade thru imperfection. In effect, it feels like Blunt manages to squeeze all the sterile sheen out of overly tasteful music, leaving a throbbing mass of flesh, blood vessels, nerve endings - exposed and beautiful. It’s what AR Kane called ‘Kaning’ (see Dhanveer Singh Brar’s excellent 'Beefy's Tune’ book for more on this) - and effectively provides a vital riposte to a world in which so much “art" is presented and consumed as a form of numbing.

And that riposte requires no explanation - a personal narative woven with little concession to anything - there’s not even a tracklisting or credits on the physical formats, instead Blunt’s ideas are wrapped up in a succession of first grade earworms, string sections here and there, billowing subs - all melancholy, blunt smoke and bliss. 

"Flaws are discontinuities that act as tiny fissures, allowing the dim and distant, diffused gem light of pre-creation to slip thru - it is this that music existed for - a signpost, a reminder, a note.” Rudy Tambala / A.R. Kane

Black Metal 2 is as real as it gets.

items.body:
Reworked from the original 'Sextet' session recordings by Bizarre Inc's Andrew Meecham (aka The Emperor Machine), 'The Joy of Sextet' celebrates the art-funk landmark's 45th anniversary without having to drudge up an extra disc of demos.

Anniversary reissues are just a part of life right now; pick a round number and you can guarantee some label or other is putting together a special remastered edition. And that's why 'The Joy of Sextet' is so novel - there's some elbow grease gone into it, with Meecham going back to the original recordings and putting his own spin on the entire record.

He's not completely off track, either; it's a suite of versions that's a little more dynamic than a simple remaster. Meecham adds "some new dynamics", imparting his contemporary engineering smarts on material that was recorded in Stockport way back in 1981. It's never sounded better: disco-inspired opener 'Lucinda' smacks and lurches, pumping very differently but giving plenty of space for Martha Tilson's casually affecting vocals, while the lengthy 'Knife Slits Water' has been fleshed out with watery textures and even more mind-bending FX. It's subtle, but it works.
items._genre: post-punk / art-funk / disco / electronic
items._cn_summary: 为庆祝《Sextet》专辑45周年，Andrew Meecham以The Emperor Machine的身份重新处理原始录音，并未选择常规的再版重制，而是对整张作品进行再创作。他在保留A Certain Ratio艺术放克特质的基础上，加入新的动态和当代混音技术，使开篇的《Lucinda》在迪斯科节拍中拥有更鲜明的冲击力与律动空间，同时保留了Martha Tilson松弛而富感染力的演唱。《Knife Slits Water》则被扩展出更丰富的水感纹理和更具迷幻色彩的声效处理。整体改动细致但不张扬，让这些1981年录制于斯托克波特的素材呈现出更鲜明的声音层次，兼具复古气质与现代工程感。

items.body:
Curated by Rosa Pistola, 'Dioses Tribales' surveys Mexico's tribal landscape, placing scene architects like Javier Estrada, Ricardo Reyna, DJ Mouse, DJ Tetris and Dj Morphius alongside beatmakers who are steering its current course, such as "TEKTRIBAL" innovator Freebot and Monterrey's Clap Freckles.

Pistola continues her "Tribal Sound System" project with this tight, tidy selection; rewind a few weeks and you'll remember 'Incorrigible', her latest album that built a sequence of rickety, hard-swung club tracks on the foundations of Mexico's tribal sound. 'Dioses Tribales' is a companion piece in a sense, providing a way for Pistola to pay her respects to the scene's pioneers and also highlight her contemporary peers - basically, it's an invaluable (and very digestible) line in to a movement that's far too often misunderstood outside of Mexico. The first vibrations were felt back in the early 2000s, when producers in Monterrey and Mexico City began to define their own sound as American house and techno flooded local clubs. Back then, you could wander round any city center and hear local bands playing indigenous music on pan flutes, shakers and traditional drums. And it was Ricardo Reyna, on 2005's 'Danza Azteca', who was the first artist to integrate these elements into his forward-thinking productions. This track's the reason it was labeled tribal prehispánico music in the first place, in fact.

Fittingly, Pistola opens the compilation with three of tribal's key artists. Reyna provides a sequel to his milestone, 'Danza Azteca II (El baile de los Dioses)', a track that shows the development that's happened in the last two decades, spicing up the central 4/4 kick with vocal chants, clattering rhythms and an urgent, driving bassline. And then Pistola puts the spotlight on tribal guarachero, the sound that emerged as artists began to fold in rhythms from Cumbia and other Afro-Cuban and Afro-Spanish dances. Manu Morales, aka DJ Mouse, is one of the most conspicuous early visionaries in this respect - his sunny 2005 breakout 'Folklore' is still one of the genre's touchstones. And he appears here with another nod to the Caribbean, muddling reggaetón's ubiquitous 'Dem Bow' rhythm, repurposed from Shabba Ranks' 1991 anthem, with EDM stabs and clanking pan drums. Oaxaca's DJ Tetris, meanwhile, was responsible for shaping tribal costeño, notoriously defining the sound on that epic 'N.A.A.F.I Tribal' compilation from 2014. His 'Rumbea Conmigo' is a collaboration with DJ Giovanni Rios that shows how, in the coastal south, tribal fused with Mariachi music, using synths to replace the accordions.

And it wouldn't be proper if there wasn't an appearance from Javier Estrada. Estrada didn't invent tribal prehispánico, but you could say he perfected it - just peep his 2014 album of the same name. And that's where Pistola pulls 'Guerrero Azteca' from. It's arguably one of the genre's affecting tracks, packed out with animalistic growls, deep, pounding rhythms and ASMR-ready rainforest sounds that seem to have directly inspired Pistola's own productions. And over on German netlabel KUMBALE a year later, Alfonso Luna released his own 'TRIBAL PREHISPANICO' treatise, referencing its potent cocktail of percussive dings and vocal snippets with the brilliant 'Bakalao'. The contemporary charge then is led by Pistola's production partner FREEBOT who displays how modern techniques have shaped his razor-sharp, Berghain-ready "TEKTRIBAL" sound on 'Ela toma (Dioses tribales)' and Clap Freckles, who made his name producing cheeky bootlegs and edits, and impresses with his hypnotic exclusive 'Los Dioses Tribales (Deja fluir)'.

We can't think of a better way to get acquainted with tribal's past, present and future - even the cover, showing the genre's notorious pointed boots, is iconic. You know what to do.
items._genre: tribal guarachero / tribal prehispánico / electronic / Latin fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由罗莎·皮斯托拉策划，是她“部落声音系统”计划的延续，也是其前作个人专辑的姊妹篇。选曲呈现墨西哥部落电子二十多年来的发展，既收入里卡多·雷纳、哈维尔·埃斯特拉达、莫斯、泰特里斯等场景早期代表人物，也收录了弗里波特、克拉普·弗莱克斯等正在改变方向的新生代制作人。雷纳2005年的作品最早将排箫、沙锤和传统鼓融入电子舞曲，开创了“前西班牙部落”这条线索；合辑中的续作和埃斯特拉达的选曲都带有更沉重的低音与密集的打击层次。莫斯的曲目把雷鬼顿节奏与合成器音色、钢鼓声响混合，泰特里斯则与另一位合作者用合成器替换手风琴，表现墨西哥沿海地区与马里阿奇音乐的融合。整张合辑以较短篇幅串联起原住民音乐、昆比亚、非裔古巴节奏与当代电子舞曲之间的脉络，是进入该场景的清晰入口。

items.body:
FELT capture deep & mysterious activities for posterity with a double bill from someone called bushes (no clues!) and scene veteran Klaus, recorded and mixed by Murray Collier (aka Dip Friso, Grim Lusk) in Glasgow, 2024. Trust there’s oodles of intrigue & stuff inside.

Always encouraging when music has no immediate frames of reference, RIYL’s or FFO’s, and this lot do it very fucking well, operating at a sort of eyes-at-half-mast tempo and headspace that’s neither ambient nor primed for the club, like some kinda holding music between modes of existence (we didn’t say liminal lol), full of dank atmosphere and the promise of whatever the night has in store. 

If the A side gives a whiff of isolation, the flip is all dusk and romance, snatches of saxophone drifting off in the distance with bass pulses and endless delay sending us to an unintelligible, beautiful place.

One of those tapes we guarantee you’ll rinse endlessly, we’ve had it on a loop for a couple of hours and trust it casts a fucking spell.
items._genre: ambient / experimental / electronic / jazz
items._cn_summary: 这张现场录音由Murray Collier录制混音，收录Bushes与Klaus在格拉斯哥的双人现场。音乐处于半合眼的速度与心绪中，既非氛围也非舞池，更像存在状态之间的过渡音乐。A面弥漫孤立感，B面则充满黄昏与浪漫，远处飘来萨克斯片段，贝斯脉冲与无尽延迟将听者带入难以言明的美丽境地。作品没有现成的参照系，充满幽暗氛围与夜晚的未知承诺，具有持续循环聆听的吸引力。

items.body:
Layered guitars, synths and wordless vocals set the scene on the introspective solo debut by Lynn Wright.

"Wright, who has mostly eschewed developing a fixed artistic identity throughout his already long career, has preferred to remain on the periphery of collaborative projects and behind the scenes. It took until recent times for him to make “Before The Sinking Plains”, which arrives as his first solo recording after decades of traversing underground scenes in New York and beyond. Wright defines the album as “a collection of atmospheric compositions structured as songs or songs masking as atmospheric compositions.”

The album began during a long neurological illness as guitar loops Wright would make each morning in his apartment and let play quietly in the background. At some point he began recording the ones he liked and adding layers of treated guitars, vocals, and synths, and then, eventually, giving them defined structures. The album features none of the aggression of his louder bands and improvisatory projects, but retains the dark hues.

Before The Sinking Plains lives on the familiar peripheries of our post-everything sound world, with elements of everything from washed-out dream pop and atmospheric drone works to sparse noir folk and minimalist vocal composition moving within the linings of Wright's subtle yet grand pieces, creating a perfect backdrop for watching the sky merge with the vast open fields.

Since relocating to Berlin some years ago from New York, he has worked closely with composer Simon Goff, who mixed his current album, as an editor, engineer and composer on various film and recording projects. He also plays lap steel guitar in Swans bassist Dana Schechter’s band Insect Ark. This is just the top of the iceberg when it comes to Wright's collaborations and projects throughout the years."
items._genre: atmospheric / drone / dream pop / experimental / minimalism
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Lynn Wright的首张个人录音室作品，源自他在长期神经疾病期间每天早晨制作的吉他循环，后逐渐加入处理过的吉他、合成器与人声，最终赋予其明确结构。作品回避了他参与过的喧闹乐队项目中的攻击性，保留暗色基调，在氛围化作曲与歌曲形式之间游走。乐评指出，其中融合了褪色梦幻流行、氛围无人机、稀疏黑色民谣与极简人声作曲等元素，形成一种介于天空与开阔原野之间的细腻而宏大的背景。专辑由柏林的Simon Goff混音，制作背景与个人经历也为作品增添了独特气质。

items.body:
I can feel the waves is Frances Chang's debut on RVNG Intl.

"A boundary-pushing musician and multi-media artist from Brooklyn, New York, Frances Chang disrupts accepted reality through her unique and enchanting compositions. Chang’s songs are an exercise in communication, probing the tension between idiosyncratic personal experience and the drive to understand, and be understood, through a collective language.

For “I can feel the waves,” a piano-centric melody is ornamented with primitive electronics and poetic vocals. The track boldly demonstrates Chang’s strength for unconventional yet contagious songwriting, and pioneers a genre the artist refers to as “slacker prog”: roomy and playful, offbeat and occasionally jarring, brimming with spiritual and emotional resonance.

The b-side, “Marry,” is a rollicking yet laid-back composition, with undaunted wobbly kicks bubbling under pianistic textures until a dialogue, acted out between Chang and Sylvia Gorelick, takes the foreground in the final moments of the track. As the instrumental carries its freewheeling pulse forward, the conversation, inspired by films like Kenneth Lonergan’s Margaret and Catherine Breillat’s Fat Girl!, along with Broken Social Scene’s “Anthems for a Seventeen-Year Old Girl,” turns toward the relationship between internal subjectivity and the external necessity of “staying small.”

Where is Frances headed from here? A piano is at the center, synths and strings swelling around its shoulders. A little less tension, a lot more production. Some shadows will be encountered, some forgotten skeletons unearthed. Music excavated from the subtler, deeper layers of cerebral and shared experiences. Music that is truly its own."
items._genre: slacker prog / experimental / avant-garde / electronic / art pop
items._cn_summary: 本作是Frances Chang在RVNG Intl.的首支发行，以钢琴为核心的旋律缠绕原始电子音色与诗性人声。A面《I can feel the waves》体现她所称的“懒散前卫摇滚”：空间宽阔、俏皮、节拍错位且偶尔突兀，同时承载精神与情感共鸣。B面《Marry》在摇摆的低频与钢琴织体之上推进，结尾处与Sylvia Gorelick的对话成为焦点，灵感来自电影及Broken Social Scene的歌曲，探讨主观内在与“保持渺小”的外部要求之间的张力。整体制作较以往更丰满，合成器与弦乐在钢琴周围扩展，作品从深层经验与共享记忆的缝隙中被挖掘出来。

First time Vinyl reissue of Frank Bretschneider’s turn of the century productions as Komet, originally released via 12k in the year 2000 and offering a blueprint of sorts for the bass-pulse minimalism that would come to dominate the Raster Noton label Bretschneider founded with Carsten Nicolai four years earlier. "Built from clean sine tones and a deliberately sparse sound palette, it contrasts minimalist electronics with playful polymetric rhythms, creating a precise yet engaging take on early glitch and experimental electronic music."

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Frank Bretschneider以Komet名义于2000年在12k发行的作品，此次为首次黑胶再版。它以纯净正弦音和刻意精简的声音材料为基础，将极简电子与富有游戏性的复节奏交织，呈现出精确而具动感的早期glitch与实验电子面貌。作品被视为bass-pulse极简主义的蓝图之一，预示了Bretschneider与Carsten Nicolai共创的Raster Noton厂牌后来主导的美学方向。其极度克制的音色配置令它跨越时代，至今听来仍不显过时。

Jubilant art-funk about cocaine addiction—absolutely. Swooning orchestral pop about Jerry Garcia—why not? items.body:
Asher White releases latest album "Love Aggregates" via Joyful Noise Recordings.

"For any other artist, an album like Asher White’s Love Aggregates might come out of a conscious push to treat no idea as off-limits, to make something bold and new. Jubilant art-funk about cocaine addiction—absolutely. Swooning orchestral pop about Jerry Garcia—why not? Rippling electronic noise, jazzy brushed drums, an elderly motorcyclist with dementia, a profoundly emotional bass solo—put them all in one song. There are threadbare folk tunes, glammed-up power-pop bangers, “Sir Duke” horn charts, Morton Feldman string arrangements, layers of guitar feedback like violins made of liquid chrome. Yes, for another artist, Love Aggregates might be the most adventurous album in their catalog. For Asher White, it’s what passes for settling down.

White is 25 years old and has been making records—writing, recording, producing, and playing almost everything herself—for over a decade. She’d released two dozen of them on Bandcamp before catching the indie-rock industry’s attention with 2024’s Home Constellation Study and last year’s 8 Tips for Full Catastrophe Living. The latter album’s dizzy eclecticism and formidable craft landed her on Rolling Stone’s Future 25 list with the likes of xaviersobased and Oklou, along with a slew of other accolades. That came as something of a surprise to White, who didn’t craft the chaotic 8 Tips with a breakthrough in mind. Love Aggregates feels like a chance, for one of the most thrilling musical talents of her generation, at a more deliberate introduction.

She wrote and recorded her new album while her previous one was gathering momentum, tinkering in the DIY recording studio where she always works, acutely conscious now that people would be listening to whatever she came up with. At around the same time, her years-long romantic relationship ended in a flurry of betrayal and addiction, her first experience of devastating heartbreak. Even so, Love Aggregates is not a bitter album about wallowing or seething, but instead making use of those impulses as raw materials in work that transcends the specificity of its origins, fashioning them into something surprising and new."
items._genre: experimental pop / art-funk / electronic / avant-garde / orchestral
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以高度杂食的创作方式，将成瘾、失恋与老年摩托车手的记忆错乱等素材揉入音乐，既有关于可卡因成瘾的欢快艺术放克，也有致敬Jerry Garcia的管弦流行，甚至在同一首歌里并置电子噪音、爵士鼓刷、深情贝斯独奏。原声民谣、华丽摇滚、铜管号段、Morton Feldman式弦乐与液态铬般的吉他反馈层层叠加。作者长期DIY制作，在分手与背叛的情绪中不以宣泄为导向，而是将痛苦作为材料转化为超越源头的创作，适合对拼贴式、高密度声音冒险感兴趣的人。

items.body:
Demdike Stare’s DDS label kicks off a new series of limited edition 12”s with the return of Shinichi Atobe, offering a slow evolution of his inimitable deep house, finely balanced with a new found sub-heavy bias while unlocking extra space in the upper registers.

Atobe’s third 12” since debuting on Chain Reaction in 2001 marks a subtle but crucial development of his style, leaning towards classically deep, dub house templates, assisted by additional editing and mixing from Miles ov Demdike Stare. On both sides he adds supple flesh and hypnotic emotive pathos to his stripped formula, resulting in some of the most immediate and enduring work in his canon thus far. It coincidentally also marks a decade since he first graced DDS with his debut album ‘Butterfly Effect’, followed by a tranche of cultishly acclaimed albums in the years since.

On the A-side pearl ‘Ongaku 1’ he steps out with a shimmering take on the effortless gait of M-Series blueprints, as derived from the deepest NYC house, delicately ornamented with cascading levels of detail. Precision-tooled kicks precipitate Prescription-via-Maurizio feathered dub chords, interlaced with a frisson of darker strings and synth melodies for the full goosebump. ‘Dub 6(six)’ on the flip whisks up a psychedelic lattice of arps and synth voices with ruder bass ballast, taking its sweet time before the kicks come to swing the ‘floor deep and wide. 

Straight bullets, no messing.
items._genre: deep house / dub house / electronic
items._cn_summary: Shinichi Atobe在DDS厂牌的新系列12英寸黑胶中回归，延续其标志性深浩室风格，同时向经典dub house模板倾斜，并新增了更重的低音倾向与更开阔的高频空间。A面曲目在精密底鼓与羽毛般飘浮的dub和弦间编织出层层细节，暗色弦乐与合成旋律增添情绪张力；B面则以迷幻的琶音和合成音色配合粗粝低音底座，节奏缓慢铺陈后才引动舞池律动。乐评认为这是其作品谱系中最直接且耐听的篇章之一，展现了他在极简框架内注入具象质感与催眠性情感表达的能力，是深浩室脉络中具有辨识度的一次推进。

items.body:
St Circul's debut album "Ley Lines" via Archaic Vaults.

"Concise collection of folkloric grime instrumentals to rise from a new moniker taken on by the elusive First Circle. A breadcrumb trail of effortlessly crafted early 2000s-era grime, trap and drill instrumentals can be found on a fairly sparse Soundcloud account and numerous NTS shows spanning the last ten years, on which he is known to play almost entirely his own material. Now a different energy takes hold on »Ley Lines«: ten tracks by the enigmatic producer to be released both on a label and in physical format for the first time.

»Ley Lines« was born from a meandering quest through South London’s more leafy dwellings. These cherished regions became a place of refuge in which to ruminate on the hopes that love and community can outlast the dwindling state of Britain’s social and political climate. Photo documentation was made which would later form the genesis for each track, and a return to the studio resulted in something which could not be fitted into the existing First Circle discography.

Harpsichord and brass samples (»A Plan Is Formed«, »Hilly Fields«) are underpinned by murky bass loops and tight militaristic percussion – motifs recognisable amongst white label grime’s most influential producers (Wiley, Skepta, Lewi White etc.) that push the formula into far more rapturous territories than any of FC’s previous productions. The more introspective moments of the album (»Wares at the Ivy House«, »Blythe Vision«) put local field recordings and devotional reverberant ambience to the forefront, alluding to St Circul’s proto-dungeon synth influences and giving the whole album a unique world all its own.

Archaic Vaults is proud to host an album which shares intrinsic roots with the label’s own South London birthplace. »Ley Lines«’ ten tracks of psychogeographic drifting are available in digital and limited cassette format via Archaic Vaults.

Mastered by Owen Pratt Design by Severin Black Artwork image by St Circul"

items._cn_summary: 本专辑是神秘制作人以新化名发布的处女作，源自他在南伦敦绿意地带的漫游与影像记录。十首曲目将古键琴与铜管采样置于低沉贝斯和紧凑打击乐之上，同时穿插田野录音与残响氛围，在早期英国街头舞曲的骨架中融入类似前地下城合成器的内省气质。该作延续了白标时代的制作脉络，但通过照片转译和地域感知拓展了声响边界，使粗粝的节拍与教堂般的混响交织，营造出兼具军事化律动和幽灵般旋律的心理地理学世界。由独立厂牌以数字和限量磁带形式发行，制作与视觉设计均保持统一的美学调性。

items.body:
Last spotted on A Good Year's 'Play', Texas-born singer, producer and multi-instrumentalist Riya Mahesh, aka Quiet Light, turns in the sequel to 2023's 'Blue Angel Sparkling Silver', mashing Imogen Heap's experimentation with The Postal Service's emo-friendly electro-pop.

There's a polish to 'Blue Angel Sparkling Silver 2', but Mahesh's production smarts don't ever overwhelm the music's emotional core. And although she plays fast and loose with the vocal effects, chopping, processing and layering her voice in much the same way Heap did when she inadvertently kickstarted cloud rap, it's still possibly to sense the human in the machine. It's a technique that's helped Mahesh get noticed recently; she appeared alongside Late Verlane on A Good Year's sublime album opener 'Dealerz' and the new mixtape sees her move to True Panther, labelmates with artists who share the same DNA: Glasser, Oklou and Lauren Auder, for example.

On 'Berlin', that seems as if it would be self-explanatory, she avoids the temptation to drape her song in techno finery, instead telling her story of over-indulgence with restraint, singing almost unaccompanied until her sparse drones are met by a simple breakbeat. Her voice is left to do the heavy lifting and it's up for the job; Mahesh is a gifted producer, sure, but as a singer she's able to really show her range, comfortably belting out power pop or existing in a more ambient space, like on 'New Dream'. She's even able to bridge the gap between electro pop and Surf Gang-style Soundcloud rap on 'Postinternetfame' - and the breathy 'New Girls' sounds like it was at least partially inspired by Burial. Nae bad at all.
items._genre: electro-pop / art pop / ambient / experimental electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张续作延续了德州音乐人兼具制作人与歌手身份的创作路径，在情绪化电子流行中融入英伦实验流行式的人声切片、叠层与处理，机械感之下仍保留人情温度。节拍整体克制，如《柏林》以稀疏长音与简约碎拍衬托人声，展示从有力流行到氛围空间的音域；同时将电子流行与网络说唱气质接合，部分曲目带有人声的气声质感与呼吸感。制作精巧但不遮蔽情感核心，适合关注当代电子流行与实验人声处理的听众。

items.body:
Erykah Badu teases her first album in 16 years with a collaboration with superproducer 'The Alchemist' that's as vital as anything on her 'New Amerykah' records - and far more psychoactive.

Badu just doesn't do things by half. She waits until we're ready and somehow always has the perfect sound for the moment - just think about the impact of 'Baduizm' in 1997, or the fanged 'New Amerykah: Part One (4th World War)', released on the cusp of the Obama era. 'Witch Doctor' is a lucid reflection on the media's stranglehold that Badu coaxes into a lilting, soulful coo at first, harking back to her Motown era with The Alchemist's cool-headed, jazzy keys and blunted beats. 

But there's something just beneath the surface; when the boom-bap smack fades to silence, Badu's doubletime syncopated rhythm emerges that had been driving the track all along. Badu lets it run out, dubbing out voices and loose percussive elements to enhance the syrupy, ritualistic qualities until that's the core focus of the track. Remarkable stuff, really - bring on the album.
items._genre: neo-soul / hip-hop / jazz / dub
items._cn_summary: 这是Erykah Badu与制作人The Alchemist合作的新作，也是她十六年来首张专辑的先行预告。作品最初以轻柔的灵魂乐唱腔呈现，配合Alchemist冷静的爵士钢琴与钝重节拍，带有Motown时代的复古质感；但随着嘻哈节拍逐渐消退，隐藏的双倍速切分节奏浮现，成为驱动整首作品的核心。Badu随后将人声和松散打击乐元素进行dub式处理，强化了迷幻而仪式化的氛围，使歌曲从表面舒缓的叙事转向更深层的心理暗示。乐评指出，这首作品以清醒的眼光审视媒体对意识的控制，却用催眠般的声音结构让人沉浸其中，其强度与个人色彩不亚于她此前《New Amerykah》系列中的代表作。相比之前的专辑，这次的声响更加具有致幻性，显示出Badu在节奏与声场编排上的持续探索，也让人们对完整专辑的走向充满期待。

items.body:
Hakushi Hasegawa’s Honest Feeling Album is the Tokyo-based composer, producer and multi-instrumentalist’s second full-length release for Brainfeeder.

"Working with HaHa & The Hairpins as a backing band, Hasegawa brings greater scale and momentum to their restless blend of jazz, pop, J-rock and electronic experimentation.

Featuring collaborations with tofubeats, Lang Lee, Tsukino Mito and Accorinrin of Otoboke Beaver, the album moves between intricate arrangements, melodic songwriting and sudden shifts in pace. Lead track ‘The Owner of Sweetness’ sets the tone: a sweeping ballad where virtuosic playing and detailed production meet head-on.

For fans of Iglooghost, A. G. Cook, Yaeji, Underscores and Louis Cole."

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是东京作曲家、制作人与多乐器演奏家长谷川白纸的第二张全长作品，由伴奏乐队扩大了编曲规模与推进力。音乐在爵士、流行、日本摇滚与电子实验之间快速切换，细密编排与旋律写作并存，并频繁出现节奏和情绪上的突转。多位合作者的参与带来不同演唱与声响层次；主打曲《甜蜜之主》以抒情歌谣铺展，演奏技法与后期制作形成直接碰撞。整体在复杂结构与可听性之间取得平衡，延续了实验电子与跨界融合的路线。

items.body:
Jospehine Foster's 2016 release "No More Lamps In the Morning" available again via Fire Records.

"Foster, on nylon string guitar, and husband Victor Herrero, accompanying on Portuguese guitar, together weave intimate readings of songs spanning Foster's songwriting career including selections from recent albums "This Coming Gladness" (2008) and "I'm a Dreamer" (2013) and back to Born Heller (2004). Foster's new route is a free, chromatic music, a tuneful montana of mind--an expansive harmonic space dominated by Rif mountain on the horizon. As highwater as the music is, as broad the stylistic palette of the musicians, the music really exists in service of the lyrics. Two of the songs on No More Lamps are poems by Rudyard Kipling and James Joyce given musical settings by Foster. The rest arguably are musical settings of her own poems strengthened in a fiery crucible of guitars (and on 2 tracks Gyða Valtýsdóttir's cello) in which dissonant notes bend and quaver as wirefork embers, dying without affecting the glowing tonal fire which unites contrary forces in a Moroccan speakeasy. She and Herrero have performed, for an audience of burros, concerts of Federico Garcia Lorca poems set to music. A music of wandering and a music of roots."
items._genre: experimental folk / avant-garde / world fusion / free improvisation
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Josephine Foster与丈夫Victor Herrero以尼龙弦吉他和葡萄牙吉他为核心的双人二重奏，重新演绎了Foster自2004年以来的创作历程。音乐呈现出自由而半音化的特质，和声空间开阔，不和谐音像余烬般弯曲颤动，却始终围绕着一个炽热的调性核心，将相异力量统一于摩洛哥地下酒吧般的私密氛围中。歌词占据主导地位，其中两首直接采用吉卜林和乔伊斯的诗歌谱曲，其余则基于她自己的诗作，使得整张作品带有浓厚的文学气质。两首曲目加入大提琴，进一步丰富了声响层次。整体在漫游感与根源感之间取得平衡，既疏离又亲密，展现了实验性声乐与传统乐器结合的可能性。

Necessary reissue of Marc Leclair’s immaculate Y2K micro-house/dub-house 12” as Akufen, dispensed by Low End Activist’s guess-again BRUK sibling to Sneaker Social Club - huge RIYL Maurizio, Studio 1, Mike Huckaby.

‘Architextures 1 -2 -3’ is a sought-after slice of hypnotic house by a noted pioneer of the micro-house movement that emerged in the late ‘90s. Its reissue arrives in the wake of a re-up for Marc Leclair’s (aka Akufen) sole solo album ‘Musique Pour 3 Femmes Enceintes’ (2005) with a strong reminder of his pivotal role in dressing house music down to fundamentals around the millennium, as deployed in Richie Hawtin mixes and praised for its exquisitely efficient, effortless, hiccuping funk.

It’s really all about the  A-side’s ‘Architexture 1’, a pendulous 127BPM roller inflected with chef’s kiss dub chords and frisky drums, on one of the smoothest, deepest basslines since ‘M5’. There’s a good reason why it’s been fetching triple figures on 2nd hand markets, so BRUK are doing the Lord’s work with this reissue, which also includes the slower, sub-heavier swivel of its Pt. 2, and more signature, strutting clip of his tight sampling tekkerz on Pt. 3.

TIP!

items._cn_summary: 这张12寸以再版形式呈现这位加拿大制作人在千禧年前后的三部曲作品。A面曲以每分钟约127拍的稳定节拍为基底，叠加带混响延迟的迷幻和弦、细碎弹跳的鼓组和深沉顺滑的低音线，在极简框架内形成持续催眠感；第二首转向更慢、低频更重的摇摆节拍；第三首则突出标志性的密集采样剪贴手法，用大量细小声音碎片构筑律动。乐评强调其将电子舞曲剥离至基本元素后的高效与轻盈感，也解释了它成为二手市场高价追捧对象的原因。此次由独立厂牌再版，补上了这位制作人相关作品流通上的缺口。

items.body:
A sought-after Dub Techno classic originally released on Berlin’s legendary Chain reaction in 2001, remastered from vinyl for this edition in 2015 by Matt Colton.

A massive personal favourite of Demdike Stare's, Shinichi Atobe's 'Ship Scope' was Chain Reaction's penultimate release in 2001 and, with the benefit of hindsight, also one of the label's most sublime offerings. Phase fwd to 2015 and DDS rightly put it back into circulation with this necessary reissue arriving in the wake of Atobe's much loved archival salvage, 'Butterfly Effect', which caused quite a ripple in late 2014.

Notable not only for its unusually dreamier tone - especially when compared with the rest of the CR#'s - but also for its happily lost-at-sea feel, connoting a deeply romantic and almost shoegazy late '90s / into-the-'00s deep techno aesthetic that would essentially become washed away with the advent and normalisation of mnml techno's pristine production values.

Quite simply, it's a must-have for followers of the romantic streak in Ross 154, Convextion and classic Chain Reaction - do not miss!
items._genre: dub techno / deep techno / shoegaze / ambient techno
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是日本制作人Shinichi Atobe于2001年在柏林Chain Reaction厂牌发表的经典作品，2015年由Demdike Stare主理的DDS厂牌重新发行。相较于同期Chain Reaction的其他出品，它呈现出更梦幻、朦胧的听觉质地，带有一种迷失于海上的浪漫漂泊感。音乐在深沉的Dub Techno节拍中融入近似Shoegaze的吉他噪感与Ambient氛围，营造出世纪末至千禧年初深沈而抒情的Techno美学，与后来精致化的Minimal Techno形成鲜明对照。作为该厂牌倒数第二张发行，它被视为厂牌史上最动人的篇章之一，也是连接Dub Techno与氛围电子脉络的重要作品。

items.body:
Patricia Wolf's second Balmat album is the soundtrack to experimental filmmaker Edward Pack Davee's feature-length documentary 'Hrafnamynd', and mixes field recordings with AFX-esque lullaby themes, tape-mangled instrumental vamps and VHS-burn'd analog pads.

There's something oddly soothing about 'Hrafnamynd', and without seeing the documentary it's hard to know exactly why. Using film and digital, Davee recounts his childhood in Iceland through the volcanic island's ravens, exploring the landscape and folklore while scraping his own nostalgia. And Wolf's score attempts to mimic the surreal fusion of old and new by using her UDO Super 6, a powerful binaural analog-hybrid synth, to bring the past towards the present. "It has the ability to sound very modern," Wolf explains. "But can also sound so warm and fuzzy, like a synth from the 1970s." 

So we're treated to time-warped tracks like 'Early Memories', 'I Thought I Could Fly' and 'Hrafnaﬂing', the latter of which sounds as if it's an off-cut from Leila's 'Like Weather', and distressed, casual jams like 'Krummi's Theme' - the cue for the film's talking raven. But these are bounced against more self-consciously contemporary compositions; the glassy 'Huginn and Muninn', for example, or the balletic 'Surfing on Wind'. And the album's most generous track 'Echoes Through Time' reflects Wolf's full spectrum, distorting harmonies that settle into percussive sine chimes before disappearing into the distance.

items._cn_summary: 帕特里夏·沃尔夫在电子/实验厂牌下面向实验纪录片的第二张配乐专辑，影片透过冰岛渡鸦串联童年记忆、地貌与民间传说。配乐使用模拟混合合成器，让旧日声响与当代质感相互渗透：田野录音、类似实验电子风格的摇篮曲主题、被磁带损伤的器乐循环，以及录像带灼烧般的模拟铺垫交错出现。部分曲目带有碎拍与松动即兴的意味，另一些则是清透的现代主义铺陈；压轴长曲从扭曲和声沉入打击式正弦钟声，再向远处消散。整体氛围柔和却不安定，在环境与电子、配乐与独立作品之间保持张力。

items.body:
The Original Motion Picture Soundtrack for Crime 101 by experimental electronic musician, producer and composer Blanck Mass (She Rides Shotgun).

"Thunderous synth soundscapes are paired with nuanced character-driven themes creating a multi-faceted backdrop to the intense thriller. The Amazon MGM Studios film directed by Bart Layton is set against the sun-bleached grit of Los Angeles.

Crime 101 weaves the tale of an elusive jewel thief (Chris Hemsworth) whose string of heists along the 101 freeway have mystified police. When he eyes the score of a lifetime, his path crosses that of a disillusioned insurance broker (Halle Berry) who is facing her own crossroads. Convinced he has found a pattern, a relentless detective (Mark Ruffalo) is closing in, raising the stakes even higher. As the heist approaches, the line between hunter and hunted begins to blur, and all three are faced with life-defining choices– and the realization that there can be no turning back.

On creating the music, Power says :

“Crime 101 was an incredible movie to have the opportunity to score. At the centre of the story is, of course, the heist. However, it very quickly became apparent to me that this was not any heist movie, but more a Noir which happens to have a heist in it. The central characters and how their lives become intertwined was more important than the action, in a way. This is high-octane in parts, of course, but what really drew me to this movie was the character development. Lou, Davis and Sharon are the beating heart. I wanted to ‘be with them sonically’ throughout. Both the tender and the furious needed to be sympathetic with one another”."
items._genre: experimental electronic / synth-based / film score / dark ambient
items._cn_summary: Blanck Mass 为电影《Crime 101》创作的原声带，以轰鸣的合成器音景搭配角色驱动的细腻主题，构建出层次丰富的黑色电影氛围。配乐围绕宝石窃贼、保险经纪人和刑警三条人物线展开，将高能段落与情感内省交织在一起。作曲家表示，故事的核心并非动作场面，而是人物命运的彼此缠绕，因此他希望以声音伴随角色全程，让温柔与狂暴相互共鸣。这张原声带在延续 Blanck Mass 标志性实验电子声响的同时，也体现了配乐服务于叙事与心理刻画的面向。

items.body:
Techgnostic pied piper of Latin club, Tra Tra Trax co-founder Verraco hustles a class handful of techno, electro and hard groove bustlers for German compilation series The Third Room.

The Colombian producer-DJ takes The Third Room’s brief, to create a “place where different cultures existing and correlating to each other, mix and transform into hybrids” his own way, after precedents laid by Oscar Mulero, Freddy K, and GiGi FM, among others.

An exclusive ’Stone Version’ of Substance & Vainqueur’s 2007 dub techno ace ‘Libration’ opens a set spanning Skee Mask’s frisky deep techno swanger ‘Clear Sky 909’, thru the shearing sound design of Verraco’s own ‘Untitled (Teamgeist Mix)’, to the polyrhythmic hard groove charge of LA’s 1morning, and compatible tackle of ‘PatumPa’ by Monterrey, Mexico’s Regal86.

items.body:
Composer-producer-musician-DJ Floating Points, aka Sam Shepherd's "Mere Mortals", his first full-length ballet score.
"Commissioned and directed by the San Francisco Ballet’s Artistic Director Tamara Rojo, with choreography by Aszure Barton and design and visuals by Hamill Industries, the ballet reimagines the story of Pandora in a fusion of myth, music and movement. Recorded with the San Francisco Ballet Orchestra for Deutsche Grammophon, the 14-track album is a potent mix of elegiac strings, apocalyptic brass and pulsing electronics. From the lyrical solo violin of Hope to the dissonance and pummelling percussion of Rage of the Gods, and the exquisite harp melody of Her Gift before the eeriness of Opening of the Jar, the score is rich in texture and effect. Orchestral music emerges from an electronic haze, mirroring the ballet’s central question: where does the human end and the machine begin?"

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Floating Points的首部全长芭蕾配乐，由旧金山芭蕾舞团委约，以当代视角重构潘多拉神话。音乐以管弦乐队为基底，叠加脉动电子音色与实验性声响设计，在抒情弦乐、激烈打击乐与恢弘铜管之间切换，并融入氛围化的电子织体，使古典编制与现代电声彼此渗透。作品注重音色层次与戏剧张力，独奏小提琴、竖琴段落与不和谐段落形成鲜明对比，整体呈现出兼具叙事性与抽象感的音响空间，回应了人性与机器界限的命题。对于关注当代古典与电子融合的听众，这是一部值得深入聆听的跨界作品。

items.body:
Revisiting their debut album '.After', Tujiko Noriko and Adrian Corker commission a suite of remixes, bringing in Koshiro Hino ov YPY, goat (JP) and KAKUHAN fame, Tashi Wada, DJ Trystero, Shojiro Nakaoka and DJ ojo to put their spin on the source material.

The original album only took Noriko and Corker a couple of days in the studio, but they wired the results to percussionist and arranger George Barton, who took it to the next level. They continue the thought on '.After Again', dishing out the stems to a carefully pruned list of collaborators - artists whose distinctive sounds only extend the original album's sonic universe. And of course it's the YPY version of the album's opening track 'Yasashii Sayonora' that'll have most of y'all chomping at the bit; Hino turns Corker and Noriko's source material to dust, time-stretching Noriko's vocal and zeroing in on the stuttering percussion and rusted turntable loops. Adding his signature jerks, he fills the track with clattering metallic clangs, twisting the voices into downsampled groans from a neighboring cyber-reality.

Tokyo's DJ Trystero opts for a different but similarly unique approach on his two reworks, the "All Frills" remix of 'Toku No Minato' and his "Naive Declension" version of the same track. On the former, he isolates almost indistinguishable elements of the original, setting the ghost traces to a typically deep, dubby groove and on the latter, creates a rugged, gear-heavy jam from the remains. It's actually Nakaoka who provides the weirdest - yet strangely most recognisable - versions, using his custom generative code to match Noriko's voice with whirring interference and warbling digital detritus.
items._genre: experimental electronic / glitch / dub / avant-garde
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Tujiko Noriko与Adrian Corker对首张专辑《.After》的remix延伸，邀请Koshiro Hino、Tashi Wada、DJ Trystero等实验音乐人，将原始素材拆解为可重塑的声源。Hino的版本将人声时间拉伸、节拍碎化，叠加金属碰撞声与降采样低语，营造出邻近赛博现实的扭曲感；DJ Trystero则分别以低音节拍与重型机械律动呈现同一曲目的两种面向；Nakaoka运用自写生成代码，将人声与电流干扰、数字残渣交织。整张remix专辑并非简单的风格复刻，而是每位艺术家以独特手法拓展原作的声音宇宙，在实验电子、故障噪音与dub空间感之间游走，保留日式细腻的同时注入强烈的先锋质感。

items.body:
The Sultans of Sludge slang a definitive label debut for Sub Pop, bringing their singular sound to roost on a legendary label local to their origins in the US north west, whose rugged landscapes fed directly into the LP’s formidably primal concentration of dualistic energies

Hailing some 30 years since Sunn O)))’s formation, their eponymous 10th studio album reckons with forces of nature - time and space, dark and light - for 80 minutes of air-shuddering pressure limning epic, craggy vistas from a thick haar of distortion. Subtly enlivened with field recordings made in forests near Bear Creek Studios, Woodinville, Washington, where O’Malley says they would “go hiking and be out in the woods, spend time outdoors”, the resulting six-part sequence sees the duo drill down to fundamentals with an absorbing sense of purpose and telepathically-attuned intuition. A notable dearth of other contributors also means it’s one of their truest statements as a duo; just Stephen O’Malley & Greg Anderson howling into the wilds on all instrumentation, from trusted axes to keys and electro-acoustic sorcery. 

At this point, not to labour the arboreal metaphors, but it may take a certified guide to see the wood for the trees in Sunn O))) lands, such is the uniquely coherent sprawl of their sound at 30 years up to the hilt in atonal rock doom. Our hair’s not long enough to lay claim as spirit guides, but after 23 years of bearing witness to them live, and ingesting most of their LPs, we can say this side is wholly emblematic of their radical steez. Between the two 18 minute totems of a ‘XXANN’ laced with location recording of running water at tender points, and a ‘Mindrolling’ monstered with claw-handed riffs, they take it to typically stare-down levels of intensity with the sustained threat of ‘Does Anyone Hear Like Venom?’, and billowing sheets of subharmonic distortion harnessed in ‘Everett Moses’. Closer ‘Glory Black’ is, however, a sort of sore thumb with a relatively conventional riff progression and rising banks of silvery wheeze that collapse into keys and field recordings, hearkening most closely to the duo’s precedents and NW peers in the Sub Pop roster, Earth, or even another touchstone, Black Sabbath, at their most strung out. 

Heavy as your life.

items._cn_summary: 这张同名专辑是这支双人乐队成军三十年来的第十张录音室作品，在华盛顿州森林中采集实地录音，融入长达八十分钟的六乐章结构。作品以厚重失真音墙与极缓慢的推进为核心，在仅由两人演奏的条件下营造出沉浸式压迫感；除惯用吉他外，还加入键盘与电声原声处理，使原始金属声响与自然环境声相互渗透。乐评认为这是二人组最纯粹的合作体现，部分曲目以流水声作为微妙点缀，另一曲则呈现咄咄逼人的强力和弦。结尾曲相对常规的推进方式被指为略带异质，但整体仍显露出该组合标志性的强度与专注。

This is the peaceful and contemplative scene that Matt Gold and Resavoir set
items.body:
Lushest, subtropically-infused jazz lilt by seasoned Chicago musicians who’ve worked with SZA, Whitney, Lil Nas X and Clairo, between them - all stamped with International Anthem’s seal of approval and with the pirates of Milton Nascimiento and Herbie Hancock in its breezy air. Record of the summer..?

“album notes by Josh Terry: Imagine it’s late afternoon, you’re outside by the lake, and there’s sunlight on the water. This is the peaceful and contemplative scene that Matt Gold and Resavoir set on their collaborative LP Horizon. Across 10 lush and exploratory tracks, it’s the product of two Chicago-based musicians—Will Miller, the acclaimed trumpeter, composer, and producer who’s worked with SZA, Whitney, and more, and Gold, a seasoned multi-instrumentalist and accomplished guitarist—effortlessly combining their distinct sensibilities for something hypnotic and tangibly inviting. What started as a love letter to their shared admiration for ‘60s and ‘70s Brazilian music evolved into a dynamic and sprawling body of work. These sunny and expansive tunes are as immersive as they are endlessly replayable.

Both Miller and Gold attended Oberlin College’s Conservatory of Music together and in the years after graduating, they orbited each other around Chicago’s music communities. “We were showing up for each other as friends and taking an interest in each other's projects, noticing a lot of resonances and similarities working within in our music,” says Gold, who’s collaborated with artists like Makaya McCraven and Jamila Woods and stretched the bounds of jazz and Americana on solo albums Imagined Sky and Midnight Choir. “We had talked so much about eventually working together that it was almost like an ongoing bit at a certain point,” says Miller. Though they had known each other for over a decade, they first had their chance on “Inside Minds,” the breezy lead single on 2023’s Resavoir. While those sessions were remote, two had palpable chemistry.

It wasn’t until Miller left the touring band of the Chicago group Whitney in 2023 that their plans to make music together in person came to fruition. “When I first started Resavoir, I was chasing the desire to produce records and now that I had time to focus exclusively on that, Matt was the first person I called to come to the studio,” says Miller. The two had bonded over an admiration for the Brazilian guitarist Luis Bonfa and songwriter Milton Nascimento, especially the latter’s work with Herbie Hancock and Wayne Shorter, so they decided to use nylon string guitar as a starting point for these early sessions. “Canopy,” which opens Horizon, was the earliest track. Kicking off with bright acoustic chords, the song slowly unfurls into a slinking groove, samples, and fluttering leads from soprano saxophonist Tim Bennett.

As these initial experiments proved successful, Gold and Miller felt they could broaden the scope of their vision. “We were initially conceiving of it as this acoustic guitar driven record but eventually we wanted to frame it orchestrally and see how many shades and colors we can bring in around that sound,” says Gold. “Dewy” thrives within this orchestral palette of woozy synths, strings from Macie Stewart, Claire Chenette’s oboe, flautist Wills McKenna, and French horns from Lloyd Billingham. “We discovered that our multi-instrumentalist mentalities—using piano and bass, samplers, drum grooves, guitar ideas all as starting points— nurtured the broad orchestration across this record,” says Miller.

“The LP took about a year with on-and-off sessions,” says Miller. “The songs benefit from letting them ferment for a couple months, coming back to it, and seeing what sort of new flavors have developed.” Co-produced by Miller and Gold (and mixed by Dave Vettraino), Horizon proudly reflects the artists’ vast artistic community and musical network in Chicago and beyond. Along with Gold, Eddie Burns (Clairo), Peter Mannheim (Tony Glausi), and Carter Lang (SZA, Lil Nas X) provide drums and percussion throughout. On the dreamlike single “Diversey Beach,” New York songwriter Mei Semones lends vocals and along with her band members Noah Leong and Claudius Agrippa, collaborated on a mesmerizingly conversational string arrangement. “We wrote "Diversey Beach" on the coldest day of the year watching a blizzard coming down out of the window, where the sounds of the cars driving by sounded like waves crashing on a beach,” says Miller. “I sent it to Mei Semones, who I’ve been a fan of for a long time. She's absolutely incredible and it’s amazing what she did with it.”

Horizon is a testament to the feeling of endless possibilities that come from collaboration. It’s a remarkable synthesis of two artists who share musical community and an artist lineage but have carved their own paths in unique ways. Nowhere is this more evident than “Hazel Canyon,” which boasts Gold’s silky pedal steel and a subtly enveloping arrangement that evokes Erasmo Carlos. “Musically, we're always trying to capture a fleeting moment of infinite expanse, feeling the vastness of things while knowing they'll always change,” says Gold. “This record keeps the light reflecting on the water just a little longer -- our collaborative process running through the backbone of these songs and rippling out in so many beautiful directions..””

items._cn_summary: 这张由芝加哥音乐人Matt Gold与Will Miller（Resavoir）合作的专辑，以尼龙弦吉他为起点，融入巴西音乐、爵士与采样元素，营造出阳光而沉浸的声响氛围。两人相识于欧柏林音乐学院，多年后终于面对面完成创作，从对Luis Bonfa和Milton Nascimento的共同喜爱出发，逐渐扩展为十首松散而富有探索性的作品。开篇曲以明亮和弦逐渐铺展为律动，萨克斯与电子音色交织，整体既有即兴的呼吸感，也有精心的编排层次。专辑兼具温暖质感与实验倾向，适合作为夏日背景音乐，也能在细听中捕捉到丰富的细节与融合巧思。

items.body:
Jahtari light the fuse on a bag of digidub sound system detonators by Jamaican producer Prince Riser, aka Robbie Reiser, ranging from low pressure skank to flying dread steppas and original vocal cuts by Sammy Gold & Madi Simmons, all heavily lathered in FX...

“Dub album full of sound system explosives by expert riddim tinkerer Prince Riser – hard rocking, spaced out Kawai synth digi bangers, hitting that sweet spot between analog and digital Reggae while drawing vibes from the legacy of Dread & Fred, Exterminator and Jammy.

Aside from the thunderous Dub epic “Through The Storm” Prince Riser’s debut LP is also featuring the killer vocal cuts “Poverty Ina Russia” by Sammy Gold – a super heavy depth charge of Sly & Robbie proportions – the soulful Wackie’s flavoured anthem “Keep On Trodding” by Madi Simmons (who sadly passed away in 2024) and the plonky digi stepper “Travelling Gal” by Prince Riser himself, each accompanied by a murderous Dub version.

With extra cosmic dust added by disrupt at the Jahtari home studio, “Through The Storm” is crucial gear for any sound system vinyl crate.”
items._genre: digidub / reggae / electronic / dub
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是牙买加制作人Prince Riser在Jahtari厂牌的首张作品，以数字配音风格为核心，融合模拟与数字雷鬼声响。制作上大量使用Kawai合成器，配合丰富的音效处理，营造出适合音响系统的空间感与低音压迫感。专辑包含史诗般的雷鬼配音长曲《Through The Storm》，以及Sammy Gold和Madi Simmons演唱的人声版本，如《Poverty Ina Russia》和《Keep On Trodding》，后者带有灵魂乐与瓦基风格色彩。每首人声曲目还配有对应的配音版本，体现声音系统文化中的混音传统。整体在数字节拍与模拟温暖感之间取得平衡，并加入宇宙氛围点缀。

items.body: The stars appear first. Their light seems to have traveled through the interior of a violin before reaching us, gathering the grain of wood and the pressure of a human hand along the way. Throughout Maksimal, Daniel Temkin thus treats music as celestial mapmaking, drawing places where the horizon turns out to be an instrument played from both sides. The title composition, written in 2022, carries the genetic traces of the Baroque concerto grosso into a world of fractured memory and unstable terrain. Francisco Fullana is the violin soloist, giving the music its incandescent center. Ryan McAdams conducts the Maksimal Ensemble with a keen understanding of the score’s shifting scale, allowing its smallest gestures to retain their mystery even as the orchestral field opens around them. “White Heat” begins with bells and glockenspiel drawing an aperture through which the violin’s restless language can spill across the page of the sky. Images arrive with a precision unavailable to the crude constellations of ordinary imagination, bearing the spirit of something immeasurable yet intimately knowable. Temkin’s orchestration blooms in radiant layers, creating enough space for the violin to run and fly without severing its connection to the ensemble. Fullana’s virtuosity serves as a vehicle for the music’s spirited intelligence, while winds and percussion orbit his line, occasionally catching its light. “Continuum” begins with the violin alone, carving space from time with resolute purpose while scarcely disturbing the air around it. As the orchestra unfolds along the periphery, molecular connections form between vanished cities and the people who once carried those urban spaces inside them. The piano exhales, while the brass catches and draws that breath underground. Though relatively brief, the movement produces the peculiar sensation of arrival. “Circle Games” then opens in buoyant motion before pivoting into contemplation, tracing a recurring exchange between outward momentum and inward gravity. The music brushes against the open-spaced pastoralism one might associate with Copland, yet its landscape keeps slipping beyond the trappings of such comparisons. Dreamed Landscapes, composed between 2017 and 2018 and rendered joyfully by pianist Ryan MacEvoy McCullough, brings this cartographic impulse into a more private cosmos. “Starfield” welcomes us into light as darkness’s fullest utterance, an illumination generated from within the black fabric itself. Dance-inflected steps puncture that fabric and reveal flashes of an alien expressivity, briefly exposing a grammar whose syntax exceeds the human nervous system. The suspicion of otherness soon becomes one that consciousness has always been plural. In “Glaciers crumbling, assembling,” the title’s entropy enters immediately through blocky textures and splintering masses. Fragments break loose from an immense harmonic body, while reformation becomes audible only in the ensuing silence, in which absence begins arranging the wreckage into a structure the ear can enter but never see. “Echoes of the Horizon” draws the cycle’s luminous points into its large-scale dissolutions. The insistent left hand establishes the fundament, while the right hand opens the firmament, hurling packets of emotional voltage across the distance between them. Under McCullough’s touch, the piano becomes a machine for folding vastness until mountains and oceans briefly occupy the same trembling surface. Ocean’s Call, composed in 2015 and revised in 2021, is a string quartet inspired by Big Sur and its environs. The Aizuri Quartet performs it with grace and exacting acuity, preserving the music’s sensuousness without softening its strange geological awareness. In “Hanging Cliffs, Rising Mist,” the cello draws a taut rope of purpose through the texture as the higher strings make room for a rising sun. Pizzicato details become lunar phases, while gradual coalescences deepen the field and pull the listener toward “The Bitter Salt of the Sea.” This central movement speaks in whispers, each phrase carrying the friction between water and air. The strummed cello sends tremors toward the crests of the waves, and the developing urgency becomes a form of surrender with a pulse still beating inside it. Temkin understands that yielding can possess enormous force and allows the music to lean into that paradox until submission and propulsion become indistinguishable. “Lullaby Waves” carries traces of Chinese folksong into harmonizations of light, setting them aboard a vessel woven from tenderness. As it travels farther across the water, the vessel gradually sheds the jurisdiction of the visible world. Across this recording, Temkin teaches the ear to draw maps, then quietly removes the territory beneath the pencil. Memory emerges as the architect of dimensions in which the vanished can continue to resonate. The sky finally collapses into the dark anatomy of listening itself, pierced by the patient apertures we once mistook for stars. The post Daniel Temkin: Maksimal appeared first on Sequenza21.

items._cn_summary: Daniel Temkin的专辑《Maksimal》以当代管弦乐语汇重新诠释巴洛克大协奏曲传统，小提琴独奏家Francisco Fullana在Maksimal Ensemble的衬托下，以炽热而缜密的演奏贯穿全作。标题曲将断裂记忆与不稳定地貌融入器乐对话，而“White Heat”与“Continuum”则通过钟琴、铜管与钢琴的织体营造出太空般的开阔感，在时间与空间中铺展影像。“Circle Games”在流动与沉思间来回摆动，隐约参照美国田园主义却持续滑出比较范围。钢琴家Ryan MacEvoy McCullough演绎的《Dreamed Landscapes》将地图测绘式的想象引入更私密的宇宙，以冰裂般的块状和声与重组中的寂静呈现消散与聚合。整张专辑注重光谱般的配器层次，小提琴在细碎声响与宏大管弦场域间自由穿行，体现了对声音内部空间的精密测绘。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — There is something distinctive that makes Hiromi a jazz pianist whose albums transcend the genre; she grew up listening to 70s fusion and progressive bands, incorporating those harmonies into her music. Consequently, with her group Sonicbloom, those "spacey" explorations and ethereal sounds became more prominent, heightened by the presence of David Fiuczynski, an exquisite avant-garde guitarist whose style defies simple categorization, though it undoubtedly reflects the legacy of Allan Holdsworth. With this group, she created a concept album for her debut centered on the theme of time, as evidenced by the titles of the tracks."Time Difference" possesses both classical sensibility and the surgical, energetic precision of King Crimson. It engages the piano in a dialogue with the drums and guitar, then shifts to keyboard work accompanied by the electric bass."Time Out" features a funkier, more urban and cosmopolitan Groove, evoking a nighttime cocktail hour amidst marquee lights, the din of the crowd, and the sounds of traffic, while the guitar plays dissonant scales and the piano and bass cut through the air with tightly interlocking notes. The band becomes the soundtrack to a New York party, and the balance between experimentation and pure listening pleasure reaches its peak.A tranquil atmosphere with an Oriental feel, as if the spirit of Ryuichi Sakamoto had drifted in through the window, permeates Time Travel; naturally, the influence of Chick Corea's groups, such as Return to Forever and the Elektric Band, is also present. Hiromi is a fine exponent of "progressive jazz," though a different kind than that found in bands like Graham Parker's Strata or Red Kite. David Fiuczynski can play jazz, funk, or the more daring styles heard in Screaming Headless Torsos (another of his bands), while Hiromi continues to play and experiment with sounds alongside the band; at times they sound like a 1970s jam session, shifting to an 80s vibe, and finally landing on 90s fusi�n, a fitting progression, given that the album revolves around the concept of time."Deep Into the Night" reveals another, purely jazz-oriented dimension; it also offers a perfect opportunity to recommend her album with Stanley Clarke, where her piano prowess transcends mere virtuosity to convey ideas and emotions, capturing the spirit of classic jazz that she revives, offering the best of both worlds.A concept difficult to define, that chasm between what one feels and the divide between internal and external reality, is explored in "Real Clock vs. Body Clock = Jet Lag," a track where the meter is as complex as the message itself. Fiuczynski's guitar sounds as if it were melting in the midst of a surrealist act, yet at times she plays as if she were back in the 1920s. "Time and Space" is another gem (the entire album is, truth be told) and reminded me of another master well worth recommending: Misha Mengelberg and his album "Who's Bridge". In that trio setting with Daryl Jones and Joey Baron, they play with time and surprises much like Sonicbloom does here.Classical music takes time by surprise, and a fugue kicks off "Time Control" (or "Controlled by Time"), naturally bringing to mind Keith Emerson, who inhabited that same intersection of classical and jazz, before the band pulls us into the present; the Rhodes piano climbs powerfully alongside the group, reaching the very peaks of the genre and transcending them, with Fiuczynski playing his fretless guitar.Time Flies offers another moment to catch one's breath, a space where a sigh rises toward the sky, mingling with rooftops and treetops, for this album encompasses both day and night! Adventure transforms into fun and reflection; concept albums can be a delightful experience, culminating in an epic finale and the track "Time's Up" (which features a bonus track on the Japanese edition). Here, the band flows like a river, leaving genres behind on the Banks, held back by the stones, until only the purest, most transparent music remains.
