items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items._cn_summary: 挪威三人组合的新作相较前作更贴近地面，但延续了对本土之外民谣的探索。高音萨克斯贯穿始终，爵士即兴色彩明显。开场曲《Springleik》取材自挪威西部舞蹈旋律，贝斯与鼓先提供节奏框架，随后叠加模块合成器与电颤琴增添音色层次。三人的角色界限并不固定，贝斯转而与萨克斯齐奏旋律，鼓组进一步打开节奏空间，整体趋向更自由的即兴状态。作品在传统旋律、爵士演奏与电子声响之间动态游走，体现了乐队对声音组合与即兴互动的持续兴趣。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典小提琴家Mats Edén、挪威多乐器演奏家Tellef Kvifte及其鼓手儿子Knut Kvifte Nesheim组成的三重奏完成，素材主要来自挪威与瑞典的传统舞曲。但与常见民谣专辑不同，三人并未将曲调用作舞蹈伴奏，而是以近似室内乐的方式展开亲密而专注的音乐对话，逐层挖掘旋律中隐藏的意味与暗流。开篇曲《Fossgrimen》取材自挪威塞特斯达尔谷地的传说，暗示了传统音乐背后神秘甚至不安的一面。Kvifte在多数曲目中以sjøfløyte（竖笛）领奏，Edén的提琴与Nesheim的打击乐则提供纹理化铺垫。在瑞典波尔斯卡曲目中，Kvifte先吹奏重复性引子，Edén以朦胧的和声衬底，随后小提琴引入旋律并逐渐走向齐奏，最终在短时间内碎裂停滞。整体上，这张专辑在传统素材基础上进行了细致的节奏与声响重构，呈现出实验性与当代即兴气质。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."

items._cn_summary: 这是一部以芝加哥枪击暴力幸存者口述与环境录音为核心的纪实声音项目，而非传统意义上的音乐专辑。制作人Ian Brennan在街头直接录制了二十五位受枪支暴力影响者的声音，包含即兴说唱、回忆讲述与现场环境噪音，未添加任何音乐配器。录音地点选在社区门廊、飞机航线下方，蚊虫声、街巷杂音与叙述者的情绪共同构成真实的声场。参与者年龄跨度从十七岁到六十七岁，多位社区成员临时加入，内容围绕暴力造成的创伤与日常生活的断裂。作品以极简方式保留了声音的原始质感，让叙事本身成为唯一的音乐性来源。项目收益捐赠给反暴力组织，亦使该录音兼具社会行动意义。

items.body: The UK-based Nigerian producer stretches and pulls the sonics of sacred spaces into mind-bending new shapes Ibukun Sunday on 25.10.2025 at Daylight Music at St John’s Leytonstone [credit Kat Ciemiega Photography] Every year the Semibreve Festival takes attendees on a side quest through the churches of Braga. Each day brings at least one performance of deep, reverberating music in one of the Portuguese city’s many historic places of worship. It’s impossible not to notice the idiosyncratic reverbs these buildings house, but just as integral to how we listen is the hush and awe they induce. I’m not religious. My main reason for visiting a church is to experience concerts of droney, ethereal experimental music. But prolonged exposure to these kinds of places... items._cn_summary: Ibukun Sunday 是一位常驻英国的尼日利亚制作人，他将教堂等神圣空间的声学特性进行拉伸与变形，塑造出扭曲而富有沉浸感的声响形态。该作品与 Semibreve 音乐节关联，在葡萄牙布拉加的古老教堂中演出，利用这些建筑独特的混响与寂静氛围作为创作素材。文章虽为新闻简讯式报道，但揭示了创作者对空间声学的敏锐关注，以及将非洲制作人视角融入宗教空间声音实验的跨文化探索。作品介于环境音乐、田野录音与电子处理之间，属于将场地声学作为乐器的小众实践。

items.body: UK label Cold Spring releases the various-artists set “Noise” on 18 September 2026, collecting 22 tracks of harsh noise and electronics by musicians from mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan. The edition comes as a 2CD in an eight-panel glossy double digipak, with liner notes by Ban Yu. The set began life in 2012 as a China-only 2CDR carrying fifteen tracks, issued by Beijing’s Kwanyin Records. Cold Spring’s version adds seven further sets of works, some dating back as far as 2005, sequenced through the original running order rather than appended to it. Contributors include the Shanghai harsh-noise unit Torturing Nurse, Wang Changcun, Mei Zhiyong, Ronez, Taiwanese sound artist Fujui Wang, Orgasm Denial, Li Jianhong, Xu Cheng and Zafka. Cold Spring describes the material as “massive, piercing, and raucous – deliberately raw and disorienting”. The recordings come from a period when the work was solicited over the internet, through instant messaging, email and online noise groups, with most of the participants living in Beijing or Shanghai and building the tracks on software or hardware at home. Selection for this edition went by the actions and temperaments carried in the recordings rather than by chronology, which is why the added pieces sit inside the original running order. Noise (CSR376CD) by Various Artists Cold Spring ‘Noise’: the 22 tracks CD1: Shu Qi – “Get Rip Of Me” Yu Yiyi – “Free Nerve Ending” Ronez – “Cosmic Frog Bizarre Warfare” Dawang (Black Wolf) – “Untitled 2011121227” Mafeisan – “Meeting” Orgasm Denial – “Hawk Meets Penguin” Li ZengHui – “Thunder Child Crosses Electric Sea” GanzfeldLab – “14.99.17” Zafka – “Noise In Mind” Lao Dan – “This Is A Warning” Li Jianhong – “KG” Fujui Wang – “Pulsing Surds” CD2: Mei Zhiyong – “HaHaHa And The Red Sun” Xu Cheng – “STE-008” Wang Changcun – “Long Single Solid White Line” Zhou Risheng – “BIGNOISE” Beishanqnan – “Whispering Gossip Into A Cat’s Ear At A Party” Wa Hai Gui – “Que Tu Peux Me Faire Calmer” Li Yangyang – “Noise Shambhala” Zhang Yousheng – “The Dancing Girl” Torturing Nurse – “Turntable Contract” The Green Corpse – “POP (Light Version)” The 2CD is available to pre-order through the label’s webstore and Bandcamp. About Cold Spring Cold Spring was founded in 1990 by Justin Mitchell in England, after Mitchell had worked with Thee Temple ov Psychick Youth. The label started with cassette releases in the late 1980s, moved to vinyl and CD through the 1990s, and now issues physical and digital formats across power electronics, death industrial, dark ambient, neo-classical, neo-folk, soundtracks and experimental electronics. It operates from New Mills in Derbyshire. Its catalogue has drawn steadily on scenes outside western Europe, including Japanese noise and material from Russia, China and Poland. Recent Side-Line-covered items include the 1988 cassette compilation “Shoot And Crucify”, reissued on CD in July 2026 and remastered by Martin Bowes of Attrition; Hermann Kopp’s “Der Golem” soundtrack; the 10th-anniversary 2LP reissue of Coil’s “Backwards”; and the “Salò, or The 120 Days of Sodom” soundtrack, released in February 2026. “Noise” continues that reissue and archival strand, and brings a set that circulated only inside China in 2012 to general release.

items.body: Duet Emmo, the one-off collaboration between Daniel Miller of The Normal and Silicon Teens and Wire members Edvard Graham Lewis and B.C. Gilbert, will play live for the first time on Tuesday 27 October 2026 at the ICA in London. The show forms part of the venue’s In The Round series and comes nearly 45 years after the three musicians first met at Blackwing Studio to record “Or So It Seems”, their only album together. Tickets go on sale at 10am UK time on Friday 28 August through DICE, priced at £32.71 including booking fees and the venue levy. The performance takes place on the ICA’s Stage at 7:30pm and uses d&b Soundscape, the venue’s 360-degree spatial soundsystem, with the audience seated around the musicians. The ICA describes the booking in its own announcement: “In association with Mute we’re pleased to announce that Duet Emmo will join ICA’s October In the Round series for a world premiere performance.” Duet Emmo live at the ICA on 27 October Tuesday 27 October 2026 – London, United Kingdom – ICA, The Mall (Stage, 7:30pm) The In The Round programme is curated by the ICA’s Jacob Silkin and runs across the autumn with a separate line-up of electronic and experimental artists. Duet Emmo’s date is presented by the Institute of Contemporary Arts in association with Mute. Or So It Seems (Remastered) by Duet Emmo What ‘Or So It Seems’ is Miller, Lewis and Gilbert recorded the album at Blackwing Studio in London in the gaps between Boxing Day and New Year’s Day in 1981 and 1982, with Eric Radcliffe and John Fryer engineering. All three had other commitments running at the time, and the sessions produced the only record they made together. Mute issued it in August 1983. The project name is an anagram of Mute and Dome, the Lewis and Gilbert duo that ran alongside Wire in the early 1980s. The original sleeve is a collage by the Brothers Quay, the animators and filmmakers, and it was redesigned by Bart van Damme for the reissue. Mute reissued “Or So It Seems” on 19 August 2022, remastered from the original analogue tapes by Stefan Betke at Scape Mastering and expanded to double vinyl, alongside CD and digital editions. Side-Line covered that campaign at the time, first when the reissue was announced and again when the trio shared the remastered “Heart Of Hearts (Or So It Seems)”. The remastered edition runs: “Hill Of Men”, “Or So It Seems”, “Friano”, “The First Person”, “A.N.C”, “Long Sledge”, “Gatemmo”, “Last’s Card” and “Heart Of Hearts (Or So It Seems)”. It is available on Bandcamp and through Mute’s own retail channels. About Duet Emmo Duet Emmo brought together three musicians who already moved through the same London scene. Daniel Miller had released “T.V.O.D.” / “Warm Leatherette” as The Normal in 1978 on the first Mute single, founded the label around it, and followed with the Silicon Teens project. Bruce Gilbert and Graham Lewis were two quarters of Wire, whose first three albums appeared on Harvest between 1977 and 1979, and after the band’s first pause they worked as the duo Dome, releasing four albums under that name between 1980 and 1981 on their own Dome imprint. The three convened at Blackwing Studio in London over the Christmas and New Year periods of 1981 and 1982, with Eric Radcliffe and John Fryer engineering. The resulting album, “Or So It Seems”, appeared on Mute in August 1983, credited to Duet Emmo. A 12-inch of the title track was issued in March 1983, with “Heart Of Hearts” on the B-side; that track later became a bonus cut on CD editions. The record combined electronic sound collage, drone and abstract pop, and it remained the trio’s only release together. Gilbert and Lewis continued as Dome and under further aliases, and both returned to Wire, which reformed in 1985 and again in 2000 and has released studio albums into the 2020s. Miller built Mute into the label behind Depeche Mode, Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds, Erasure and Laibach, and has more recently recorded as Sunroof with Gareth Jones. In 2022 Mute returned to the Duet Emmo album, with Stefan Betke remastering it from the original tapes for a double-vinyl edition released on 19 August that year. The ICA date on 27 October 2026 is the first time the three have taken the project to a stage.
items._genre: post-punk / electronic / experimental
items._cn_summary: Duet Emmo由Mute厂牌创始人Daniel Miller与Wire成员Edvard Graham Lewis和B.C. Gilbert组成，项目名称本身即为Mute和Dome的字母变位重组。三人于1981至1982年间在Blackwing Studio完成了唯一一张专辑《Or So It Seems》的录制，由Eric Radcliffe和John Fryer担任工程师。2022年由Stefan Betke从原始模拟磁带完成重新母带处理，扩展为双黑胶版本发行。此次伦敦ICA的现场首演是三人近四十五年来首次同台，使用360度空间声音系统，演奏将延续他们早年合作中那种冷峻、机械化的极简电子质感与后朋克骨架。Mute厂牌的独立基因和Wire一脉相承的实验脉络贯穿始终，是一次稀缺的历史性现场呈现。

items.body: For the second episode of our Musical Road to WOMEX, we go from Caracas to Berlin by way of a conservatory in Barquisimeto, the route that shaped Gotopo into one of the more unclassifiable voices on the Afro-Latin Dance circuit. She runs Afro-Indigenous Venezuelan rhythm through techno production until neither side gives way, calls the result Ancestral Futurism, and stages it with a female-warrior aesthetic built as much for main-room dancefloors as festival fields. She started at the conservatory in Barquisimeto and came up through El Sistema, the youth-orchestra system that’s put instruments in the hands of generations of Venezuelan kids. She left for Berlin afterward and started over, busking to get by while she learned German. Her stage name comes from her own family history: Gotopo was the last indigenous chief of the region her family comes from. Nobody in her family had kept that history. She found it herself, digging through records nobody else had bothered to look at. She’s described the discovery as grief and celebration arriving together, something erased and something recovered in the same breath. Her 2023 debut EP, Sacúdete, followed, released on Waxploitation, the label built around Gnarls Barkley and Danger Mouse, with Don Elektron and Bomba Estéreo’s Simón Mejía among the collaborators. The reach has widened fast since. The title track ended up soundtracking Major League Soccer’s entire 2024 season, and a newer single, “Mi Gente Lo Siente,” is currently running under the trailer for Valorant Masters 2026. This October she brings that sound to Las Palmas de Gran Canaria at WOMEX’s Club Summit, the strand built around club and electronic sound from across the world. You trained in the conservatory and El Sistema, then found your own voice in Europe by reaching back to your Afro-Indigenous roots. What was the turning point that set that direction? When you take distance you start seeing things you never noticed before or comprehend them much deeper and from new points of view. The music conservatory planted in me a seed of discomfort of existing inside a music education that was so Eurocentric. Then ironically enough, it was Europe that gave me the space to explore how an ancestor of the future could exist in 202+. WOMEX lands this year in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, an Atlantic island whose timple itself carries old Latin American trade routes back across the ocean. As a Venezuelan artist, what are you most curious to discover about that shared history there? Because of the mass migration of Venezuelans I learnt that there’s a huge Canarian community in Venezuela spanning a few decades, people who saw in Venezuela a place to thrive, which it was, and now of course, it’s a reversed migration of kids and grand-kids back to Canaria… I’m obsessed with history and this one promises to be a huge adventure: What dishes will I taste here that will remind me of home? Or maybe slang words that were Venezuelan and landed here, or the opposite? It’s sooo weird in a cool way, I’m so curious! Your work fuses ritual and rave, the sacred and the synthetic. In a WOMEX programme full of traditions, what makes that fusion distinctly yours, and what do you want people to take from your showcase? Groove and vocals are the 2 cores of the most ancient musical memories we hold as humans… sometimes I think that we sang before we even spoke. I always want to make sure that my music makes you move, to me there is nothing more ancestral than groove, and in a Gotopo show you will hardly leave without having collectively sang along with a bunch of strangers WOMEX always sparks unexpected meetings. Which artists, labels or collaborators are you hoping to cross paths with in Las Palmas? There are festivals that I love because of their eclecticism and how they don’t care about Genre but rather about energy. THIS! This is so important for music, for culture and for human connection! I know the festival scene is going through challenging times for several reasons, specially the way kids discover and connect with music is changing… so I don’t blame festivals having to make tough decisions, and including upcoming acts in that equation is a challenge. But I also hope to see a future of festival/event curation where instead of falling for the extremes of either “play safe and book what the listener wants” or “I just book what I like”, promoters and bookers truly put an effort into understanding TikTok and new audiences and how these two are reprogramming people’s way to connect with culture. If you understand something you can hack it for your purpose, kinda, you know? It would be so sad if the curator’s experience of music and culture became isolated from the new generations. I do my job as an artist on social media, but curators, bookers and promoters who also understand this and actively work to stay up-to-date are definitely people I want to meet. Your live shows are as much performance and ritual as concert. How does a room of delegates change how you bring that energy? That’s a great question… I don’t think I want to change absolutely anything about my show. Gran Canaria sits at a mid-Atlantic crossroads between Africa, Europe and the Americas — exactly the between-worlds space you describe as a Latina in Germany. Does a place like that speak to your work? So much! And it makes me interested at a human level before anything, it’s an area I have yet to explore and it’s so exciting to perform in a place where there are so many ancient traces of you… of our constant migrations and cultural exchanges as humans which remind one another: this is what makes us pretty awesome as a humanity. If you could write a personal invitation to the people of Las Palmas to come and discover your showcase, what would it say? Have you heard about this girl from Venezuela? Some of her songs are catchy like Shakira but she’s a bit weirder.   Gotopo plays WOMEX 26's Club Summit in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria 21–25 October, at the Auditorio Alfredo Kraus   PLAYLIST: GOTOPO X RHYTHM PASSPORT   You can find all the previous episodes of Musical Road to Womex HERE   The post Musical Road to WOMEX 2026 – Gotopo appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items._cn_summary: 委内瑞拉艺术家Gotopo将非洲-原住民节奏与电子制作融合，提出"祖先日未来主义"概念。出身于Barquisimeto音乐学院与El Sistema体系，后赴柏林重新出发，从家族史料中发掘原住民首领身份的血脉记忆。2023年首张EP《Sacúdete》由Waxploitation发行，与Danger Mouse、Don Elektron、Bomba Estéreo成员合作。作品同时服务于主流场景——美国职业足球大联盟主题曲、电竞预告片配乐——与俱乐部锐舞场地。整体呈现拉丁美洲传统节奏、科技舞曲质感与女性战士美学的三方交汇，文章以WOMEX专访形式展开，触及文化寻根与离散迁徙等议题。

items.body:
Still influential three decades after its release, Rachel's' debut album is a low-key genre classic, welding the cinematic orchestrations of Carter Burwell to nascent post-rock structures and influencing bands like A Silver Mt. Zion and Clogs in the process.

Originally deployed on Touch And Go's sister label Quaterstick in 1995, 'Handwriting' was a complete anomaly at the time. There was a feeling that the album had only appeared on the label because it'd been the home of Rodan, the popular post-hardcore outfit that Rachel's founder Jason Noble had been a member of. But as time ticked on, Rachel's forward-thinking fusion of post-rock and chamber music began to appear more prescient. The band was originally conceived by Noble and viola player Christian Frederickson in the late '80s, but when Rodan blew up, Noble was too preoccupied to follow up their experiments. Time, of course, ticked on and Rodan imploded, so Noble and Frederickson picked up the pieces, inviting pianist Rachel Grimes to contribute. And the band's debut is a real one-off; they'd follow it with the brilliant Nyman-esque 'Music for Egon Schiele', but by that time their post-hardcore/post-rock echoes had all but disappeared. As it is, 'Handwriting' is at the root of a sound that almost immediately blossomed further north in Montréal. 

Linking the tangled riffs of Slint and of course Rodan with the scenic ambience of Labradford and, most importantly, Michael Nyman's minimal compositions, Noble, Grimes and Frederickson pre-empted something that's permeated throughout the scene at large over the three decades that followed. Even 'M. Daguerre', one of the album's early highlights and its jazziest track, that hews closer to The Necks' early material than anything else, provides a tangible blueprint. But it's the cooler, quieter moments that keep us coming back to 'Handwriting', like the emotive 'Seratonin' or the absolute milestone 'Full on Night', a stripped-to-the-bone Southern gothic post-rock jam that dissolves into a mass of radio static, film samples and chugging steam trains. If Godspeed hadn't heard this one before they recorded 'F♯ A♯ ∞', we'd be very surprised.
items._genre: post-rock / chamber music / contemporary classical / minimalism
items._cn_summary: 这是Rachel's于1995年在Quaterstick厂牌发行的首张专辑，将Slint式的缠绕吉他与Michael Nyman风格的极简室内乐编制熔于一炉。小提琴、中提琴与钢琴在缓慢铺陈的动态中交织，既保留了Rodan时期后硬核的骨骼，又向现代古典与极简主义大幅倾斜。专辑以电影化的场景感著称，如《Full on Night》以南方哥特式的吉他骨架切入，最终消融于电台噪声、电影采样与蒸汽火车声效之中。整体氛围克制、阴郁而富有空间感，预示了随后在蒙特利尔绽放的后摇美学，被视为Godspeed You! Black Emperor《F♯ A♯ ∞》的重要前驱。制作上将即兴段落与精密编排结合，是跨界融合的一次早期成功实践。

items.body:
DJ Plead and rRoxymore with a sick debut collab of rhythmelodically restless productions, infusing limber, freewheeling styles with subtly psychedelic balearic melodics - a big one for followers of CCL, Batu, Nick León, Olof Dreijer, Joe, Nídia & Valentina Magaletti.

After meeting for the first time in 2019, Hermione Frank and Jarred Beeler got together at Frank's Berlin studio, slowly sculpting fractal geometries before finally adding the finishing spit and polish at Beeler's parents’ house in Sydney. Marking some of the first original material from either in a minute, the EP knits the duo’s rhythmic fascinations in three ways. 

‘Celestial’ splices a rolling 4/4 with quicksilver polyrhythms and zippy melodic motifs swept into hand-clap trills, imagining something like Olof Dreijer re-shaping Joe’s angular syncopations. ‘Read Wrong’ follows to foreground a thumb piano on a more pendulous, sub-weighted flex, inflected with DJ Plead’s signature palette of drum sounds and canny orchestral flashes at the right moments, dipping like D1’s more melodic works or that forthcoming Nídia & Valentina Magaletti pearl. 

The duo save their most hard-hitting for last, sliding speedy, dembow-inspired geometries through green-tinted clouds of electronics on a UKF-compatible offbeat threaded with swooping subs and flighty flutes. The momentum never lets up, but the two producers manage to evoke a mood that's as suited to a late-nite solo thing as it is to peak time wreckage. In other words; deceptively effortless gear that hits harder the louder it gets.
items._genre: electronic / experimental / club / rhythmic fusion
items._cn_summary: DJ Plead与rRoxymore的首度合作EP《Read Round City》，从柏林到悉尼历时数月雕琢完成。三首作品均围绕节奏实验展开：开篇《Celestial》将滚动的四四拍与水银般的多节律交织，辅以拍手花音与跳跃旋律动机；《Read Wrong》以拇指钢琴为主角，在更沉重、悬挂式的低音律动中点缀管弦乐闪光；终曲则以dembow启发的几何节奏穿过电子音色云层，sub低音与笛声交错，兼容UKF节奏框架。两位制作人将各自的节奏痴迷编织成三种不同形态，从深夜独处到高峰时段俱乐部均能适配。整体呈现出伪装轻松的制作质感，音量越大冲击越强。

items.body:
Mutant club flexes from YOUTH & $hotta Tapes’ alum Leo on a new LP rendering traces of UKG, dembow and brukbeats with weightless sound designer physics inna deadly style.

A certain bygone spirit of early ‘00s electronic and UK dance music guide Leo to mess with club mechanisms in expressively curious ways on ‘Dissipating Heavily.’ The tightly sculpted eight track album chases two volumes of the self-released ‘lived’ tapes with the corkscrewing results of concerted studio sessions spent eking his own sound from a Manchester air thick with ghosts of dance music’s past.

Wafting in with the melancholic sway and Pev style dubstep lean of ‘Worth’, the album buckles and tears between the peg-leg stumble of his knotty drums on ‘Banal’ to a bit of Bristol-styled dubstep tension in ‘Dramaed’, and down a trapdoor of noisier inspiration with ‘Embarrassment of Riches’. At its core, ‘Funicular’ stars out for levels of stick ’n move brukstep parry comparable to prime Demdike Stare, and ‘Courts’ zip-ties a dembow rhythm with shearing sound design to darkside effect also explored in the sidewinding momentum of ‘Jade Floors’, before ‘Passion Assets’ vents the tension upwards and outwards.
items._genre: experimental electronic / mutant club / UK bass / dubstep / sound design
items._cn_summary: Leo 在这张专辑中以曼彻斯特为背景，对俱乐部音乐机制进行解构与重组。专辑横跨UKG、dembow、brukbeats 等元素，融合Pev 式dubstep 律动与Bristol 派dubstep 张力，并在声音设计层面展现出无重力的空间感。八首曲目在紧密编排下呈现丰富的形态变化：有的以结节式鼓组构建跛行节奏，有的将dembow 律动与剪切式合成器音效绑定，制造出幽暗侧行的推进力。整体在俱乐部音乐的骨架中注入了实验性的解构逻辑与重量感的声音处理，既保留舞曲的律动本能，又拓展了其作为声音艺术的表达边界。

items.body:
'Force Majeure' looks back on ACR's P-Funk-inspired fifth album 'Force' and plucks out a handful of unreleased versions of tracks from the album - including the title track that never made it to the original release.

By 1986, ACR were a very different band than when they started. Founder members Simon Topping and Peter Terrell left after finishing their fourth album, 'I'd Like to See You Again', forcing the band to regroup. Bassist and vocalist Jez Kerr and guitarist/trumpeter Martin Moscrop took the reins, bringing in Kalima's Tony Quigley and retaining keyboardist Andy Connell before he left to concentrate on his popular pop project Swing Out Sister.

But despite the chaos at the time, the album's a sturdy entry in the ACM canon, a fusion of post-punk, funk and nascent electro elements that still stands out. This companion release showcases a few raw-er takes - the version of 'Naked and White' benefits from the additional saturation and mixing desk chaos - and it's a treat to hear the lounge-y title track, that's for sure.
items._genre: post-punk / funk / electro
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑围绕A Certain Ratio 1986年专辑《Force》的未发行版本展开，收录了包括标题曲在内的数首原始录音。彼时乐队经历成员变动，重组后的阵容在post-punk基础上融入P-Funk式放克律动与早期电子元素，形成粗粝而律动鲜明的声响。此次披露的版本保留了更直接的混音质感，如《Naked and White》在额外饱和与调音台混乱中显出更强张力，而标题曲的轻松俱乐部氛围则展现了乐队另一面。对于关注后朋克与放克交叉地带的听众，这些素材提供了观察乐队创作过程的补充视角。

items.body:
French cold wave and goth disco par excellence. Not hard to imagine Annie Hogan spinning the likes of ‘L’Appel Du Froid’ at The Batcave, or insouciant, kohl-eyed Gallic teens bopping at their local goth jamboree to this lot. Evidently there’s clear reasons why this DIY self-release of ’88 now trades for triple figures on resale markets…

“Opéra de Nuit emerge from their long slumber to grace Dark Entries with the frostiest of reissues. Formed in 1982 in Valréas in the southeast of France, Opéra de Nuit only released 3 records throughout their career: EPs in 1984 and 1986, with a full LP following in 1988. But devotees of dark music will need no introduction to this band, who are almost definitional of the coldwave genre, and whose rabid cult following has each record readily trading for three-digit prices. Opéra de Nuit’s sound is pure hellish heaven: frigid synths, jangly guitars, and sorrow-laden vox. 

Check out the pummelling desperation of “Annabella,” the uber-brooding vibes of “Boris Transylvania Camp,” or the elegant anthem “Karen Lloyd” (and don’t forget to watch the video!). This reissue collects their entire newly remastered discography – thirteen lucky tracks. This reissue marks the first time that their work will be reissued on vinyl and digital, and is presented in gatefold jacket with lyrics and photos. Whether you’re new to the genre or a veteran of the coldest waves, Opéra de Nuit brings the essential sound of immortal despair.”
items._genre: coldwave / goth disco / darkwave / post-punk
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是法国乐队 Opéra De Nuit 的完整再版，收录其1980年代三张唱片的十三首重新母带曲目，并首次以黑胶和数字形式面世，附有歌词和照片。乐评强调其冷潮风格的代表性：冰冷合成器、清亮吉他与人声的悲伤质感，同时兼具哥特迪斯科的律动，适合暗夜俱乐部舞池。作品如《Annabella》展现迫切的绝望，《Boris Transylvania Camp》营造深沉阴郁氛围，《Karen Lloyd》则是优雅的抒情之作。作为法国地下场景中的 DIY 自发行，该乐队在二手市场的高价流通印证了其邪典地位。此次再版让新听众得以接触这一冷潮流派的原初样貌，其声响设计在当下听来依然具有清晰辨识度，是理解法国冷潮音乐的重要文献。

items.body:
Decades of taut intuition feed forward into Russian Circles’ instrumental metal alloys of post-rock, hardcore, prog, and krautrock on their ninth album, recorded at local bastion Electrical Audio by Kurt Ballou (Converge, Mastodon, High on Fire)...

"Chicago-bred post metal trio Russian Circles new album Nine continues their unhurried evolution and disciplined refinement, leaning into their strengths while pushing at the boundaries of their sound. This is a band with no hit songs. No fan consensus on their best album. Just a reputation of consistency and quality that built one of the biggest heavy instrumental rock bands in the world.While they insist that their music is a confluence of broad-ranging influences, it’s fair to say that Russian Circles’ adventurous diversity has developed into a distinct and singular sound.

Although Russian Circles is now spread across the country - guitarist Mike Sullivan in Los Angeles, drummer Dave Turncrantz based in Chicago, and bassist/keyboardist Brian Cook living in Vashon Island, outside of Seattle - the band triangulate their relative positions for Nine. Its seven seismic tracks act as long-form oriented soundtracks to the trials and tragedies of life in the modern age. “The music we make is a collective process of reconciliation, navigation, and reflection upon aging both as individuals and as a creative entity. Life has created very real distances between us, but the band continues to be at the center, and this creative collaboration is a way of charting the passage of time while also giving us a reason to look to the future,” the band elaborates. Whereas earlier albums were almost playful in their traversing of territories, Nine is a document of a band that knows the lay of the land and is fortifying their dominion over the varied terrain."
items._genre: instrumental metal / post-rock / progressive / krautrock / hardcore
items._cn_summary: 这是芝加哥后金属三人组Russian Circles的第九张专辑，在Electrical Audio由Kurt Ballou录制。乐队成员分居洛杉矶、芝加哥和西雅图附近，通过远程协作完成创作。音乐延续并深化了他们对后摇滚、硬核、前卫摇滚和泡菜摇滚的融合，形成独特的器乐金属声响。七首曲目如同长格式的配乐，映射现代生活中的考验与悲剧。乐队表示，创作过程是对个体与集体衰老经验的调和、导航与反思，尽管地理距离遥远，合作仍是维系他们的核心，也是记录时间并指向未来的方式。相比早期作品在不同风格间的游走，这张专辑更像是对自身疆域的确认与巩固，体现出乐队在长期磨合后对多样化地形的掌控力，也是他们稳步演进与精确提炼的成果。

items.body:
Co-produced by Nosaj Thing and 'Donnie Darko' OST guy Michael Andrews, Eartheater's latest is the polar opposite of 2023's 'Powders', ditching the drug and club references and leaning into baby-on-board playlist fodder, including an Oklou feature. RIYL Dido, Dubstar, Sneaker Pimps.

It's still obviously an Eartheater record, more 'Phoenix' than 'Powders'. The album starts strong, with her robotically treated voice sounding oddly soothing next to a full orchestra on 'Eyes of a Dove'. Even the glossy, sync-ready 'Paradise Rains', the album's first single that details her buying back her childhood farm and conceiving her baby, is chewably eccentric, still bound to the same logic that made her bonkers early material so addictive.
items._genre: art pop / experimental electronic / orchestral pop / dream pop
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由两位风格迥异的制作人联合制作，与上一张作品的夜店与药物意象拉开距离，转而围绕育儿、原生农场与家庭经历展开私密叙事。开篇曲将机器人化处理的人声置于完整管弦乐团之上，形成一种近乎抚慰的疏离感；主打单曲带有顺滑的配乐感和明显的同步潜力，却仍以回买童年农场、受孕等具体而古怪的细节维持着创作者特有的荒诞逻辑。整体气质更接近其早期作品中偏向声响铺陈与氛围化的一面，在光滑的流行表层下保留了对声音质地和叙事细节的独特处理。对于关注实验电子与艺术流行交界的听众，这张专辑提供了兼具亲和力与辨识度的样本。

items.body:
Regelbau chief Natal Zaks, who you may better known as Danish house talent Central, returns to his Picture alias hot on the heels of a full-length under the same moniker on his usual home, Short Span.

"This EP comes on P-TON, NMP's sub label, and is pristine dub techno with clean lines and minimal fuss. 'Faaaaaaaaa' has the right amount of swing and pop under sleek chords, 'Gaaaaaaaaaa' is less about firmware demotion and more about locking you in an endless cycle of brain cleansing thought. 'Kaaaaaaaa' is a darker world of cavernous bass and icy futurism and 'Tuuuuuuuu' nods to the best of Basic Channel. Proper dub techno that reinvents nothing but does everything exceptionally well."
items._genre: dub techno / dub / techno / electronic
items._cn_summary: 丹麦制作人Natal Zaks化名Picture，在P-TON旗下推出这张EP。它不是对dub techno的激进改造，而是在既有框架内完成高精度执行的作品。开篇曲以利落和弦与恰当摇摆感营造弹性律动；随后曲目转向循环往复的净化式节拍，稳定低音与空间感逐渐铺展；中段则以洞穴般的低频和冰冷未来感勾勒出更幽暗的声响世界；末曲呼应Basic Channel一脉的经典气质。整体线条干净克制，不发明新规则，但在声音质感和细节处理上相当到位。

items.body:
Oh man this is almost too much - just wall to wall genius in action courtesy of Floating Points & Eliot Bernard's Melodies International label -  spotlightling fire in the crown of Mad Professor’s pivotal London Lovers Rock and dub stable, Ariwa Sounds: from an immense monk-steppa ‘Non Violence Dub’ ft. Horace Andy, thru the Motown soul-infused Lovers of Davina Stone on 'Silly Wasn’t I’, to a Kofi gem recently found on Moin’s street-soul/digidub mix, the ruffneck charge of Mafia & Fluxy ‘6 Million Dub’, early Wild Bunch styles on Aisha’s ‘Can You Feel It’, and deadly ‘Liberated Woman’ voiced by Ranking Ann. All killer no filler!

“In 1979, Neil Fraser (artistically known as Mad Professor) founded Ariwa Sounds, the longest-serving and one of the most influential independently owned Reggae studios and record labels in the UK. From humble beginnings set up in the front room of Neil's home in South London recording on 4-track and homemade equipment, Ariwa would go on to record and release over 300 albums including works from some of the most impactful and storied artists of their time in the genres of Reggae, Dub, and Lovers Rock

Whilst our previous release in collaboration with Ariwa captured the label's early sound, a shared performance with Neil in Osaka and regular visits to his South London studio inspired us to assemble this 15-track compilation, showcasing the label's output across 45 years. Our release emphasizes some of the label's greatest vocalists: Johnny Clarke, Sandra Cross, Kofi, U Roy, Sister Nancy, Queen Omega, Aisha, Garnett Cross, Abel Miller, Horace Andy and more — presenting the Motown and Stax influences in the Lovers Rock, but also provides a glimpse into the dubbier and more experimental side of the label, showcasing Ariwa's commitment to quality but also their personality, philosophy and their humour. Love songs, break-up songs, socially engaged songs, dub experimentations — this compilation is not a "best of" Ariwa but a diverse and honest celebration of the label through the lens of Melodies International.”
items._genre: dub / lovers rock / reggae
items._cn_summary: 这张由 Melodies International 策划的合辑，聚焦 Mad Professor 创立的 Ariwa Sounds 厂牌四十五年来的声音谱系。选曲横跨爱情歌谣、社会议题与实验性混音，既有 Horace Andy 的厚重僧侣式步调，也有 Davina Stone 的 Motown 灵魂情歌，以及 Aisha、Ranking Ann 等呈现的早期 Wild Bunch 风格。Mafia & Fluxy 的粗粝数字舞曲与 Kofi 的街头灵魂/数字混音则展示厂牌更暗面、更实验的取向。合辑并非单纯精选，而是通过 DJ 视角呈现 Ariwa 从居家四轨录音到逾三百张专辑发行的独立轨迹，体现其将牙买加声音体系与伦敦黑人社区文化融合的独特身份，在情歌与重低音之间保持张力与幽默感。

items.body:
30 year return of Model 500’s overlooked but killer comet, straddling classic late ‘80s and emergent ‘90s strands of deep 313 electro-techno.

One of the more distant stars in the Metroplex galaxy, Juan Atkins’ 1993 single tends to the more introspective, wide-eyed side of Detroit club music. ‘I See The Light’ places his signature over-the-shoulder vocoder in an aerodynamic answer to his late ‘80s electro classics, riddled with ‘Clear’-styled arps and wickedly woozy choral pads ideal for tempering a set between more boisterous gear.

‘Pick Up the Flow’ is more clearly in step with the deep techno sound he was concocting at the time (often with Moritz Von Oswald), but still whirring with electro mechanics, balancing glyding pads and vocal soliloquy for the first half, and weaving in more Eastern-oriented melodic tang on the 2nd part.
items._genre: electro / techno / deep techno / Detroit techno
items._cn_summary: 这张1993年的单曲由胡安·阿特金斯发行，是底特律电子星系中较不常被提起的一支，串联起八十年代末的旧式电音舞曲与九十年代初的深邃科技舞曲。第一面以标志性声码器人声、清脆琶音和晃动感合唱音色营造出空灵流动的氛围，适合在较激烈的段落之间作缓冲。第二面更接近他与莫里茨·冯·奥斯瓦尔德合作时期的深邃科技舞曲方向，同时保留机械化的电子律动；前半段以滑音音色和声音独白铺展，后半段加入东方调式的旋律转折。整体在俱乐部功能性和个人化声响之间取得平衡，反映了底特律舞曲从早期电音转向科技舞曲时的中间形态。

items._cn_summary: 乐评介绍了贝斯手兼作曲家Liz Draper在Edna's Park的声音装置演出。她自称的风格“classicaldoomfolkjazz”融合了古典、末日民谣与爵士元素，在公园露天环境中形成一种沉郁而即兴的声音氛围。文章以阴晴不定的天空作为背景，暗示演出与自然声响之间可能存在的对话。由于原文内容较简短，并未展开具体曲目、装置构造或演奏细节，仅能看出这是一次带有实验性质的跨界声音实践。该作品结合了当代古典的写作思维、民谣的叙事感以及爵士的即兴性，同时通过暗色调的称谓传递出某种压抑或内省的气质。对于关注融合类型和声音装置的听众，这一简介提供了可供追踪的线索。

items.body: KKKAAARRREEENNNIIINNNAAA captures a 2025 performance that the three artists did together in London Charlemagne Palestine, Oren Ambarchi and Daniel O'Sullivan are releasing a collaborative album, titled KKKAAARRREEENNNIIINNNAAA. Consisting of one extended piece, the record captures a May 2025 live performance that the three artists did together at London's Cafe OTO. The set saw the trio reimagine a key vocal work of Palestine's, Karenina, which he originally recorded in Paris in March 1997. In this version, O'Sullivan controls three cassette machines playing the original recording, and also plays viola, synths and adds live vocals. Ambarchi contributes guitar, while Palestine adds his live voice and plays keyboard. Black Truffle will release KKKAAARRREEENNNIIINNNAAA on 11 September 2026. ... The post Charlemagne Palestine, Oren Ambarchi and Daniel O’Sullivan Collaborate on New Album appeared first on The Quietus.
items._genre: experimental / avant-garde / drone / electroacoustic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了Charlemagne Palestine、Oren Ambarchi与Daniel O'Sullivan三人在2025年5月于伦敦Cafe OTO的现场合作录音，作品重新演绎了Palestine于1997年录制的关键声乐作品《Karenina》。演出中，O'Sullivan操控三台卡带机播放原始录音，并演奏中提琴、合成器和进行现场人声；Ambarchi贡献吉他，而Palestine则以现场人声与键盘参与。整张专辑仅由一首长篇幅作品构成，聚焦于声音层次的重叠与实时即兴，将原始录音媒介与原声乐器、电子声效融合在一起。该专辑由Black Truffle厂牌发行，适合关注实验声乐、极简主义与即兴演出的听众。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — These Arizona bros are definitely hooked on Krautrock ala Neu!, Can, Tangerine Dream and more of thekind. Soundscapes of Tangerine Dream, Cluster, early-Kraftwerk and the hypnotic "motorik" rock ofNeu! or Can. However, Trees Speak take 1970s German experimental rock & electronic music and puttheir own modern spin on them. Too bad they don't expand (read extend) more some of those greatideas (some of these tracks are way too short, IMHO), thus inducing a bit of a frustration in termsof depth - though this is never shallow, au contraire. One can only wonder if they'd dared plunginginto epic-length sonic explorations that Froese & Co. had done in their heydays.We've got a series of 16 short soundscapes (none over 4-mins) that are +/- fused into each other,and they transport you into the realms of synth and computer servers and other electronicsnightmares, and it's rather addictive, partly because there are real drums and a few more realinstruments played by guests (some will return on the next albums). The middle of the album , fromSadness of Wires until the title track is one amazing trip in copper and silicium. AFAIAC, my favetrack is Chamber Of Frequencies, where 'trons and and guitars create a special little plus.Though the following albums are of the same ilk, I must that none of them have resonated as muchwith my eardrums as their debut Ohms, partly because the surprise is gone. Impossible to pull outthe CD for only one sole listen: minimum two or three plays and it usually remains close to the deckfor possible more spins before heading (finally) back into the shelf. My 3.5 stars are of course notobjective, because Post-Human probably deserve as much as their previous releases, but I can't helpbeing subjective, not having that "Wow" factor.
items._genre: krautrock / experimental rock / electronic / psychedelic rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以1970年代德国实验摇滚与电子乐传统为基底，乐评人指出Trees Speak在Neu!、Can、Tangerine Dream等影响之上加入当代电子制作和真实鼓组/器乐客串，形成比单纯复古更贴近当下的质感。16首曲目大多不足四分钟且彼此衔接，中段从Sadness of Wires到标题曲被形容为一次连贯的铜与硅之旅行；Chamber of Frequencies因电子与吉他互动尤为突出。乐评人认为曲目长度限制了意念的延展，缺少前作Ohms的惊喜感，但整体并不浅薄，且具有反复聆听的吸引力。

items.body: Review by ProgExpert — It is amazing to hear H�llas go fully prog on *Panorama*. The record feels broader, more ambitious, and more mature than ever, while still retaining the melodic instinct and personality that make the band distinctive. I only wish a few especially beautiful musical ideas had been explored further, particularly the passage around 3:30 in the first suite and the wonderful final theme at the very end of the last song. Those moments are so strong that I wanted them to keep unfolding. It is brilliant to hear these artists growing in ambition and maturity. We simply cannot have enough of this music.
items._genre: crossover prog / progressive rock / rock
items._cn_summary: 乐评人认为Hällas在《Panorama》中展现出比以往更宏大、更具野心的创作格局，同时保留了乐队标志性的旋律感与个性。专辑中的一些段落，如第一首组曲约3分30秒处的过渡，以及最后一曲结尾的主题，被特别点出为最动人的瞬间，但乐评人希望这些音乐材料能获得更充分的展开。整体上，乐评人对乐队在创作广度和成熟度上的成长给予肯定，认为这样的音乐值得更多呈现。

items.body: Review by ProgExpert — This is a remarkably delicate and sensitive record, played with exceptional taste throughout. Every arrangement feels carefully judged... nothing is overstated, and the musicianship is consistently impressive without ever becoming showy. There is a warmth and naturalness to the playing that gives the music an almost timeless quality! At several moments, it recalls the more pastoral and adventurous side of 1970s Caravan, with that same combination of melodic richness, subtle complexity, and effortless flow. What stands out most, though, is the restraint. Beautifully performed, elegant, and deeply musical. I cannot get enough, I wish they had composed 10 records! Not just 2! Come back Jouis!
items._genre: crossover prog / progressive rock / canterbury
items._cn_summary: 乐评人形容这是一张极其细腻而敏感的唱片，演奏品味贯穿始终。编曲的分寸感被反复称道：不夸张、不炫技，但器乐表现始终保持凝练与温暖。音乐带有1970年代坎特伯雷场景的牧歌与冒险气质，旋律丰富且暗藏复杂度，整体流动自然。最突出之处在于克制与留白，使作品显得优雅而富有音乐性。评者还表达了对乐队创作量的期待，认为这样的音乐值得反复聆听。

items.body: Review by yarstruly — Really 4.75, but clicked 5...4 is too low.Quivira are new prog band consisting of: ?Jake Livgren (Emerald City Council, Kerry Livgren Band, Proto Kaw?he's Kerry's nephew) on lead vocals, ?Composer Lisa LaRue (RematriNation, Solo, 2KX, Federico Fantacone), on keyboards and programming, and ?John Baker (Forever Twelve, Mars Hollow, Little Girls) on guitars, bass and vocals. There are two guest performers: - Joe Deninzon (Kansas, Stratospheerius) / violin (5)- Evan Stanley (Stanley-Simmons?Paul Stanley's son) / guitar (9)According to the press release:This project blends historical themes, classic rock, and cinematic progressive rock into multi-movement works that emphasize narrative cohesion, harmonic exploration, and textural depth. The debut focuses on the story of pre-Kansas "Quivira", the Native American villages that Coronado believed held gold.This album comes courtesy of Nick Katona of Melodic Revolution Records (MRR). As always, I receive no further compensation, and I call it like I hear it. As per my usual method, this is a cold listen.Track 1 - (Intro) The Coming of the Spaniards (3:52)A blend of vocal and string sounds provides a cinematic beginning, joined by drum accents. This feels like the beginning of an epic movie. Acoustic guitar gradually enters the soundscape along with the choral and orchestral themes. The acoustic guitar becomes more prominent as we proceed. A grand introduction!Track 2 - The Benefits of Breathing Quietly (5:55)The music quiets down to a single violin-like sound, then piano, bass and percussion enter. Jake Livgren enters on vocals with a very expressive melody. There are wonderful harmonies as the verse continues to build. The piano parts are absolutely beautiful as a synth solo enters soon after. The sound is warm and full; great production. Jake's vocals are exceptional! Not to play too heavily on the Kansas connection, but he is reminiscent of Steve Walsh in his prime. Lisa LaRue's synth solo is fantastic. The drum programming has some nice fills and syncs nicely, but I would always prefer a live drummer. Outstanding piano work as the song nears its conclusion. Jake closes it out with more top-notch vocals. Fantastic track!Track 3 - The Plains Truth (6:49)A quiet piano starts things off here. I believe the violin is synthesized, but it's convincing. This album is very dynamic! We get into a nice 6-8 groove here. John Baker has a nice guitar solo, making good use of delay effects. This is a wonderful instrumental track! Baker plays an acoustic solo at around 5:45 as well. Lisa LaRue shows her strengths here, not only as a terrific keyboardist, but an amazing composer and arranger. Another great piece of music! Track 4 - Quivira Bound (5:31)This begins with a prog-tastic intro with the synth in the spotlight, followed by acoustic guitar. Jake returns on vocals at around the 40 second point. I love the accents and harmonies as it approaches the chorus. This is glorious! The synth fill before the second verse is outstanding. Again, I hate to compare too much, but this really does remind me of classic Kansas. The "violin" solo could be Robbie Steinhardt. A strong guitar solo from Baker follows. I'm loving this track!Track 5 - Moving Forward (6:49)This commences with a brisk 6-8 and moves through several odd meters. This is the track on which current Kansas violinist Joe Deninzon appears, and his presence is felt early. This track will appeal to fans of prog with lots of meter changes. Joe's violin sounds like it's being fed through a distortion pedal, and even a wah-wah at times. Baker has a super-cool guitar feature after that. LaRue's piano continues to impress. Even the drum machine parts are solid and fit perfectly. This is another instrumental-only track, and it's amazing! Track 6 - The Turk - Follow the Wind (5:37)A syncopated piano part starts us off here. The vocals have adopted an accent, presumably that of "The Turk". A drum-groove and bass enter at around 1:25 to help propel the momentum. Nice change of pace into the chorus. The "violin" parts sound so realistic, I'm surprised it's not Joe Deninzon throughout the album. The solo that closes out the track is evidence of that. There are some sound effects at the tail end. This is another spectacular song!Track 7 - Nothing Is Everything (7:31)This one gets going with a high energy intro not unlike "No One Together". Again, I apologize, but this REALLY sounds like classic Kansas, while still being original?maybe it's just the setting of the music, but it really evokes that vibe. The intro consumes the first 3-minutes of the track, but I doubt anyone will mind! That was incredible! Things quiet down and become calm following the intro. There is a slow-build beginning at 3:45. I think this is another instrumental. Again, the dynamics on this album are incredible! LaRue's piano at 5:45 is nothing short of masterful. An acoustic guitar solo follows. Another stunningly awesome piece of music!Track 8 - Carved From the Sun (8:01) A mid-tempo introduction starts off this longest track. I like the bass line. The musicians have layered beautiful melodies and harmonies over the rhythm section. The tempo picks up at 1:40. This one rocks hard! Yet, that's not all it does. The arrangements throughout this album have been impressive; every bit is right where it should be. I think Jake is sitting this one out, too. Lisa and John have crafted some amazing instrumental prog here. Track 9 - Kicking Rocks (4:18)This is the track on which Evan Stanley plays. I have to say that when I learned that KISS' Paul Stanley's son was playing on this, I didn't see THAT coming! Piano and bass open the track, and the drums soon enter. Great bass line from John Baker. Evan Stanley's guitar playing is excellent. He and LaRue alternate between guitar and piano breaks. I like the blend of piano and synth. Stanley's main feature seems to be at around 3:00, and it's quite good. Track 10 - Prelude to Anywhere - Weekend Conquistadors (5:42)LaRue's fluid piano lines bring us into this track. After a cinematic opening, some short guitar riffs tease us. More masterful playing from LaRue follows. Hey, Jake's back at 2:40. He's accompanied by piano only at first, then the rest of the "band" kicks in for the chorus. And it's a great chorus at that! I love the lull then crescendo with about a minute left. Things quiet down, then there are spoken words:Male voice: "I will go to the end of the earth for that which I seek."Female voice: "True gain in life is not measured by the things we accumulate, but by the peace we possess."Awesome track!Track 11 - Still Breathing (5:58)Beautiful piano and violin take us into the final song. At around 40 seconds, big accents help amp up the energy. At 1:15, the music temporarily pauses. Shortly afterward, the beat kicks in for some wonderful melodies. I believe this is another instrumental track to close out this fabulous album. Tempo and mood changes abound! This one is quite cinematic as well. As the track fades out a horse neighs and trots off. A terrific ending!OVERALL IMPRESSIONS:I keep having to say what an amazing year this has been for prog rock! I thought 2025 was great, which it was, but this year is phenomenal! Quivira have entered the running for prog album of the year here as well! What a debut! Certainly, a contender for best new prog band! My only nit-pick is that I would have preferred a live drummer. That said, the drum machine programming is very well-done. Lisa LaRue has established herself as a premiere composer, arranger and keyboardist. I am blown away. I was already familiar with Jake from his work with his uncle and even more so with Emerald City Council, but he really knocked me out with his performances on this album; spectacular. John Baker's bass parts and, especially his acoustic solos are quite tasty. I give this a nearly perfect 4.75 out of 5 stars (95%). Fans of symphonic classic prog will love the hell out of this album!

items._cn_summary: 这是前卫摇滚乐队Quivira的首张专辑，以科罗纳多寻找黄金的土著村庄Quivira为叙事主线，采用多乐章结构和电影化的音景。键盘与弦乐营造出史诗般的开场，原声吉他与合成器独奏交错展开，主唱表现力突出，和声层次丰富，鼓编程与钢琴段落配合紧密。乐评特别强调了作品的动态起伏、编曲的完整性以及作曲家在键盘与管弦乐融合上的功力。整体属于典型的交响前卫风格，注重旋律与氛围构建，但并未突破传统前卫摇滚的框架，适合偏好叙事性摇滚的听众。

items.body: Review by alainPP — 1. "Two Roads": for the prog intro?100% spot-on?with crystalline guitar work washing over the ears and Anna's divine vocals (defying her age) channeling the style of the great Kate Bush. The atmosphere is inimitable and highly accessible, featuring Floyd-esque guitar work reminiscent of a sensitive Gary Moore, alongside flute and keyboards that evoke?however distantly?the renowned band Collage. In short, a heavyweight track in the neo-prog scene!2. "Shadows in the Dark": for the breakdown and the warm vocals of Marcin (the singer, not the guitarist); for the solemn, delicate finale featuring a melting piano and a spellbinding choir, with keyboard tones that echo the soundscapes of Vangelis.3. "Single Game": for a vibrant, colorful ballad featuring soaring, moving vocals; it shifts into an atmospheric, classical mode driven by lush keyboards, leading into a beautiful decrescendo.4. "Cheaters": featuring an intro with an electro-new-wave vibe; for the tension and the soaring guitar solo that drives this energetic track, along with a sharp riff reminiscent of Saga?in short, it's punchy and infectious. Prog is right here before you.5. "When We Played By Heart": for the return of Anna?who remains, in my view, the highlight of this album?with vocals that drift seamlessly across prog, atmospheric, and ambient spaces. Her contributions to numerous Polish bands often elevate the quality of their albums. Special mention goes to the bewitching violin that pairs perfectly with this vibrant ballad.6. "Silent Rooms": for the piano interlude showcasing Kamil's magical, fiery touch; his keyboards convey far more emotion than those of many better-known neo-prog players?which says a lot. A beautiful opening to launch...7. "Friends of Blood": featuring a guitar solo by Marcin?a top-tier guest musician. It's an accessible track; the album needed something more repetitive and melodic that truly takes flight with that stratospheric solo. ...a finale that makes you want to hit replay.8. "All About You" begins with a syrupy, Floyd-esque intro; Anna seamlessly joins in, lending this soft, melodic track a sense of tenderness and voluptuousness?indeed, a highly sexualized feel. The melody builds, exploding in hushed tones?the price paid for such musical ecstasy. It is a multi-layered track that settles into the violin before launching back into Anna's compulsive, punky, trance-like mantra as the sound unfolds. Ideal for an endless finale. (4.25)

items._cn_summary: 这张波兰乐队专辑以新前卫摇滚为基底，在八首曲目中展开丰富的声音层次。女声带有Kate Bush式的戏剧张力，男声温暖，吉他段落兼具Floyd式空间感与更抒情的气质，键盘和合成器营造出Vangelis式的宏大氛围。曲目在摇滚、古典、ambient与new-wave之间游走，钢琴间奏、小提琴对奏、合唱段落与爆裂的吉他独奏交替出现，形成从静谧到激昂的动态起伏。人声与器乐编排细腻，部分篇章融入迷幻和trance般的律动，整体具备流畅的旋律性与精致的编曲结构。

items.body: Cabaret Voltaire have released the 7-inch version of “Don’t Argue”, the second track lifted from the remastered reissue of their 1987 album “CODE”, out 9 October on Mute. The Sheffield electronic duo’s original recording was produced by Cabaret Voltaire with Adrian Sherwood and built around vocal samples from Frank Capra’s 1945 short film “Your Job In Germany”. It reached the UK Singles Chart on its original release. The track follows the John Robie dub mix of “Thank You America”, shared in July when Mute announced the remastered “CODE” reissue. Out of print for years, the album returns on limited edition “CODIFIED” marble vinyl and as a triple CD set, the latter adding two discs of remastered period remixes plus unreleased mixes found in the archive. Both editions carry new sleeve notes on the album’s production and its afterlife. The 7-inch version of “Don’t Argue” sits on disc two, alongside the Hate and Destroy Mix and the single mix of the same track. “CODE” was recorded at the band’s Western Works studio in Sheffield, with Sherwood joining for pre-production before sessions moved to Red Bus in London for mixing. Guest players include saxophonist Simeon Lister, bassist Mark Brydon of Chakk and Bill Nelson of Be-Bop Deluxe. Denis Blackman handled the remaster; work on the reissue began in 2019 with Richard H. Kirk and was completed after his death using his notes, in consultation with Stephen Mallinder and Kirk’s estate. Cabaret Voltaire tour dates in 2026 Stephen Mallinder and Chris Watson close the run they began in 2025 for the 50th anniversary of the band’s first performance. I Speak Machine supports the North American leg, Gazelle Twin most of the UK dates and Fader the two Welsh and south-west English shows. 11 September – Dallas, TX (US), Granada Theater, with I Speak Machine 15 September – Chicago, IL (US), Metro, with I Speak Machine 16 September – Chicago, IL (US), Metro, with I Speak Machine 18 September – Toronto, ON (Canada), Phoenix Concert Theatre, with I Speak Machine 19 September – Montreal, QC (Canada), SAT, with I Speak Machine 21 September – Boston, MA (US), The Wilbur, with I Speak Machine 25 September – New York, NY (US), Knockdown Center, with I Speak Machine 26 September – Philadelphia, PA (US), Underground Arts, with I Speak Machine 7 October – Dublin (Ireland), The Academy 8 October – Belfast (UK), Limelight 10 October – Birmingham (UK), Town Hall, with Gazelle Twin 11 October – Liverpool (UK), Arts Club, with Gazelle Twin 13 October – Nottingham (UK), The Palais, with Gazelle Twin 14 October – Cardiff (UK), The Globe, with Fader 15 October – Bath (UK), Forum, with Fader 17 October – Newcastle (UK), Boiler Shop, with Gazelle Twin 18 October – Glasgow (UK), Barrowland, with Gazelle Twin 19 October – Manchester (UK), Albert Hall, with Gazelle Twin 21 October – Brighton (UK), Chalk, with Gazelle Twin 22 October – London (UK), Roundhouse, with Gazelle Twin 25 October – Sheffield (UK), Octagon, with Gazelle Twin – sold out About Cabaret Voltaire Cabaret Voltaire formed in Sheffield in 1973 around Richard H. Kirk, Stephen Mallinder and Chris Watson, working with tape manipulation, electronics and found sound well before the equipment caught up with the idea. Watson left in 1981. Kirk and Mallinder continued as a duo, signing to EMI in the mid-1980s and issuing “CODE” in 1987, the album that produced their two UK chart singles, “Don’t Argue” and “Here To Go”. The pair wound the project down in 1994. Kirk later carried the name alone, performing at Berlin’s Atonal festival in 2014 and issuing the connected run of “Shadow of Fear”, “BN9Drone” and “Dekadrone” across 2020 and 2021. He died in autumn 2021. Mallinder and Watson returned to the stage in 2025 to mark 50 years since the band’s first performance, a run that included a Roundhouse booking for 2026 and continued into this year around the live album “But What Time Is It Really?”, from which the pair also shared a live “Yashar”. The “CODE” reissue lands three weeks into that final tour.

Kirk在2019年的工作，并由Stephen Mallinder及其遗产管理机构共同完成。文章还列出了乐队2026年纪念首演五十周年的巡演日程。整体而言，这是一篇偏重发行信息与历史背景的新闻稿，适合关注工业电子经典再版与现场演出的乐迷。

items.body: Belgian cold wave and EBM duo Parade Ground put their 1988 debut album “Cut Up” back on vinyl on 4 September through VUZ Records, in three 180-gram colour pressings of 100 copies each: clear glass, clear orange and clear orange smoke. Each carries a lyrics inlay. The same day brings two pressings of the companion album “Remixes”, on smoked grey and opaque white, again limited to 100 copies apiece. Cut Up by Parade Ground “Cut Up” was the first full-length from brothers Jean-Marc and Pierre Pauly, originally issued by PIAS. The record was cut at A.B.S. Studio in Brussels, with the exception of “Moans”, recorded at Daylight Studio and produced by Wire‘s Colin Newman, who also plays guitar and synthesizer and sings backing vocals on it. Jean-Marc Pauly handles vocals, guitar and keyboard, Pierre Pauly bass, keyboards, percussion and backing vocals. Daniel Caron wrote the music for “Cut Up The Neck-Tie”. The nine tracks run “Hollywood”, “Modern Hunting”, “I Will Talk”, “Moans”, “Moist Hands”, “Such Is The Bow”, “Cut Up The Neck-Tie”, “Cut-Throat Business” and “Strange World”. The album sits close to the Belgian electronic scene that produced Front 242, with whose members the brothers kept working ties, but its combination of stark electronics, post-punk guitar and studio experiment stayed its own thing. Parade Ground’s ‘Remixes’ collects eight Peter Rainman reworks The “Remixes” LP gathers eight tracks from across the back catalogue reworked by French producer Peter Rainman, who records as People Theatre and has remixed for Apoptygma Berzerk, Chinese Theatre and Psyche. Rather than take the originals apart, Rainman keeps their arrangements and atmosphere and adds new textures and rhythms. The running order is “Moan on the Sly (People Theatre’s Catch Mix)”, “The Net (People Theatre’s Vault Mix)”, “I shut My Eyes (People Theatre’s Optic Mix)”, “Took Advantage (People Theatre’s Favour Mix)”, “Gold Rush (People Theatre’s Klondike Mix)”, “A Day at the Park (People Theatre’s Footsteps Mix)”, “Retired (People Theatre’s Laugh Mix)” and “Strange World (People Theatre’s Airplane And Crash Mix)”. Side-Line covered the collection when it arrived as the second 45th anniversary release in April 2026. About Parade Ground Parade Ground started in Brussels in 1981 as a duo of brothers Jean-Marc Pauly on vocals and Pierre Pauly on bass and keyboards. A run of maxi-singles between 1983 and 1987 came before “Cut Up”, their 1988 debut album for PIAS, recorded largely at A.B.S. Studio and marked by Colin Newman’s production work on “Moans”. “The 15th Floor” followed in 1989, though it only reached CD in 2021. The brothers kept the project going in bursts: “Sanctuary” arrived in 2018 in a run of 300 copies, their first live album “Life (Live in Frankfurt)” in June 2019, and 2007’s “Rosary” returned as a download in December 2021. The 336-page book “Words Sword Words”, issued with a CD, appeared in July 2024. Jean-Marc Pauly set out the pair’s working aim in a 2019 Side-Line interview. VUZ Records has handled the recent catalogue work, from the archival compilation “Heaven With Care” in October 2025 through the 45th anniversary items of 2026: the “Strange World” 3-inch CD-R and digital edition in February and “Remixes” in April. The 4 September pressings extend that anniversary run to vinyl.

items.body: Pyrroline released the video for “Day 45” on 25 August 2026, the ninth track on the electro-industrial and old-school EBM duo’s sixth album “Ambiguity”, out since 17 July 2026 on Electro Aggression Records as a Digipak CD and digitally. The label describes the track as addressing the war in Ukraine. “Ambiguity” runs twelve tracks: “Ambiguity”, “Transition Fault”, “Ulysses”, “Britzelgritzel”, “Eventually”, “Already Defined?”, “Crossroads of Progress”, “It’s all for Nothing”, “Day 45”, “Relentless (feat. TC75)”, “Stay Away” and “Inner Resonance”. Pyrroline wrote, produced and performed the album themselves. TC75‘s Tino Claus contributes guest vocals to “Relentless”, and the lyrics of “Stay Away” draw on Dylan Thomas, James Whitcomb Riley and Lord Alfred Tennyson. Ambiguity by PYRROLINE The album follows the double CD “Struggling” by five years, and moves through transition, doubt, technological change and the effects of war. The label describes the record as combining “cold synthetic textures, driving rhythms and atmospheric soundscapes with lyrics that remain deliberately open, fragmented and tense”. About Pyrroline Pyrroline is an electro-industrial and old-school EBM duo built around Arnte on vocals and Schmoun on synths and chants. The project records for Electro Aggression Records, the label founded in 2011 that concentrates on old-school EBM and electronic body music, and has stayed with it across its full-length run. Side-Line covered the CD album “In The Dawn Of Freedom” in September 2017 and the double CD “Struggling” in May 2021, the latter the duo’s fifth album. The sixth album “Ambiguity” was announced in June 2026 and shipped the following month. “Day 45” is the latest clip taken from it.

items.body: The American duo Magic Wands—comprising Dexy Valentine (guitar, keyboards, vocals) and Chris Valentine (guitar, vocals)—have already released several notable albums and returned this spring with this six-track EP. It features three new songs alongside three familiar tracks presented in a fresh guise. Magic Wands remain true to their musical identity, carefully blending Dream-Pop with a touch of Shoegaze. The guitar remains the musical highlight, creating a distinctive, dreamy atmosphere while adding a certain zest to the songs. Synths introduce an extra melodic—and at times melancholic—touch to the overall sound. Add to this the dry snare drums reminiscent of the golden era of the 80s and Dexy’s lovely, ethereal vocals, and the result is simply superb. I was particularly impressed by the first two tracks, both of which are new material. The opening track hints at Dark-Wave, yet that dark, dreamy quality remains the band’s trademark. The familiar tracks include the former single “Sacred Mirrors” (featuring Psychedelic Furs guitarist John Ashton), a remastered version of “Wishing Well,” and a remix of “Golden” (originally from their previous album). While these are all good songs, they fall just a notch below the two opening tracks, with “Starline” standing out as my absolute favorite. Magic Wands continue to do what they do best: cool Dream-Pop. (Rating:7½). Listen to “Starline”: Starline by Magic Wands About Magic Wands Magic Wands is a dream pop duo from Los Angeles, California, formed by Dexy Valentine (guitar, keyboards, vocals) and Chris Valentine (guitar, vocals). The project started in 2007 with the single “Teenage Love”. The debut album “Aloha Moon” appeared in 2011, followed by “Jupiter” in 2015, the “Lazer Bitch” 7-inch on Cleopatra in 2016, “Abrakadabra” in 2018 and the self-released “Illuminate” in 2020. The duo moved to Metropolis Records, which issued the singles “Joy” and “Time” and the album “Switch” in 2023, followed by the remix album “Switched”. “Hide” and “Armour” came in 2024, and “Across The Water”, “Time To Dream” and the LP “Cascades” in 2025. “Wishing Well” is the duo’s six-track EP for the label.
items._genre: dream pop / shoegaze / darkwave
items._cn_summary: 这张EP收录三首新歌与三首旧作的新版本，延续了乐队一贯的梦幻流行与自赏风格。吉他声部构成核心亮点，通过混响与音墙营造出朦胧而富有层次的氛围，同时为歌曲增添灵动感。合成器在整体音色中融入旋律性与一丝忧郁，配合干练的军鼓音色和女主唱飘渺的人声，形成该乐队标志性的暗色梦幻质感。开场两首新曲较为突出，其中一首带有暗潮倾向，另一首《Starline》则成为整张EP中最具吸引力的作品。旧作部分包括单曲《Sacred Mirrors》、重制版《Wishing Well》及《Golden》的混音版，质量略低于新曲，但整体保持了一贯的创作水准。EP适合喜欢梦幻流行、自赏以及带有80年代气息暗色旋律的听众。

items.body: Do you feel regret Do you even know my name… Ahead of the September 18 release of Get Mean, Boy Harsher have unveiled “Tough Luck (When You Don’t Call),” the third advance single from their first new album since the 2022 film and soundtrack The Runner. The song finds Jae Matthews trying to maintain the appearance of composure while an unanswered telephone turns distance into rejection, doubt, and the humiliating fear of having been forgotten. An uneasy synth introduction quickly opens into a brisk new-wave dance beat, with a firm kick, rounded bass, bright keyboards, and clipped bursts of distorted guitar giving the track a warmer and more openly pop-minded character. Matthews sings in a heartbroken drawl that seems to drag against the arrangement’s forward motion. The contrast makes the song feel almost euphoric at first, although every melodic lift carries another reminder that the person she wants remains absent. “Tough Luck (When You Don’t Call)” is a song that could have occupied late-night radio in the mid-1980s, when sleek synthesizers, post-punk guitar, and bruised romanticism regularly met inside a four-minute single. Boy Harsher retain the uncanny atmosphere that has always accompanied their music, yet the unease here is romantic and immediate: the sort of private crisis that can accompany a night drive while the road continues forward with far more certainty than the relationship. The verses are built from questions sent into silence. Faith has waned, time has been lost, and Jae questions whether the person on the other end feels regret or even remembers her. The plea “Do you even know my name?” cuts deep, as recognition is now the least she expects. In response to this fear, the repeated assurance “I’m OK” increasingly resembles a rehearsed line, seemingly for the benefit of the one saying it. The official lyric video transforms that rehearsal into an analog karaoke experience. Made using vintage video gear by Los Angeles video artist Sean McGuirk and shot at PropHaus Brooklyn by Jesse Korman, it keeps the camera focused on the curved glass of an old CRT television in a dimly lit room. The screen displays a cold blue background with thick yellow letters appearing beneath rolling scan lines, bowed edges, and concentric patterns created by photographing a cathode-ray display. Its opening card resembles a selection from a home karaoke catalogue: “IN THE STYLE OF,” followed by the artist, title, and parenthetical subtitle. From that point, the lyrics move across the blue background in uppercase, with parts of each line fading, smearing, or bleaching toward white alongside the vocal cues. The abbreviations “U,” “YR,” and “N” mimic the shorthand of text messaging, yet they appear on a television from an earlier technological era. Thus, a song about failed communication is conveyed through two outdated mediums: the silent, unanswered phone and the solitary glow of a karaoke machine. McGuirk also leaves the machinery’s awkward instructions intact. Cards reading “INSTRUMENTAL BREAK” interrupt the lyrics with dry literalism, while the chorus is broken into syllabic prompts that make Matthews’ faltering reassurance available for anyone to sing. Karaoke usually transforms private listening into a social performance; here, there is no visible room, microphone, or gathering of friends. The viewer faces only the television and the uneasy invitation to inhabit the singer’s denial. The absence of performers becomes the video’s central image. Matthews is heard but never seen, much as the person she addresses exists only through the failure to make contact. The warm momentum of the music presses against the cool television light until the screen returns to its title card at the end, ready to begin the selection again. That reset gives the waiting a circular quality: another call can go unanswered, another chorus can insist that everything is fine, and the machine will remain prepared to repeat the performance. Watch the lyric video for Tough Luck (When You Don’t Call) below: Stream “Tough Luck (When You Don’t Call)” across digital services here. Get Mean began during a period when the continuation of Boy Harsher was far from assured. In early 2024, after years of international touring and increasingly ambitious work across music and film, Matthews and Augustus Muller ended their romantic relationship. The separation followed personal turmoil, family loss, and a creative block that left both the band and the prospect of another album uncertain. Writing resumed when Matthews took to the road, moving through West Texas, the Pacific Northwest, South Florida, and points between. That unsettled geography became part of the album itself. Described as Boy Harsher’s “road album,” Get Mean was recorded across eight locations in the United States, Mexico, and Italy, gathering cellphone voice notes, environmental recordings, and changing emotional states along the way. Matthews describes the album as: “what I had to give during the most extreme period of my life.” Across its twelve tracks, the duo’s familiar coldwave momentum meets detuned pads, abrasive synth leads, pedal-steel bends, New Romantic guitar, percussive jokes, and unadorned phone recordings. Those additions allow grief and exhaustion to coexist with flirtation, humor, and the possibility of beginning again. The album follows the collapse of one form of intimacy while testing whether another—the creative bond between Matthews and Muller—can survive it. Get Mean arrives September 18 via Atlantic Records. Pre-order and pre-save the album here. GET MEAN by Boy Harsher Matthews and Muller formed Boy Harsher in 2014 after meeting while studying film in Savannah. Their first EP, Lesser Man, began as a small cassette release before “Pain” spread widely online. The duo followed it with Yr Body Is Nothing in 2016, the Country Girl EP in 2017, and Careful in 2019. Their filmmaking background came fully into view with The Runner, the 2022 horror film and accompanying soundtrack that they wrote, produced, directed, and scored. Their cinematic work continues with The Lonely Woman, their forthcoming feature-length horror thriller starring Chloë Sevigny, FKA twigs, Sturgill Simpson, Will Oldham, and Jake Weary. Boy Harsher are directing the film and providing its score. Following the release of Get Mean, Boy Harsher will begin an extensive North American headline tour before continuing through Europe and the United Kingdom with support from Choir Boy. The itinerary includes sold-out two-night runs in Chicago and Portland, a sold-out Los Angeles appearance at the Hollywood Palladium, and newly sold-out dates in Denver, Paris, Glasgow, and Bristol. items.body: Most fantasies of quitting preserve some faith in manners: a resignation letter, a slammed drawer, a final walk past reception. Mighty Crimes tears through that decorum with a workplace homicide and a car pointed toward open country. Yet escape does not clear the mind. The office recedes while the argument continues in the driver’s seat, where relief, panic, and self-justification take turns holding the wheel. London post-punk band Blow Dry, the project conceived and led by Sydney-born frontwoman Genevieve Welsh, have shared their off-kilter video for Mighty Crimes. Released on July 28 and co-written with Jorge Elbrecht—whose credits include Japanese Breakfast, Sky Ferreira, and Angel Olsen—the song turns an under-the-breath workplace fantasy into fugitive comedy. Sick of corporate life, a woman kills her boss, runs for the horizon, and gradually loses command of her own explanation. A spring-loaded bass line opens the track, with clipped guitar accents and post-punk jangles darting around percussion that carries the fleet, slightly camp momentum of a 1960s heist score. An eerie rising-and-falling figure, poised somewhere between an organ buzz and a guitar whine, keeps the floor tilted beneath Welsh’s theatrical delivery. Her voice purrs, quivers, yelps, and steadily pushes toward the edge as each repetition makes the character sound less convinced by her own defence. Welsh explains: “On the surface it’s a relatable laugh – ugh, I want to kill my boss – I mean, how many people have said that before?! But there are real emotions under the humour too: the freedom and release of throwing everything away and heading out into the unknown, tangled up with the anxiety of ‘what have I done,’ and then comes the self-talk you do to convince yourself that yes you were right to make the choices you’ve made… whether you actually were or not. Or at least, that’s the mental olympics my brain goes through. It’s such a playful track combined with the Blow Dry dark humour – as soon as we recorded it I could see the imagery – a Thelma & Louise meets Tarantino meets Priscilla, Queen of the Desert getaway film, but set in the Australian outback. An off-kilter homage to my homeland.” Speaking with Eliot Odgers for Still Listening Magazine, Welsh said that writing through a fictional character “let me detach and have more fun.” The small crew followed a similar instinct while filming in Western Australia: “No permissions, a rough plan, and the rest we were winging.” Directed by Blair Gauld, with cinematography by Ryan Murphy and grading by Spike Luke Wright, the video carries the song’s office-crime premise into the red vastness surrounding Kalgoorlie. Welsh’s outlaw stands against burnt-orange earth and an immense blue sky, her white clothing and wind-tossed hair cutting across the Goldfields landscape. The Coolgardie Caravan Park and Broad Arrow Tavern anchor the getaway in a specific corner of Western Australia. Meat pies, a Bunnings hat, skimpy-bar culture, and other slices of Australiana bring homesick affection and dry comedy to the flight. With only three people travelling and filming, the clip retains the looseness of its production: a desert crime picture assembled through roadside encounters, local generosity, and the willingness to see what might happen next. Watch the video for Mighty Crimes below: Blow Dry brings Welsh’s background in fashion and love of cinema into a theatrical strain of post-punk informed by punk rock, new wave, and gothic rock. The group’s recent single MR. BIG introduced its more confrontational side through an aggressive, dance-led performance video; Mighty Crimes widens the frame into character-driven film and black comedy. Alongside stylist Matt King, Welsh also runs Tainted Pleasure, a Blitz Club-inspired night held at The Social in London. Mighty Crimes is out now. Listen on Spotify and Apple Music.
