items.body: You know it felt like a war, hungover on a parquet floor But now it’s like I hardly think about you anymore Adulthood is an exercise in presentation. We learn the correct expressions and develop plausible explanations for why the compromises we once feared are now signs of wisdom. On Desperate Journalist‘s Terrible Years, the lead single from the London quartet’s sixth album, Gilding the Lily, lead singer Jo Bevan turns that performance into a social comedy, complete with escape, panic, and the suspicion that maturity may simply be youth with better excuses. The song begins with Rob Hardy’s verse progression and expands into three minutes of crowded guitars, orchestral synths, and a rhythm section that keeps pressing forward as though hesitation might expose somebody. Simon Drowner’s bass and Caz Helbert’s drums give the track an eager gait, while Hardy’s guitar has the bright edge and density that made Desperate Journalist recognizable. After the sparse, industrial cast of No Hero, the arrangement feels luxuriant and busy, capped by a chiming middle eight whose sweetness sharpens the song’s mockery rather than softening it. “This is one of the last songs we wrote for the album,” Bevan explains. “Rob had a kernel of an idea for the verse chord progression and we all goaded him into basically writing all the rest of the music one day at rehearsal. Lyrically it’s from the perspective of a character who’s cashed in and moved to LA or somewhere exotic, and is mistakenly under the impression that they are now blissfully balanced (and definitely not in denial about how much they miss the chaos and excitement of their youth). It’s sort of sympathetic but also caustic, as they’re lording it over the people they used to know whilst still clearly being a bit of a mess and scared of how old they’ve become. A lot of this album is about the horror of becoming aware of your own mortality – but, you know, in a fun way.” Bevan sings from inside a personality built to advertise success, allowing vanity and fear to occupy the same immaculate room. The character has escaped, cashed in, moved somewhere sunny, and achieved the balance everyone else failed to find. Yet every boast carries the faint desperation of a holiday photograph posted for an audience of former friends. Jez Leather’s performance video, filmed with warm lights in a white room, gives the song an uncluttered frame. The band plays with a directness that suits its raucous construction, leaving Bevan’s words to supply the psychological mess. Watch the video for Terrible Years below: Desperate Journalist are a London post-punk quartet comprising vocalist Jo Bevan, guitarist Rob Hardy, bassist Simon Drowner, and drummer Caz Helbert. Across five albums, the band have paired richly layered guitars and propulsive rhythms with Bevan’s incisive lyrics, gradually incorporating the electronic and industrial textures heard on 2024’s No Hero. Their forthcoming sixth album, Gilding the Lily, continues that evolution while preserving the melodic force and emotional candor at the heart of their work. As an introduction to Gilding the Lily, due out on November 20 through Fierce Panda Records, Terrible Years suggests Desperate Journalist are fascinated by the humiliations hidden inside self-possession: the older we become, the more elaborate our methods for pretending we have arrived. items.body: Julian Asher sings “Elohim” as an invocation of divine power reclaiming a throne, both a “He” and a “She” arriving “in full power” to “take His place upon the ancient seat” among “those who lead astray and cheat.” The song draws its title from the Hebrew name for God and threads it through Rastafari language, addressing Abba and Selassie I directly across the verses. Asher is a South African singer rooted in Rastafari belief, splitting his time between South Africa and Berlin, where he currently lives. He has spent years working with Downtown Steppas, the Berlin-based reggae backing band and riddim makers, built out of the same rehearsal-room and live sessions that shaped this song. “Elohim” comes from Just Cause, the pair’s debut album, recorded last winter and drawn from material the two had been playing together for years. items.body: Honestly, I didn't know what to expect from this release. My relationship with Russian Circles has been fraught, to say the least. Some of their music is pure genius to me, trendsetting to the full extent of the term. It's safe to say that modern post-metal and post-rock wouldn't look the same without them. But then there are years and years of material which I personally did not find impactful. It's not that it was bad, it was just...weightless. Which is funny to say about one of the bands that are most famous for being present, heavy, weightful, especially in the spaces of post-metal which suffer from much abstraction and "ambience". But that was just it; that undefinable spark that made the early Russian Circles material seemed absent. Everything was technically there but the arrangement fell flat.And so, I approached Nine with some trepidation. Happily, all my concerns were proven to be misplaced. Nine feels like Russian Circles reborn, refocused on what made them tick as a band. But it's a not a re-tread; on the contrary, it is quite different to the band's previous releases. Don't get me wrong, it's definitely Russian Circles. We are still talking about heavy, patient, instrumental metal. The tones are still dark and brooding. But there's a lot more in there; there are electronic touches which do wonders for the groove of certain tracks. There are riffs which move with a purpose, mixing things up from just "weight" with feelings of aggression and forward momentum. The formula is the same but Russian Circles feel mean on this release, hungry like they haven't in a while."Empath", the second track on the album, is probably my favorite example. It opens with this haunting, buzz-saw like synth line and almost immediately blows up into one of the most swaggersome (swaggerful?) riff of the band's career. It's hard to overstate how much this riff goes hard. It's not just that the guitars are tight as all hell, that the bass rumbles in just the right way, or that the cymbals are pure, crashing joy. It's that everything feels purposeful. Nothing is there just to be there, to be scaffolding. It's all lean and no fat. I am aware this is entirely subject; we're talking about je ne sais quoi here, "the juice", as the kids call it. Everything just feels like it has it, the rock n' roll impact, that metal heft. And then it goes heavier; the riff which ushers "Empathy" out is the angriest I've heard Russian Circles. The riff just repeats and repeats, swirling around some black and red abyss of rage and outcry.Things feel better even when the band does go atmospheric, like on "Meridian". This is more of a classically constructed Russian Circles track, made up of builds ups and crescendos. But there too, Russian Circles sound like a band revitalized - the bass lines which make up the majority of the track's substance are delicious and the building up instruments feel vital and secure, pointed towards a well understood and executed direction. Of course, it's "obvious" that Russian Circles can execute a track like this well; it's their bread and butter. But, again, something feels more right than before, more present and demanding. You're not zoning out listening to the buildup; it has you arrested.I don't know what has spurred this new fire in the band but, whatever is it, I salute them for it. It's not easy to keep pushing and rethinking your approach after twenty-two years of operation and nine albums. Russian Circles have done it; Nine feels like an album worthy of their legend, a recommitment to the ideas at the base of the band alongside a new way to bring them forth. Here's to nine more. Nine by Russian Circles
items._genre: post-metal / post-rock / instrumental metal / electronic
items._cn_summary: 乐评者坦言与Russian Circles过往关系复杂，早期作品天才但后期常显失重空洞。新专辑《Nine》则令其改观，认为乐队仿佛重生，重新聚焦于自身核心驱动力。专辑依然保留厚重、沉稳的器乐金属基调，音色黑暗低沉，但加入了更多电子触点，显著提升部分曲目的律动感。吉他段落更具指向性，在纯粹重量之外注入攻击性与前行动力。例如第二首《Empath》以阴森锯齿状合成器音色开场，随后爆发乐队生涯中最具威慑力的连复段，结尾陷入反复回旋的愤怒深渊。即便是偏氛围化的《Meridian》，贝斯线条与层层递进的器乐编排也显示出焕然一新的生命力。整体上，这是一张在既有框架内重新找回锋芒与目的性的回归之作。

items._cn_summary: Punch Brothers在Brittany Haas加入后的首张专辑，也是乐队成立以来的首张全器乐作品。全碟11曲中仅有一首正统蓝草，其余作品以所谓“前卫蓝草”为核心，将蓝草乐器的即兴张力与古典室内流行的精致编曲融合，甚至加入布吉节奏元素。三首传统曲目被重新演绎，但整体更强调原创性的器乐叙事。小提琴取代人声成为旋律主导，在密集的拨弦与拉奏中穿梭，既保留蓝草音乐的技术性，又拓展了类型边界。这张专辑展现了乐队对器乐表现力的探索，以及蓝草音乐向更复杂、更具实验性方向延展的可能。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 这张丹麦三人乐队GuldGanger的处女EP以数字形式发行，由经验丰富的北欧民谣歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首作品大多基于传统曲目，但乐队以个人化视角重新诠释，整体弥漫着古老而略带粗粝的质感。开场的《Svennedal》以奔放的节奏展现歌者的感染力，口弦和风笛在《Nordgård》中形成持续推进力，而《Agnete Af Bjergmanden》里的钦巴龙则提供了精致背景。器乐作品《Ormsö》让口弦与长笛、弦乐交织出偏离常规的声响，显示出乐队对音色层次与神秘氛围的掌控力。虽仅五首，但已能感受到这支乐队成熟且完整的艺术面貌，是值得关注的北欧民谣新声。

items.body: Yendri, the Hamburg electro and darkwave project of Nina Cording, has not released an album since “Bitter” on 26 June 2011. Across the previous decade the project put out eight studio albums on Matrix Cube and Rudy Ratzinger’s Mental Ulcer Forges, and Cording’s remixes appeared on record after record by :wumpscut:. Then the releases stopped. In a new interview with Side-Line, Cording explains what happened after that, why she now works mainly under the Machinespirit name, and how likely it is that anything new appears under the Yendri banner. Her answer to the last question is short: “No, not really.” She has not stopped making music, though. Machinespirit’s most recent track, “X26”, went up on 18 August 2026, nine days before this interview was published. Bitter by Yendri Yendri interview: Nina Cording on the quiet years SL: Yendri was very active throughout the 2000s, but after “Bitter” in 2011 the project became much quieter. What changed for you around that time? “It was harder to find a way to publish the music and I didn’t want to run my own label (like for example, Rudy Ratzinger, who runs his own label), and the project was too small to justify it. Also it has to do with the 2nd question.” SL: You later released music under your own name and as Machinespirit. How do those projects differ from Yendri, both musically and personally? “The difference is mainly that it’s not as dark anymore maybe. Still can be, but it’s not a ‘default setting’ anymore ;-), and only rarely with vocals. It’s just electronic music in any direction I like to go. Personally this also gives me more freedom.” SL: Looking back at the Yendri catalogue now, which album or period still feels closest to who you are today, and which one feels the most distant? “I think the later ones are quite close, from ‘Malfunction’ to ‘Bitter’.” SL: You were always interested in programming, technology and electronic music. Has your work with technology changed the way you compose or think about music in recent years? “Of course, making music is also a bit like programming and I like nerdy stuff. That’s why I switched to Reaper as a DAW later. There you can have some quirky configurations, but it’s also ergonomically challenging. Cubase, which I used before, feels much easier to use. But then, I also hated dongles very much and wanted to make music on the laptop without this thing blocking one of the precious USB ports (especially if you have an audio interface which doesn’t like hanging on a hub).” SL: Do you still consider Yendri an active project, and is there any chance of new music, reissues, or previously unreleased material appearing in the future? “No, not really. But there is a small chance of reissues, even though just a (literal) handful of people would even notice it.” SL: How have have things been for you lately? “The last year I was occupied fighting cancer, so I didn’t make much music. And then I spent much time with my mother who died in March this year. My therapy was successful so far and my hair grew back, but it’s curly now and I actually like it very much. I keep most of it out of social media, after all I’m a nerdy geek that’s not too much into social interaction ;-)” About Yendri Yendri is the electronic project of Nina Cording, based in Hamburg, Germany, and running since 1999. Its first appearances were on compilations that year, including Orkus’ “Goths’ Paradise III” and the “Bizarre 12” cassette, and the project’s catalogue kept a close relationship with the German compilation circuit throughout: Yendri tracks turned up on Depeche Mode, The Cure and Nine Inch Nails tribute sets between 2000 and 2001, on “Cryonica Tanz V.1” and on several volumes of Zoomshot’s “Schattentanz” and “Der Seelen Tiefengrund” series. The albums began in 2000 with “Inhaliere Meine Seele Und Stirb” and “Breakdown Of Reality”, both CDs on Matrix Cube, which also issued “Fluch Und Segen” in 2003. From 2006 the project moved to Mental Ulcer Forges for a run of five albums: “Playdoll” (2006), “Malfunction” (2007), “Dreams Of An Undead Girl” (2008), “Broken World” (2009) and “Destination Oblivion” (2010). Several arrived with separate bonus download sets. The last two Yendri releases came in 2011, the “Cherry Blossoms & Samegame EP” on Audiomagnet and the fifteen-track “Bitter” on 26 June, which Cording issued herself. Alongside her own records Cording built up a long remix credit list, most of it for :wumpscut:. Yendri remixes appear on “Evoke” (2005), “Cannibal Anthem” (2006), the “Body Census” and “DJ Dwarf Seven” releases (2007), “Fuckit” (2009), “Women And Satan First” (2012) and “Bulwark Bazooka” (2014), which means the Yendri name kept surfacing on other people’s records for three years after her own albums stopped. Rudy Ratzinger, who runs :wumpscut: and its Beton Kopf Media label, is the example she reaches for above when explaining why she did not start a label of her own. Cording now records as Machinespirit, whose Bandcamp catalogue holds the albums “Yin”, “Yang”, “4 of those”, the “5XMU EP” and the archival “Subsonic I (1997)”, alongside a long list of standalone tracks including “Live your life” (2021), “Mellow 4” (2023), “FM8 Mallet” (December 2025) and “X26” (18 August 2026). It is, by her own description above, less consistently dark than Yendri and only rarely uses vocals. Yendri itself she now describes as inactive, with reissues the only opening she leaves.

items._cn_summary: 本篇为汉堡电子与暗潮项目Yendri的访谈报道，主创Nina Cording回顾了2011年专辑《Bitter》之后长达十余年的沉寂期。Cording解释了当年停止发行的原因——缺乏合适的发行渠道且不愿自营厂牌，同时项目体量不足以支撑独立运营。此后她转向以本名及Machinespirit名义发表作品，音乐方向不再以暗色调为默认设定，转向更自由的电子音乐探索，偶尔加入人声，偏好在Reaper DAW中进行个性化配置以追求技术层面的灵活性。Cording明确表示Yendri基本处于停滞状态，仅有小概率发行再版。整篇文章以问答形式呈现，提供了关于厂牌运营、创作工具迁移及项目定位转变的一手信息，但缺乏对音乐本身的深度乐评分析。

items.body: “Our Love Will Live Forever” had its title before the event that made those words much harder to take literally. Jason Corbett took the phrase from his grandparents’ tombstone; only later, during the writing and recording of the album, a serious cardiac emergency forced him to consider whether he would finish the record at all, or return to the stage. His answer in this interview is strikingly unsentimental: “There is no permanence, there is no forever.” That does not negate the title so much as change the problem underneath it. “Our Love Will Live Forever”, ACTORS‘ third full-length album, due 4 September 2026 through Artoffact Records, becomes less about permanence as a promise than about what can remain meaningful once permanence itself is no longer credible. The new material emerged through “CTRL”, “Left On Read” and “Youth”, while Corbett’s enforced interruption gave the record a context he could not have planned when he began it. What is equally interesting, however, is how little Corbett wants to intellectualise his own process after the fact. Again and again, questions about control, rhythmic contradiction, genre or emotional design lead him back to instinct: the beat comes first, a song is left alone until it can be heard afresh, and technical decisions survive only if they produce an emotional reaction. Shannon Hemmett, meanwhile, gives the album’s central idea a visual counterpart through a star adapted from an engraving on medieval armour. The conversation moves between mortality and process, instant communication and old anxieties, authorship inside a four-person band, and what comes after the European tour. Youth by ACTORS Karo: “Our Love Will Live Forever” existed before the album acquired its most difficult context: the words come from your grandparents’ tombstone, and you had already chosen them before the cardiac emergency interrupted the record. I find that chronology fascinating because the sentence remained exactly the same while your relationship to it changed completely. When you returned to the album, did you feel that you were now making a different record underneath the same title? Jason: Yes and no. There were definitely challenges to this album that I had not experienced before. When you are forced to take a break like that, you can’t help but reevaluate your motivation and intentions. At the end of the day, there is no permanence, there is no forever. I’m lucky to be here making music. Karo: The cardiac emergency was serious enough that you were asking yourself whether you would finish the album or ever return to the stage. I’m less interested in the shock itself than in what happened when you went back to work. Did it change your threshold for what was worth keeping? Did anything suddenly feel too clever, too guarded or simply too unimportant to spend time on once not finishing the record had become a real possibility? Jason: It took some time for me to recalibrate and get my direction again. If anything, the whole situation gave me perspective. You can’t take yourself so seriously that it becomes stifling. The songs come from somewhere inside and outside of myself. I chose to continue trusting in my process. Karo: The album first became visible through “CTRL”, “Left On Read” and “Youth”, and to me they initially occupy quite different emotional spaces: compulsion and control, digitally prolonged rejection, then memory and the passage of time. Once they became parts of the same album, did you discover a connection between them that perhaps was not obvious while you were writing the individual songs? Jason: The songs naturally connect. Even the previous two albums were written over lengthy periods of time but were still cohesive. The commonality is that it’s all through my lens. That ties the music together. Karo: ACTORS are constantly described as “modern post-punk”, but I sometimes think “modern” has become one of those adjectives that explains almost nothing, particularly now that post-punk itself is such an established musical language. You’ve also said that you think less and less about genre. So what actually makes ACTORS contemporary to you now? Is it production, emotional language, technology, or simply the freedom not to treat the past as a set of instructions? Jason: Genre has become even more prevalent with the advent of streaming. We use modern post-punk as a recognisable jumping-off point for newcomers to our music. I think we operate artistically in the spirit of the first generation of post-punk, but we definitely have one foot firmly planted in the now. I don’t think about what other artists are doing. I’m interested in getting to the core of what we do. Karo: By now ACTORS have a sound that can be recognised very quickly, which is a huge achievement but potentially a dangerous one. Jason, you also produce the band yourself at Jacknife Sound, so you have an unusual degree of control over that identity. Have you ever made something technically good and unmistakably ACTORS and then deliberately damaged, changed or abandoned it because it felt too much like something you already knew how to do? Jason: All I think about is whether I like what I’m hearing. Is it eliciting an emotional reaction when I play it back? I will start work on a song, then leave it alone for a month, so when I come back to it, it tricks my mind into feeling like I’m collaborating with someone else. Then I get another level of creativity from the process. Karo: “Left On Read” takes something almost absurdly ordinary in contemporary communication and makes it psychologically cruel: silence is no longer simply absence, because you can see that your message has been received. I find that tiny technological change quite brutal. Has technology actually changed the experience of rejection and abandonment, or has it simply engineered a much more precise interface for anxieties people have always had? Jason: It’s the same feelings in a world that’s instant. The fact that we have access to each other 24/7 only expedites the emotional transaction. Karo: “CTRL” is intensely physical, with that very precise four-on-the-floor propulsion, while emotionally the song revolves around the absence of control. I like that contradiction because the body is being given something extremely disciplined to follow while everything underneath it is becoming less stable. How consciously do you use rhythm that way? Can musical control create a safe space in which emotional control can collapse? Jason: I couldn’t tell you. I’ve never analysed the elements of a song in that way. When I’m writing a song, the beat and vibe come first. Then I react to that and start writing the lyrics. It’s a natural process. Karo: One thing I keep noticing with ACTORS is how attractive the music can be while dealing with material that is not particularly comfortable. Melody, rhythm and production seduce first; sometimes the darker psychological content registers afterwards. But on this album there also seems to be a stronger movement back towards connection and life rather than simply dwelling inside damage. Has it become more difficult to write hope convincingly than darkness without making it sentimental? Jason: I hate to sound cliché, but the songs really do kind of arrive on their own schedule and with their own vibe. Once the spark hits, I do my best to craft it. You can say whatever you like. If that’s your honest expression, it should land. Karo: Shannon, you created the visual design for “Our Love Will Live Forever”. Here you were dealing with a title that already had an intensely personal history before you began giving the album a visual identity. What did you want the artwork to understand about the record without literally illustrating mortality, memory or love? And because the artwork comes from inside ACTORS, can you allow the visual language to disagree with the music rather than simply explain it? Shannon: The star design on the cover comes from an engraving on a medieval breastplate. To me, it was an ideal symbol to pair with the themes of the record. As the light from the star reaches into the dark, love becomes a form of armour and protection too. Karo: ACTORS have also allowed recent songs to be substantially reconstructed through remixes, from Dave Clarke‘s “In Real Life” to “Dead Inside (Crackmix)”. I always find the interesting remixes are the ones that stop behaving respectfully towards the original. When somebody else takes your song apart, how much do you actually want them to preserve? Is a misunderstanding sometimes more revealing than a faithful interpretation? Jason: I just love to hear what other artists do with a song. It’s fun to hear what their interpretations are. I’m not precious about it. Once the stems are out the door, they’re free to go wild. Karo: ACTORS originate with your songwriting and production, Jason, but live the project is unmistakably four people. Shannon, Kendall and Adam are not simply reproducing a finished studio object. After all these years of playing together, where does authorship begin to become collective? Can the live band teach you that something you considered fundamental to a recording actually wasn’t fundamental at all? Jason: Each member brings context and mood to the music. We exist on recordings and live onstage. Both are a different experience and important. The band members are an integral part of what the band and songs are. Karo: We’ll meet at NCN in Deutzen on September 5, almost at the beginning of the “Our Love Will Live Forever” tour. From there you have an extensive run through Germany, Rotterdam, Switzerland, Spain and Paris, followed by the UK shows with She Past Away and then Canadian dates in October. What happens after this announced run? Are you already discussing more European shows or festivals for 2027, and are there places where you particularly want to take this album that are not on the current schedule? Jason: After this fall tour, we have a bunch of US dates we will be announcing. That’s all I’m allowed to say. About ACTORS ACTORS are a Vancouver-based quartet consisting of Jason Corbett on vocals and guitar, Shannon Hemmett on synthesizers and vocals, Kendall Wooding on bass and vocals, and Adam Fink on drums. Corbett also produces the band’s music at his Vancouver studio, Jacknife Sound. The current line-up is confirmed by both the band and Artoffact Records. The band’s first full-length album, “It Will Come to You”, was released through Artoffact Records in 2018. Its combination of guitar, synthesizers, bass-driven momentum and tightly controlled production established the sound with which ACTORS became internationally associated. The follow-up, “Acts of Worship”, arrived on 1 October 2021, again produced by Corbett at Jacknife Sound. That album also marked Kendall Wooding’s first ACTORS album on bass. “Reanimated” followed in 2022, collecting earlier B-sides and related material, while the next period increasingly unfolded through individual releases. “In Real Life”, “Dead Inside” and “Object of Desire” appeared in 2024, followed by the “Crazy Lovers” remix collection in 2025. In 2026 ACTORS opened the new album cycle with “CTRL” in February, “Left On Read” in April and “Youth” in July. Their official Bandcamp currently lists those releases alongside the band’s earlier catalogue. Hemmett also records as Leathers, whose debut album “Ultraviolet” appeared in 2024. “Our Love Will Live Forever” is scheduled for 4 September 2026 through Artoffact Records. According to the album announcement supplied by the band, it is ACTORS’ third full-length studio album and was produced by Jason Corbett at Jacknife Sound. Shannon Hemmett created the album’s visual design. The album arrives simultaneously with a major touring period. The European run begins in Berlin on 4 September, followed the next day by NCN Festival in Deutzen. ACTORS then continue through Germany, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Spain and France before three UK dates with She Past Away in Manchester, Bristol and London. Canadian shows follow in October in Vancouver, Edmonton and Calgary. And, as Corbett reveals here, that will not be the end of the 2026 live cycle: a further run of US dates is already planned, although the band is not yet ready to announce the details.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑的核心张力围绕'无常'展开：Jason Corbett从祖父母墓志铭中提取标题，却在心脏急症后重新审视了'永远'的意味。录音过程被迫中断，使整张唱片从关于永恒的承诺，转向探讨当永久性本身不可信时，什么仍能保有意义。Corbett拒绝过度理性化创作，强调本能驱动——节拍先行，技术选择以情绪反应为唯一标准。Shannon Hemmett为视觉部分引入中世纪盔甲雕刻中的星形图案，与歌词主题形成跨时代呼应。专辑涉及即时通讯与古老焦虑的并置、四人乐队中的创作权分配，以及欧洲巡演之后的去向。Artoffact厂牌发行，定位介于暗潮与后朋克之间的冷调美学，情感处理冷静而不煽情，但音乐本身的实验性和声音设计细节在现有文本中尚未充分展开。

items.excerpt: You’ll be food for a hawk if you live like a lamb the hours decay like a corpse in the sand eternity calls and we’re singing for the damned There are records that announce their mortality with violins and candlelight, and then there are records that sound as if somebody has kicked open the crypt door. 1919’s Last Dance of the Departed, their first studio release since 2021 and first 7” since 1983, belongs to the latter breed: hard bass, serrated guitar, drums with the discipline of f
items.body: You’ll be food for a hawk if you live like a lamb the hours decay like a corpse in the sand eternity calls and we’re singing for the damned There are records that announce their mortality with violins and candlelight, and then there are records that sound as if somebody has kicked open the crypt door. 1919’s Last Dance of the Departed, their first studio release since 2021 and first 7” since 1983, belongs to the latter breed: hard bass, serrated guitar, drums with the discipline of factory machinery, and Rio Goldhammer singing as though the end of civilization has inconvenienced him personally. 1919’s Bradford roots place them among the original wave of groups that pushed post-punk into darker territory during the early 1980s. Bands like Bauhaus and the Virgin Prunes were contemporaries in establishing what would later be called “goth”, working in parallel from different cities with a related vocabulary of skeletal guitars, theatrical dread, physical rhythm, and damaged religious imagery. On Last Dance of the Departed, 1919 carries that vocabulary forward with the blunt force of musicians who have spent years dragging these songs through clubs rather than preserving them behind glass. Ding Archer’s bass gives the track a heavy, stalking center, the guitar cuts across it in cold diagonal strokes, and the drums maintain a martial insistence that makes mortality feel strangely danceable. Last Dance of the Departed stares directly at extinction: brother killing brother, wages exchanged for useless possessions, gods who may have stopped answering the telephone, and the ridiculous persistence of hope. Goldhammer delivers these ideas with enough bite to prevent the song from collapsing into gothic sermonizing. There is black humour buried in the fatalism, the sort that develops when you have been around long enough to know death is coming so you may as well crank up the amp to give him a proper fanfare. The production leaves plenty of exposed bone. Guitar, bass, and percussion occupy their own hostile corners, colliding without becoming muddy, while Goldhammer rides above the racket with a voice closer to a public warning than a conventional rock performance. The video, directed by Goldhammer, pushes that idea into the flesh. Live footage flashes through a band still throwing itself at the stage after decades marked by departures and death. Members have been lost along the way, and the song carries that knowledge without converting grief into museum-piece reverence. These musicians still look dangerous because they remain committed to movement, volume, friction, and the communal absurdity of standing in a room together while the clock keeps chewing through time and space. Watch the video for Last Dance of the Departed below: For a band whose early history includes Cry Wolf, Machine, and two Peel sessions, 1919 sounds remarkably uninterested in reenacting 1983. Their post-punk remains angular and severe, but age has thickened the music’s sense of consequence. Last Dance of the Departed knows the party ends, knows the gods may be absent, knows the body goes back to ash, and still finds enough electricity in that knowledge to keep the dead dancing. 1919’s Last Dance of the Departed and its B-side Satellite Man are available on black and limited-edition green 7″ Vinyl. Order here. items._cn_summary: 1919 乐队自1983年后首张7寸单曲，由Rio Goldhammer担纲主唱。贝斯线条沉重如猎食者潜行，吉他以冷峻的对角线切入，鼓点维持军事化的推进感，使死亡主题获得诡异的舞动感。歌词直面灭绝意象：兄弟相残、薪金换无用之物、神明或许已停止接听电话，却仍顽固地怀抱希望——这种黑色幽默避免了哥特式的说教。制作保留大量裸露骨架，三件乐器各自占据敌对角落而不混浊，人声则近似公共警报。MV由主唱本人执导，穿插乐队数十年间的现场片段，成员逝去的历史被携带却不沦为博物馆式的哀悼。整体延续Bradford后朋克传统，但拒绝简单复刻1983年的自己。

items.body:
Latest Edition of the WPH Summer Special released on We Play House Recordings.

"In the early ‘10’s the WPH Summer Special was a yearly tradition: a stamped vinyl only releases featuring lost tracks, one-off collabs, dreaded digital only gems, etc. Some summer specials were so hot we released them in the winter to battle the cold…

Guess what? It’s back! Four killer tracks on one slice of vinyl. Satoshi Fumi remixing Ian O’Donovan to devastating Detroit-styled effect, Red D taking things deep with some dreamy deep house magic, Fabrice Lig going from ‘Border 2 Border’ on vinyl with Red D & Lady Linn and then Uit De Hoogte teaming up with Lefto for an oldskool house jam that will only be available on this release."

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑是夏日特辑系列时隔多年后的回归，延续了早年以黑胶形式收录遗珠曲目的传统，以单张黑胶容纳四首作品。内容包括将原曲重塑为底特律风格混音的作品，偏向梦幻深邃的浩室制作，以及一首仅在本黑胶发行的老派浩室合作；该系列也曾因部分特辑反响热烈而改在冬季发行。曲目来源包括一次性合作与数字独占遗珠，整体属于扎根俱乐部场景的电子舞曲发行。

items.body: You might not have heard of London's Perpetual Paradox, but you should definitely give them a listen. Although ostensibly a groove-laden death-thrash/core outfit, there's a lot more going on here than that already enticing description might suggest. The 5 tracks on their new EP May Misery Befall You deliver a killer combination of wiry, off-kilter lead-work that reminds me of Psycroptic (except without the Nazi merch) along with and added progressiveness à la Rivers of Nihil, the crunch of Lamb of God and brutality of Fit for an Autopsy. It's a potent concoction to be sure and one of the more exciting "new" artists I've come across this year. Check out their ferocious "Source of Hate" below, and keep reading to see what other ingredients go into making such a devastatingly delicious sound.Jorge (Guitar)Lamb of God was definitely the band that made me realise I absolutely love groove. I used to stay awake on Sunday nights to watch MTV's Headbanger’s Ball and when I first heard "Set To Fail" there, it absolutely made me go crazy!The riff, the aggressiveness, the drums, the vocals…I was like “I wanna write shit like this”!From thrash to metalcore and later on deathcore, groove was always what got me hyped with metal. Mark Morton and Will Adler are absolute riff beats and were a major influence in my playing style!Adrian (Vocals)For me it goes back to when I was just a teenager, listening to what everyone else was listening to, trying to figure out life. Then one friend showed me "A Little Piece of Heaven" by Avenged Sevenfold, and the spark was lit.That song was on repeat day and night. The theme, orchestras, trumpets and vocals were unlike anything I had heard before. It made me realise heavy music could be so much more than just guitars, bass and drums, and that atmosphere and arrangement could be just as important as the riffs. That’s probably why on most Perpetual Paradox tunes, whenever there’s orchestras or samples, I’m usually behind them, or at least have been involved."My Curse" by Killswitch Engage made me want to pursue vocals. I became obsessed with the contrast between warm, melodic vocals and brutal screams. Howard Jones’ vocals were out of this world and I remember thinking, “fuck, I wish I could sound like that.” I already liked singing when I was alone—doing chores, in the shower—so I started taking it seriously and kept gaining the confidence to develop my chops.Then came the 2020s deathcore era. Bands like Lorna Shore, or songs like "Death Empress" by Disembodied Tyrant/Synestia, changed how I looked at heavy music. I loved the filthy breakdowns, while Sleep Token became a huge anchor for the clean, atmospheric side of my vocals. Combining that beautiful, warm voice with something fucking disgusting is probably one of the biggest things that shaped how I write for Perpetual Paradox today.Ollie (Guitar)For a long time I didn’t really listen to music because I couldn’t find anything I liked. But then a friend showed me Metallica’s Ride the Lightning (1985) and everything changed. I dove headfirst into the macabre world of metal, not long after which I discovered its more extreme genres and the bands behind them, like Death and The Black Dahlia Murder. Although a thrasher at heart, I branched out early, in doing so discovering the genres and bands that would define what I listen to and write now: Bleed from Within, Lorna Shore, August Burns Red, Fit for an Autopsy, and Decapitated, to name a few. I try not to let myself stick to one genre as it’s a detriment and a waste to do so, so anything I think sounds good, I’ll listen to and find a way to emulate in my own music. More recently I’ve been getting into bands like Nails, Converge and End, which has had a notable impact on how I write and approach the equipment I use to do so. I think I’m far from done discovering and learning about metal and I’m loving how it’s shaping the music I write for Perpetual Paradox.Harry (Drums)As much as I’d love to write about my musical upbringing, I don’t think many people would take much interest in the finer details, so here's the top line. My favourite bands, and the bands that really got me to where I am today, include Slipknot, PeelingFlesh, Deathgrips, Chelsea Grin, Thy Art is Murder, Korn, Primus and Infant Annihilator. To anyone who hasn't checked out the drummers in these bands, please do, and you’ll know exactly why I play the way I do. Simply put, the bands and music I was brought up on have taught me everything I know: Hit hard, be aggressive and treat your snare like it owes you money …mine still hasn’t paid me yet.

items._cn_summary: 伦敦乐队 Perpetual Paradox 的这张 EP 共五首，在死亡金属、敲击金属与硬核/金属核框架内加入明显的律动感和前卫倾向。吉他线条扭曲、偏离常规，接近 Psycroptic 的技术化手法，同时具备 Rivers of Nihil 式的氛围铺陈、Lamb of God 式重击段落和 Fit for an Autopsy 式残酷感。乐队还强调管弦乐/采样与清嗓/兽吼的对比，受 Killswitch Engage 与 Sleep Token 影响，在段落编排上注重氛围与张力。整体并非单纯复古或模式化 breakdown 堆砌，而是通过不同金属子风格的融合形成辨识度。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — S�guin's second album's artwork (still released on the major Warner Bros label) may take a wink to LNF's Hymne Aux Quenouilles, but I don't see much a musical link. Anyway, the band returns with the same line-up, but also get reinforcements by a slew of guests, but it's not like they bring a new dimension.The A-side consist of 6 relatively-short tracks that are in the standard folk-rock mode (too gentle for my tastes), though some of the arrangements can be quite pleasant, especially the closing Nous Voyagerons, which luckily happens to be the longer track, by a margin. The flipside starts in the same gentle folk-rock, however a violin enters Chante, Danse and bring a much-more exciting and exotic (almost dronal/medieval) ambiance/arrangements. The same magic ambiance is transposed (albeit differently) into the Mois de Mai. But We're now facing an 8-mins closer, named F�te du Feu, opening on deep horns & crickets, but it develops to an Amerindian chant (something we'd suspected with their first album's G�nocide track) over bagpipes and steady martial drums then 100% native chants, the whole thing being quite dramatic (though not as strong as G�nocide) the two merging together, before the final crickets return. If En Attendant can be considered as a bit of a disappointment to progheads, but for folkheads, it's got everything to please them. Thankfully, the best three tracks are the album's longest and it ends much better than it started.
items._genre: folk rock / progressive folk / medieval folk
items._cn_summary: 这张1974年的专辑是Séguin乐队的第二张作品，由华纳兄弟发行。整体以民谣摇滚为基调，A面六首短曲风格偏轻柔，编曲尚可但缺乏力度；B面则更具探索性，小提琴的加入带来中世纪般的异域氛围，长篇作品《火之节》融合了美洲原住民吟唱、风笛和军鼓等元素，戏剧张力较强。专辑将法式民谣、原住民音乐传统与早期前卫摇滚手法结合，展现出一定的跨文化融合意识，但整体仍偏温和，前卫性有限。乐队阵容稳定并有客座乐手助阵，作品在民谣框架内尝试拓展音色与叙事结构，最佳段落集中在较长的三首作品中，结尾明显优于开头。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — After the schizophrenic two factions disbanded La Nouvelle Fronti�re, the S�guin twins went in the prog-folk direction, while the rest of the band went into the much rockier Le Match. Richard & Marie-Claire became the master of their destiny for four albums before parting ways , each having their own solo careers, Richard first teaming with Harmonium's Fiori for an album that could be considered as l'Heptade Bis. But that's another story, and we're now dealing with the duo's stunning eponymous debut album. And if the album's sleeve is something to go by, they chose the troubadour image, both on the front and back cover. Marie-Claire will design the project's album sleeves. I'm not sure at which point the twins became high-profile in La Belle Province, but they didn't sell out if you judge by their original hippie idealism. Btw, they had a more of less stable backing band of Gr�goire (bass) and Lagac� (drums), but Gilles Valiquette was a frequent contributor.Opening on the stunning medieval-like blood-curdling Som S�guin, they announce a new level from their LNF's contributions, while still claiming their original hippie folky roots (Caf� du Quai and En Toute Simplicit�). The A-side closes on the stunning Genocide, an 8-mins+ monster track that will drive shivers down your spine and its solemnity will drive the rest to your brains. What an awesome track, even 50 years down the line.The flipside returns to simpler form of folk-rock, even going to blues-rock Train du Nord. and the very Qu�b�cois Dans Ma Maison and the overlong Dis-Moi with a bit brutal change halfway though, going gradually rock. If they ever tried selling off a bit it's in the bilingual It's All Right My Friend, close to country rock, but nothing offensive (no "twang"). The album ends on the lovely and dreamy Tout Est Meilleur, but unfortunately, the second side lacks a stunner like the other face. On the merit of two stunning track on the A-side, the album is closer to 4* than 3.5*, hence the rounding up.
items._genre: progressive folk / folk rock / chamber folk
items._cn_summary: 这是Séguin双胞胎在La Nouvelle Frontière解散后的首张同名专辑，以行吟诗人形象示人，延续了乐队的嬉皮民谣根基。A面以中世纪风格的开场曲奠定沉稳基调，紧接的《Genocide》长达八分钟，庄严沉重，驱动情绪直击听者神经。B面回归更轻简的民谣摇滚形态，融入蓝调摇滚与魁北克本土色彩，偶有双语乡村摇滚的尝试。整体编曲偏向原声乐器与简约编制，虽未呈现极端实验性，但将法国民谣传统与前卫摇滚结构相融合，展现出独立创作时期的双胞胎艺术主张。作为1973年魁北克独立发行的民谣作品，带有明显的地域文化特征，但风格上更接近传统民谣摇滚，与实验或前卫领域有距离。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — A much more focused album than their very naive debut, though you'll still find the hippie idealism found on LNF. And this is because Quenouilles (survival plants water reeds) was recorded soon after their first effort, so you'll find traces of everything. Graced with a lovely gatefold artwork, l'Hymne is a much better affair, despite opening on a Ballade des Bourgeois not exactly announcing things to come. A slow organ looms and cowbells of Transition is taking things to the upper level , though not that satisfyingly so, because the instruments jam clumsily. Citoyens Du Monde shows the usual hippie idealism and Si Loin has Marie Claire singing solo over a an electric piano. On the flipside, Confiture Bleue (Blue Jam/jelly) is a bit too derivative of another song that it lacks a bit of credibility, though its bluesy dimension is quite enjoyable around the end of the track. The almost 7-mins Indifference starts slowly but develops in a very interesting (adventurous) middle section . But the real highlight of the album is the 7.5-mins title track that should blow some minds out with its slow organ crescendo and driving drums .Much like their debut , Quenouilles is still flawed, but the peaks are really enjoyable. Again a bit schizophrenic , torn between folk (mainly the A)side) and psych rock(the flipside), Quenouilles is out to stretch your mind, but doesn't necessarily succeed because of their overt naivet�. I will round out the album to the upper forth star, because of the intent, even if not entirely successful.
items._genre: progressive folk / psych rock / French
items._cn_summary: 这是法国乐队La Nouvelle Frontière的第二张专辑，相比首张天真之作更为聚焦，但仍有嬉皮理想主义色彩。专辑分为两面：A面以民谣为主，包括《Ballade des Bourgeois》等慢板风琴作品和Marie Claire的电钢琴独唱；B面转向迷幻摇滚，蓝调风格的《Confiture Bleue》略显借鉴痕迹，近七分钟的《Indifference》以缓慢开场发展出有趣的冒险段落，而七分半的同名标题曲以风琴渐强与强劲鼓点构成真正的高光时刻。整体展现出民谣与迷幻摇滚之间的分裂感，虽因过于天真而未能完全实现意图，但峰值段落仍有可圈可点之处。

items.body: Pittsburgh post-punk and shoegaze duo Lowsunday have released a music video for “Someone To Talk To“, the third track on their EP “low sunday ghost machine black ep”. The video went up on August 25, 2026 and was directed by Jer Herring, who has worked on the band’s earlier clips. The EP itself came out on Projekt Records on May 15, 2026. Bobby Spell connects the visuals to a subject the duo return to across the release: “This video conveys the delicate coldness, detachment and loneliness of this song. A theme frequently visited by us involves a feeling of isolation which seems to be increasingly common in modern life. The visuals in the video demonstrate this feeling in a variety of scenarios where separation, miscommunication or distance is implied throughout. Our creative partner Jer Herring has once again created a perfect visual counterpart for a Lowsunday song and we’re very proud of it.” The ‘Black EP’ and its five tracks “low sunday ghost machine black ep” holds five songs: “You’re So Wired”, “Shattered”, “Someone To Talk To”, “This Is Not Heaven” and “Don’t Want To Dream Again”. Projekt Records issued it on May 15, 2026 as a digital release and as a one-sided 12-inch vinyl EP limited to 200 copies. It is the second half of a two-part series that began with “low sunday ghost machine white ep” in November 2025. Videos have now been released for three of the five tracks. Side-Line covered the You’re So Wired clip in July. low sunday ghost machine black ep by lowsunday About Lowsunday Lowsunday formed in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania in 1994 under the name Low Sunday Ghost Machine. The group self-released a debut album under that name in 1996, with Shane Sahene on vocals and guitar, Scott Bedillion on guitar, Marc Turina on bass and Dale Reckless on synthesizer, produced by Lou Contumelio. A second record, “Elesgiem”, circulated as a self-released promo CD in 1999 before Projekt Records issued it commercially on April 3, 2001. Sahene produced it and played guitar and sang, Bobby Spell played bass and engineered, and A. T. Vish, Shaun Leslie and Shawn Bann filled out the sessions; Peter Beckerman mixed. Projekt released a remaster of “Elesgiem” in 2024 and a sixteen-track remaster of the 1996 debut in 2025, the latter including a 1999 re-recording of “For A Moment”. The band returned to new material with “low sunday ghost machine white ep” on November 28, 2025, its first all-new songs since 1999. Side-Line covered the “Soft Capture” and “Nevver” videos from that EP. Lowsunday is now a duo of Shane Sahene, who handles vocals, guitar, synth, bass and drums, and Bobby Spell on bass, guitar and drums. “Someone To Talk To” is the third video pulled from the “Black EP”, which closes out the two-part series the band began in late 2025.

items.body: Dublin post-punk band Fontaines D.C. release their fifth studio album, “Dopamine Chamber”, on 16 October 2026 through XL Recordings. The band confirmed the album on 18 August 2026 and issued the lead single “Marianne” the same day, with an official video directed by Dave Meyers and Cam Erickson. The album runs to eleven tracks. Only two titles are public so far: “Marianne”, which sits second, and the opener “Six Shot Morning”, which the band played live in Cádiz before the announcement. The full tracklist has not been published, and the band’s own release page still lists it as coming. James Ford produced ‘Dopamine Chamber’ in London and Palermo James Ford produced the record, as he did on “Romance” in 2024. Sessions moved between London, the English countryside and Palermo, where Grian Chatten recorded vocals in a makeshift booth built from mattresses and cushions. The label describes the result as a move away from guitars toward cold synthesiser tones, marching drums, samples and triggers, with several songs carrying no guitar at all. Chatten describes the album as a device rather than a set of songs: “The album itself is a dopamine chamber. You step inside and we test these different mind- or mood-altering pieces of music on you.” He measures the shift against the previous record in the same terms the band used for it. “I think “Romance” was maybe 60 per cent human and 40 per cent corrupted by automation, and a loss of feeling… This one feels more like 60 per cent corrupted – the mask is wearing the face a little more.” On the decision to strip out the consolation the earlier album ended on, he said: “I felt it would be more powerful to leave the hope out and reflect the ugliness honestly. This one needed to feel more like a catastrophic warning.” Bassist Conor Deegan III places the record in a run of albums built around location. “Our albums have always questioned a sense of place. First Dublin, then being away from Dublin, and then trying to find the romance elsewhere. On this record, the question became: where do you escape to?” Guitarist Conor Curley describes his own brief in one line: “I was trying to find stuff that pointed into the future.” “Dopamine Chamber” comes in six physical editions. The deluxe version is a double LP cut at 45rpm on black vinyl in a gatefold jacket with printed innersleeves, a printed insert and a poster. There are single LPs on blue and on black vinyl, both gatefold with a printed innersleeve and insert, a blue marble pressing sold as an indie-store exclusive, a CD in a gatefold digipak, and a cassette with alternate artwork and a foldout J-card. Pre-orders run through the band’s own store, the XL Recordings shop, Bandcamp and independent retailers. Dopamine Chamber by Fontaines D.C. Fontaines D.C. live dates in 2026 The dates listed alongside the announcement are the band’s existing summer and autumn festival commitments rather than an album tour. A separate headline run tied to “Dopamine Chamber” has not been announced. 18 August 2026 – Lausanne, Les Docks, Switzerland 20 August 2026 – Sankt Polten, FM4 Frequency, Austria 28 August 2026 – Reading, Reading Festival, UK 29 August 2026 – Leeds, Leeds Festival, UK 30 August 2026 – Stradbally, Electric Picnic, Ireland 18 September 2026 – Atlanta, GA, Shaky Knees, USA 20 September 2026 – Asbury Park, NJ, Sea.Hear.Now, USA 27 September 2026 – Dana Point, CA, Ohana Festival, USA About Fontaines D.C. Fontaines D.C. formed in Dublin in 2014, after the five members met at BIMM Dublin. The line-up has been unchanged since: Grian Chatten on vocals, Carlos O’Connell and Conor Curley on guitars, Conor Deegan III on bass and Tom Coll on drums. The band signed to Partisan Records in 2018. The debut album “Dogrel” came out on 12 April 2019, produced by Dan Carey, and was nominated for the Mercury Prize and the Choice Music Prize. Carey also produced “A Hero’s Death”, released on 31 July 2020, which entered the UK chart at No. 2 and brought a Grammy nomination for Best Rock Album and a Brit nomination for International Group. The third album, “Skinty Fia”, followed on 22 April 2022, again with Carey, and gave the band their first No. 1 in both Ireland and the UK; they won the Brit Award for International Group in 2023. “Romance”, released on 23 August 2024, was their first record for XL Recordings and their first with producer James Ford. It entered the UK chart at No. 2, gave the band their first Billboard 200 entry and their first UK singles chart placing with “Starburster”, and won International Group of the Year at the 2025 Brit Awards. A deluxe edition followed in 2025. More recently the band contributed to the Peaky Blinders: Immortal Man soundtrack and to War Child’s charity compilation “HELP(2)”, which was released on 6 March 2026 and carries tracks by both the band and Chatten solo. In August 2026 they played the final live session recorded at the BBC’s Maida Vale studios for 6 Music, their first performance since the death of their manager Trevor Dietz. “Dopamine Chamber” is their second album for XL Recordings and their first release since “Romance”.

items._cn_summary: Fontaines D.C. 第五张录音室专辑《Dopamine Chamber》由 James Ford 制作，录制横跨伦敦、英格兰乡村与巴勒莫。乐队在创作中大幅削弱吉他比重，转向冷调合成器音色、行军鼓节奏、采样与触发器，并有数首作品完全无吉他。主唱 Grian Chatten 将专辑比作一个多巴胺实验装置，每首歌对应一种特定情绪状态，延续了上一张《Romance》中关于人性化与自动化侵蚀比例的探讨。贝斯手 Conor Deegan III 将专辑置于乐队以地点为线索的创作脉络中，本作关注的是逃避的去向问题。整体方向朝向更冷峻、合成器驱动的实验性后朋克转型，去除了前作结尾的希望感，以呈现更具警示性的美学。

items.body: Belgian dark electronic project LLUMEN releases the digital single “The Leftovers” on 4 September 2026 and follows it with the fourth album “Winter Eden” on 30 October 2026, issued on CD and digital by Alfa Matrix. The record runs to twelve tracks and mixes EBM, techno, gothic electronica and future pop, the palette Pieter Coussement has worked with since founding the project in 2001. “The Leftovers” sits third on the album, between “Away From Here” and “Blood And Bone”. The full running order is “Adrift”, “Away From Here”, “The Leftovers”, “Blood And Bone”, “Eden After Winter”, “All Clouds Will Be Horses”, “The Gold Lined Scars”, “Between The Words”, “The Endless Faded Grey”, “I Take What’s Mine”, “Behind The Door” and “Holy Tears”. Coussement describes “Winter Eden” as a record built on contrast, with winter and Eden treated as opposing but linked states, and a sequence that moves from disorientation and detachment toward intimacy and reflection. He describes the album as a record of that distance: “Winter Eden has become a witness to that journey, spanning the distance between who we were and where we stand now.” LLUMEN brings ‘Winter Eden’ to a double release party with Implant One of the twelve tracks has already reached listeners. “Between The Words” appeared in July 2026 on The Odin Files, the darkwave compilation Side-Line issued alongside “The Freya Files” in support of Ukraine. LLUMEN presents the album live on 20 November 2026 at mOtown in Sint-Joost-ten-Node, Belgium, in a double release party with Implant, who launch their own album “The Kinematics of Doubt” at the same event. The two acts previously shared a double release party in Antwerp in October 2021. About LLUMEN LLUMEN is the dark electronic project of Pieter Coussement, based in Ghent, Belgium, and active since 2001. The name draws on Front 242’s “U-Men”, a track Coussement later covered for the Alfa Matrix compilation “Recovery >For You< – An Alfa Matrix Tribute To Front 242” in 2016. The project’s first album, “The Memory Institute”, was issued through Alfa Matrix, with an expanded bonus-tracks edition dated 13 January 2017. “Polygon Heart” followed on 18 June 2021 and the nine-track EP “Die Stille Totgeschwiegen” on 30 November 2023; Side-Line covered the latter in Belgian electro act Llumen is back with 9-track EP ‘Die Stille Totgeschwiegen’ – Out now. Third album “The Breaking Waves” arrived on 17 May 2024 as a limited 2CD set, reported here in Llumen is back with an all new album as a limited 2CD set, and Coussement discussed the record at length in the Llumen interview: ‘The Breaking Waves’ album acts as a reflection of inner turmoil. Alongside its own catalogue, LLUMEN has produced official remixes for Noemi Aurora, C-Lekktor, Pre-Emptive Strike 0.1, Implant, Alien Vampires and Mildreda, and contributed a version of Depeche Mode’s “Halo” to “Alfa Matrix Re:covered Vol.3” in 2019 and a reading of Front 242‘s “Gripped By Fear” to “Recovery 2 For You” in 2026. On stage the project has played Infest, Mechanismus, Castle Party, BIMfest and electriXmas, with its most recent appearance at Infest in Manchester in August 2025. “Winter Eden” is the first LLUMEN full-length since “The Breaking Waves” and the project’s fourth studio album in a run that started twenty-five years ago.

items._cn_summary: 比利时暗潮电子项目LLUMEN由Pieter Coussement自2001年运营，第四张专辑《Winter Eden》以冬季与伊甸园的对立意象为核心概念，十二首曲目从迷失疏离逐步过渡至亲密反思，主题围绕过去与当下之间的距离展开。制作上融合EBM、Techno、哥特电子与未来流行等多种暗潮系元素，属于该类型框架内的常规探索。单曲《The Leftovers》提前释出，另有一曲收录于支援乌克兰的暗潮合辑中。由Alfa Matrix独立厂牌发行CD与数字版本，并将在比利时与Implant共同举办双专场发行派对。文章内容偏向新闻信息发布而非深度乐评，缺少对声响设计、编曲手法与艺术创新的具体分析。

items.body: Our monthly We Have A Commentary bonus podcast works a bit differently this month; with Alex being off in the UK we’ve prerecorded a double dose of discussion of Synthetic Symphony’s 1998 comp “EBM Club Classics”, with the first disc dropping today and the second this coming Sunday. Disc one functioned as a handy DJ tool in the late 90s and early 00s, linking some of the first cuts from the likes of And One, Leaether Strip, and Bigod 20 with contemporary state of the art from Covenant, while also throwing in some left-field choices and proto-EBM cuts which have us speculating about the genre and the idea of an EBM canon at large. Tune back in this Sunday for the second half! As always, you can rate and subscribe on iTunes, download directly, or listen through the widget down below. items.body: BALTHVS take the title of “Pale Blue Dot” from Carl Sagan, who used the phrase for the Earth as Voyager 1 photographed it in 1990: a single point of light six billion kilometres from the lens. The Bogotá trio are declared Sagan fans, and they turn his warning into one blunt question: “Why destroy the one place that we call home, while there is nowhere else to go anyway?” The single announces MANIFEST, the band’s sixth album, out on Mixto Records on 7 October. Guitarist Balthazar Aguirre leads the trio with drummer Santiago Lizcano and bassist Johanna Mercuriana, who returns for this album after stepping away from touring to raise a child. The three regrouped in the Colombian countryside and wrote the record in the studio, where Transmutations, released in March, had reworked their live sets. “Pale Blue Dot” opens the album’s second side, a slow-burn that runs close to five minutes. BALTHVS cut MANIFEST on the rigs they use on stage, running analogue direct systems from Chile’s DSM Humboldt alongside their Fender instruments, with Bogotá producer Christian Cifuentes at the board. Across the record the trio push their psychedelic funk towards drum and bass, a harder rock attack and Ethio-jazz. items.body:
Faun Fables’ musical theatre work ‘The Transit Rider'.

"At once a work of theatre, allegory and autobiography, ‘The Transit Rider’ amplifies Faun Fables’ distinctive electroacoustic wash of Anglo-European folk sounds, shimmering allusively from traditional to Kurt Weill to folk-rock and back again.

The route that led to ‘The Transit Rider’ goes back even further than 2006; it was first embarked upon in the early 1990s, when Dawn McCarthy moved to NYC and was introduced to the transient and constant glories of its subway system, a massive world unto itself. As she rode the trains, the subterranean, singing landscape suggested a journey in song: a rider aboard a ubiquitous transit system, a network of rails, roads, corridors and trails extending in all directions, meeting itself again on the far side of the world. Upon this endless circuitous path, she encounters characters that may or may not help her search to find a clearing amid this mass of machinery and humanity in which to stop and have a picnic.

In 2001, ‘The Transit Rider’ took the form of a full-length theatre production in San Francisco, with a cast of thirteen aided by the inspiring work of director / lighting designer Allen Willner. Its music was further developed / recorded/adapted into a touring show by Dawn and her stalwart co-conspirator Nils Frykdahl (of Sleepytime Gorilla Museum), joined by multi-instrumentalists Jenya Chernoff and Matt Lebofsky.

The album features contributions by Dawn’s mother Michelina Tyrie (‘Earth’s Kiss’) and father Will McCarthy (‘I No Longer Wish To’, a poem written during his last days as a stockbroker), with thematically related songs by Zygmunt Konieczny (‘Taki Pejzaz / Such a Landscape’) Soeur Sourire (‘Je Voudrais / I’d like to Be’) and the Anglo Saxon traditional ‘House Carpenter’ added to the mix."
items._genre: electroacoustic folk / avant-garde theatre / folk-rock
items._cn_summary: 《The Transit Rider》是Faun Fables的音乐剧场作品，将盎格鲁-欧洲民间传统与库尔特·韦尔式的剧场音乐及民谣摇滚熔于一炉，形成独特的电声民谣质感。作品构思始于上世纪九十年代，Dawn McCarthy在纽约地铁系统中的日常体验成为核心灵感，乘客在无尽延伸的轨道网络中穿梭，遇见各色人物，在庞大的机械与人性之间寻找一处可以驻足野餐的宁静空地。专辑音乐经由与Sleepytime Gorilla Museum成员Nils Frykdahl等合作者反复打磨，融合了Dawn母亲的演唱、父亲临终前的诗作朗读，并嵌入波兰作曲家与比利时修女的原版录音。整体呈现出一种寓言式的、带有自传色彩的音乐叙事，将民间传统的质朴与都市文明的迷宫感交织在一起。

items.excerpt: アフロビーツ界の一角を担うナイジェリア発のスターが、自身のレーベルを立ち上げて放つ4作目。2パック“Do For Love”がイメージの源であろうメロウな“Oba”、アマピアノ界の重要DJであるカブザ・デ・スモールをフィーチャーした“Asambe”などなどの佳曲が並ぶが、ゲストの数は抑えて派手な仕掛けもなし。粗削りなストリート・ミュージックではなく上質なポップスを狙ったような印象で、それはゴスペル歌唱で始まるアルバムのイントロから、曲名通りに清らかなコーラスが入るDJスネイク作の“WORSHIP”へと繋がるオープニングからも感じられる。聴きやすくBGM的な耳当たりもある一作。

items._cn_summary: 这是尼日利亚Afrobeats明星Asake的第四张专辑，也是他成立个人厂牌后发行的作品。乐评指出，这张专辑不再强调粗糙的街头质感，而是更接近制作精良的流行音乐。曲目如《Oba》带有柔和抒情的黑人音乐气质，《Asambe》邀来Amapiano领域的重要DJ合作，整体上客串阵容克制，也没有刻意制造噱头。专辑开场从福音式演唱进入，再连接到DJ Snake制作、拥有清亮合唱的《WORSHIP》，显示出对主流听感的追求。作品保留了非洲节奏的地域底色，同时旋律流畅、易于接受，甚至适合作为背景音乐使用。对于偏好实验性和前卫取向的听众而言，这张专辑的流行化路线显得相对常规，但其非洲流行身份仍带来一定的文化辨识度。

items.body: Review by Abrasmatheus — Masterpiece from a band at the height of its creativityI have known A Night at the Opera since my teenage years, when it became one of my favorite albums. I first heard it through my father during family road trips, and those memories are certainly one of the reasons why this album remains so special to me. The fact that I did not approach it with any particular expectations and simply discovered it naturally makes my relationship with the record even more personal.For me, A Night at the Opera is one of Queen's best albums. It is remarkably consistent, with no weak tracks, and it perfectly represents many of the elements that made the band so distinctive during the 1970s. Hard rock, rock opera, pop, folk influences and theatrical arrangements are all present here, creating an extremely varied but cohesive album.I would not call A Night at the Opera a progressive rock album, but it undoubtedly contains several progressive elements. The clearest example is 'The Prophet's Song', probably the most progressive composition on the record. Its unusual structure, extended length, dramatic changes in atmosphere, complex vocal sections and ambitious arrangements give it a much more progressive character than the rest of the album. The famous vocal canon in the middle of the song, with multiple overlapping voices creating an almost hypnotic effect, is particularly impressive. The track also develops through different sections rather than following a simple verse-chorus format, making it one of the most adventurous compositions Queen ever recorded.The album's production and arrangements are also among its greatest strengths. Even without being an expert in production, it is impossible not to notice the enormous amount of detail in the record. The layered vocal harmonies, guitar overdubs, theatrical arrangements and constant stylistic changes create a rich and almost cinematic sound. This is an album that rewards repeated listening because there always seems to be some new detail to discover.Freddie Mercury delivers some absolutely beautiful vocal performances throughout the album. In my opinion, he had the greatest voice in rock music, and A Night at the Opera offers plenty of evidence for that opinion. Brian May's voice on ''39' is also a highlight, perfectly fitting the song's folk rock atmosphere, while Roger Taylor's more aggressive vocals make 'I'm in Love with My Car' a strong hard rock track.The album opens brilliantly with 'Death on Two Legs', an aggressive combination of hard rock and theatricality that immediately displays one of Queen's greatest identities during the 1970s. 'Lazing on a Sunday Afternoon' is one of the most unusual songs on the album and has a very distinctive character, while 'I'm in Love with My Car' brings a more direct hard rock approach and is also a perfect song for a road trip.'You're My Best Friend' is another extremely memorable track, while ''39' is one of my personal favorites because of its wonderful folk rock character and Brian May's vocals. 'Sweet Lady' brings another excellent dose of Queen's hard rock side, while 'Love of My Life' is probably one of the more pop-oriented songs on the album and became one of Queen's most iconic compositions.'Good Company' is another fascinating and unusual track, difficult to place stylistically but similar in spirit to 'Lazing on a Sunday Afternoon' in its old-fashioned and theatrical approach.And then there is 'Bohemian Rhapsody'.For me, this is not only the best song on the album but the greatest rock song of all time. It deserves every bit of its legendary reputation. The combination of ballad, opera and hard rock was an extraordinary innovation, and the composition remains as impressive today as it was when the album was released. It is a true rock anthem, but its fame should not overshadow the fact that the song is also an incredibly ambitious piece of musical creativity.The transition from 'The Prophet's Song' into 'Love of My Life' is another of my favorite moments on the album. Although the two songs are completely different, their placement creates a memorable contrast and contributes to the album's dramatic flow.No track is weak here. Every song has its own identity, and the diversity of styles never makes the album feel unfocused. If anything, that diversity is one of its greatest strengths.In my opinion, A Night at the Opera stands alongside Queen, Queen II, Sheer Heart Attack and A Day at the Races as one of the best albums Queen ever made. It may not be a progressive rock album in the strict sense, but its ambitious compositions and willingness to experiment with different musical styles explain why it can appeal strongly to progressive rock listeners.More importantly, this is an album I associate with family road trips and my adolescence, which makes it personally significant to me. However, even putting nostalgia aside, I still consider it an outstanding record that deserves its legendary status.Recommended to every fan of classic rock.
items._genre: hard rock / rock opera / progressive rock / folk rock / pop
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑展现了Queen在创作巅峰期的多样风格，融合硬摇滚、摇滚歌剧、民谣与流行元素。乐评人认为它并非严格意义上的前卫摇滚，但包含明显的前卫成分，尤其以《The Prophet's Song》为代表，其结构复杂、段落转换频繁，人声卡农营造出近乎催眠的效果。制作层面细节丰富，多轨人声和吉他叠加营造出电影般的声响，值得反复挖掘。Freddie Mercury的演唱被高度评价，Brian May在《'39》中的嗓音契合民谣氛围，而Roger Taylor在《I'm in Love with My Car》中则带来更粗粝的硬摇滚质感。开篇《Death on Two Legs》以戏剧化的硬摇滚奠定基调，《Lazing on a Sunday Afternoon》和《You're My Best Friend》等曲目各具特色。整体连贯，无弱曲，体现了乐队1970年代的核心特质。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Review by JilbataPlazm — As a long time progressive and neoprogressive rock fan i must say that i am very hard to please. When i was devouring band IQ i noticed that something is off after Martin Orford left. I didn't know how to describe it, but like the soul of IQ is gone. That's always the case when someone big and important vanishes from scene. I heard it once briefly when i was a little bit younger and liked few parts of album, but didn't listen to it again. That's always the case with masterpieces, especially progressive rock masterpieces. When you hear it for the first time, just few notes stick in your head, and nothing more. In that couple of years i manage to discover a lot of beautiful neoprogressive rock bands such as Marillion, Pallas, Arena, Jadis and so on. Why is that important? Because few weeks ago i heard of Jadis and really liked it. I searched to see what are the band members, and suprise suprise, Martin Orford is their lead keyboard player. To cut it short i put "The Old Road" and listened to it once again. Bam! What a shock. First song and already a masterpiece. When something gives me a goosebumps when i listen to it i automatically know it's a masterpiece. I knew Martin Orford was a genius, but without "The Old Road" i couldn't make that statement. "The Old Road" is farewell album, but hey... what a farewell. Going back to his roots, he decided to make a extraordinary beautiful progressive rock album. Why i praise it so much? Because some parts are like Mozart himself composed it. Particullary the ending of "The Time and The Season". That would be it. Thank you mister Orford for everything! If you still have inspiration, fans would be delighted to hear yet another great album from you.
items._genre: neo-progressive rock / progressive rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是前IQ乐队键盘手Martin Orford的个人告别之作，回归根源制作的前卫摇滚专辑。作者通过自己接触Jadis乐队后重新发现这张作品的经历，强调作品首曲即带来强烈触动，尤其提到结尾段落具有莫扎特般的古典气质，整体被视为一部迟到的杰作。专辑以键盘为主导，延续了neo-prog流派对器乐编排和情感铺陈的重视，融入了古典作曲的优雅感。评论更多是个人怀旧与重新发现的叙述，缺乏对具体编曲结构、声音设计或制作细节的深入分析，音乐本身偏向传统前卫摇滚框架内的精致创作，缺少与实验、爵士、电子等领域的跨界探索。
